mr president, the catastrophe of the oil tanker prestige in november 2002 and its serious consequences are still very much alive in northern portugal. but we know that marine pollution from oil spills or other harmful substances continues even without accidents. illegal dumping and cleaning up on the high seas or even near the coast must be punished. but we also know that the fight against these illegal discharges requires not only more legislation but above all more effective supervision, by equipping the member states with the appropriate means and facilities, by requiring compliance with existing standards, by abolishing flags of convenience, by serious and well-structured record keeping of the history of ships, their movements and loads, by establishing maritime corridors further from the coast, by adequate inspection of ships in ports and by improving working and safety conditions on board. it is well known that the marpol convention is ignored daily by a large number of ships sailing in community waters, because the central objective of certain shipowners and oil companies is to obtain the maximum profit at the minimum cost. on the other hand, tackling discharges requires not only effective action at member state level and greater cooperation between member states, but also more effective implementation at global level. the creation of a european coastguard will not solve this problem. it also does not solve the problem of the lack of adequate facilities in ports for ship-generated waste and the obligation on ships to use these facilities. it is necessary to require compliance with existing directives and other standards, including the information and monitoring system - which another directive has already established - and in particular with regard to the installation of devices for recording data during voyages on certain ships, without which it will be difficult to prove the guilt or innocence of the crew of ships which cannot be treated as criminals before their guilt has been proven. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. the responsibility of the member states and their governments is therefore required, and this responsibility must be fully assumed in the implementation of the various existing conventions and directives.
mr president, better late than never, as the people say. the current proposal for a council decision is based on the idea of tightening the civil and criminal liability of maritime transport, which generates pollution, and has allowed, in line with the commission's position on the directive and the traditional positions of the european parliament, that parliament to improve the initial text with two amendments which i consider very relevant. and they were unanimously approved. the first is to extend the scope of criminal liability to conduct which results in substantial harm to persons, going beyond the restrictive criterion of death or serious injury. the second, along the same lines, extends the liability of offenders beyond damage to species of fauna or flora to substantial damage to the protected environment, which is nature, the whole framework of marine and coastal life subject to the risk of pollution. i therefore congratulate the rapporteur, mr giuseppe di lello finuoli, who has had them approved. the new legal framework on marine pollution and the future lisbon maritime surveillance agency, which the brussels council set up last month, give us reason to believe that europe is finally taking its responsibilities. it would be illogical for europe to have the power to regulate the resources of the sea without first having the means to protect them.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, parliament is responding today to the commission communication on the framework for european regulatory agencies, in which, following the white paper on governance, the commission sets out in general terms the conditions for the creation of new agencies, the regulatory framework within which they should carry out their activities and the specific responsibilities of the commission in the supervision of the respective agencies. the first word, commissioner, is to congratulate you on the initiative and also on the general criteria contained therein. parliament notes with satisfaction that its positions, already expressed in the resolution on the white paper, have been taken into account by assigning the responsibility for the creation of agencies, or an explicit choice made on a case-by-case basis by the legislator, through an act based on the provision of the treaty which constitutes the legal basis of the respective community policy to be implemented. an important point to be made is the recognition of the judicious and parsimonious use of the creation of new agencies. they will only be justified in areas of high scientific or technical expertise, where there is a precise delimitation of the tasks to be carried out, within a framework of responsibility and autonomy which does not call into question the unity and integrity of the executive function or diminish the commission's political accountability to parliament and the council. but like everything in life, there's always a "but". the report we are presenting today, however, regrets that the commission has restricted the scope of its communication to the so-called regulatory agencies to be set up in the future within the institutional framework of the ec treaty. it regrets that no reference has been made to the existing agencies, whereas we all agree on the need to make a thorough assessment of the performance of the existing agencies, the urgency of proposing some reformulation of their tasks and competences, and the need to update the structure and composition of their bodies. these are concerns, as you know, mr commissioner, which parliament has been expressing to the commission through the parliamentary committees most directly involved in monitoring the functioning of the agencies and which we are stressing once again today. it also regrets that no reflection has been given to the consequences of the profound changes proposed in the draft european constitution, namely the end of the pillar structure, the introduction of a hierarchy of rules and the explicit introduction of judicial review of the agencies' acts. it will be important to know them in order to outline the future regulatory environment of the agencies in a more complete, coherent and bold way. as regards the narrow scope of communication, parliament's main concern will always be to ensure the unity and integrity of the executive function at european level and the corresponding political responsibility of the commission. but you will also understand that parliament will pay particular attention to the rules which will enable the tasks to be carried out in a transparent and effective manner, the filling of posts and the management of the expenses of the future agencies. we will therefore pay particular attention in the proposal for the future regulatory framework to the rules applying to the agencies all the requirements for good administration, for compliance with legislation on transparency, access to documents, rules on protection against fraud and protection of the financial interests of the community. i would like to conclude by thanking the committee on legal affairs, the committee on budgets and budgetary control for their competent and informed opinions and all the members who, with their participation, were also co-authors of this report. we look forward, commissioner, with confidence to the initiative on the legal framework for agencies which the commission will present in the future. in writing. - (pt) despite the obvious diversity of the plant varieties in question, which certainly justifies a specific community instrument, the fact is that plant varieties have not only been the subject of study and consumption for a long time, but that human creative activity has played a quite natural role in their development. in view of the multiplicity of industrial property rights in this area and the particular circumstances, i voted in favour, because i agree with the view of the council and the commission that the community plant variety right should be brought into line with the directive on the legal protection of biotechnological inventions. the legal certainty and protection of the rights of inventors and developers and the relationship between them justify, as does the current importance of this area, the need to ensure consistency between the legal instruments on exploitation rights and on corresponding varietal licences covering patent-protected inventions. in particular, such harmonisation will make it possible to ensure that the holder of a biotechnological patent can exploit a variety containing his invention where the holder of the plant variety right refuses to grant a contractual licence and that invention constitutes a significant technical advance of considerable economic interest.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing is simply a destructive fishing practice that undermines the sustainable conservation and management of fisheries resources. the tuna fishery is one of the fisheries most affected by illegal fishing activity, to which it should be added that the eu fishing fleets are among those that exploit these stocks the most. in this context, the eu has played a leading role in combating this type of iuu fishing, not least by combating the use of flags of convenience. however, these measures have clearly not been sufficient. in portugal, and particularly in the algarve, we are well aware of iuu fishing and i shall not repeat the accusations i have made in the past in the european parliament. i would like to support this report, which i believe will both help to conserve fisheries resources and bring some calm to community waters. i support the report because it calls for member states to seek to discourage their nationals from taking part in iuu activities. i thank mrs mckenna for this report, which, when implemented, will effectively solve problems that we are all familiar with, although some difficulties in combating them can be identified.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the relevant purpose here is to update a community regulation which brings together the control measures agreed between the various regional fisheries organisations (rfo), since the rfo have, since the adoption of the regulation, agreed on additional measures which need to be transposed into community law. in particular, iccat (the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas), the rfmo that has been at the forefront of efforts to curb illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, is now proposing a package of measures to counter these destructive fishing practices, with a focus on fishing by vessels flying flags of convenience. another aspect that needs to be corrected is the very poor quality of the data provided by the flag states, which, although it is one of the most basic obligations of these states, has made the assessment of the size of stocks uncertain. as the eu's fishing fleets are among the biggest users of these stocks, the eu must take responsibility and set a good example. i would like to express my appreciation, as does the rapporteur, for the efforts of iccat to deal with these problems within the remit of this commission, which is undoubtedly an attitude which is inspiring other rfos and other international developments in this field. i support this report and have voted for it.
in writing. - (pt) i support mr pirker's excellent report, which proposes a reorganization of the 1997 joint action so that the new synthetic substances can be tackled more resolutely and effectively. the problem of the growing production and trade of synthetic drugs requires strict and effective controls as soon as possible. this proposal is an update which at the same time means increased transparency and an extension of the scope of the joint action in terms of information exchange, risk assessment and control of the new synthetic substances which have been a very effective tool for rapid information exchange. the scope of application is extended to all new synthetic substances and new narcotic substances, including those which can be defined as medicinal products. it is also positive that, as the rapporteur proposes, the structures are simplified so that the exchange of information and the risk assessment can be carried out as simply and efficiently as possible. we hope that the joint action will not only serve as a rapid reaction mechanism but also serve the long-term monitoring of a synthetic drug in the future in the form of a continuous exchange of information between the member states and europol and the european monitoring centre for drugs (emcdda).
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this report, which is primarily technical in nature, seeks to update, broaden the scope and strengthen the exchange of information, risk assessment and control of new synthetic and narcotic substances on the basis of current procedures such as the early warning system and the system for assessing the social and health risks - carried out by a scientific committee - and the control procedure of the member states. it is intended that in future it will not only serve as a mechanism for rapid reaction but will serve the long-term monitoring of a synthetic substance by means of a procedure of constant information exchange. i support the rapporteur's wish to simplify the exchange of information, as does my group, and he proposes a number of amendments to make the whole procedure more efficient. we can therefore support the report on the whole.
in the light of the above, the commission proposes to extend the scope of the joint action on the exchange of information on, risk assessment of and control of new synthetic drugs, which was launched in june 1997 by europol and the european monitoring centre for drugs (emcdda), to include the following areas: the joint action, which consists of three elements - an early warning system, a risk assessment by a scientific committee and a community procedure for the control of substances notified in the member states - has proved its effectiveness and fully justified its existence and the simplification of procedures, as i, like the rapporteur, welcome the extension of the scope to new narcotic substances and the introduction of deadlines for each stage of the procedure. this proposal, which, with the amendments introduced by the rapporteur, has been supported by a large majority in the committee responsible, meets the wishes of those who have not given up the fight against drugs or have chosen the irresponsible path of the least resistance. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that this area is absolutely crucial for the future of the population of the member states, especially young people, and that this fully justifies closely coordinated action to ensure a rapid response and effective monitoring of the nature, origin, trade and consumption of new narcotic drugs and new synthetic substances.
in writing. - (pt) i welcome the eu's signing of the international convention against organised crime, i.e. the un convention against transnational organised crime and the accompanying protocols on the fight against trafficking in human beings and smuggling of migrants. this extremely important convention is the first legally binding un instrument in this field and the first global instrument to combat criminal networks, providing universal definitions of certain basic criminal concepts in the fight against organised crime. it is important to establish the widest possible cooperation on the basis of common procedures and minimum harmonisation of legal norms. only in this way can we combat crossborder crime more effectively and prevent criminal networks from taking advantage of the existing differences and lacunae in the legislation of the member states. this convention could make possible more effective cooperation between the signatory states by harmonizing the definitions of criminal offences in the various national legal systems, so that an act which is considered an offence in one of the participating states is also recognized as such in the other signatory states. four serious offences are made punishable: participation in organised crime, money laundering, obstruction of justice and corruption.
in the light of the extremely miserable living conditions of millions and millions of migrants and victims of human trafficking in the world and in europe, who are subjected to totally unacceptable exploitation and humiliation and who have no rights, i welcome the fact that the council has decided to conclude the un convention against transnational organized crime and the protocols relating thereto to combat trafficking in human beings and smuggling of persons. it is an instrument of international law which will promote better cooperation between countries in the fight against organised crime, in particular through the continuous harmonisation of the definitions of criminal offences (participation in organised crime, money laundering, obstruction of justice and corruption), legal aid, joint investigations and extradition. the protocols, in turn, aim to promote measures to combat trafficking in human beings and trafficking in persons, in particular women and children, in order to protect them from slavery, sexual exploitation and illegal employment, including effective measures to provide legal aid and material support to victims. these are measures which must be implemented quickly and effectively, but which must also be complemented by policies which tackle the deep-seated social causes of the current organised economic crime, from economic crime itself to the exploitation of men, women and children.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the un convention aims to enable effective cooperation between the participating countries in the fight against organised crime by harmonising the definitions of offences in the different national legal systems, so that an act considered an offence in one of the participating states is also recognised as such in the other signatory states. this will be the first global instrument to combat criminal networks, providing universal definitions of certain basic criminal law concepts in the fight against organised crime. it is also the first legally binding un instrument in this field. the two protocols, in turn, contain strict measures to combat trafficking in human beings, especially women and children, in order to protect them from slavery, sexual exploitation and illegal employment. in this connection, attention is drawn to provisions designed to provide victims of trafficking in human beings with both legal aid and material support. article 6 thus obliges the states parties not only to provide information on the legal and administrative procedures in force but also to take measures for the physical and mental rehabilitation of victims of trafficking in human beings. in view of the importance of the issues at stake and the pioneering status of this convention, i can only vote in favour.
in writing. - (pt) i support this initiative, stressing the importance of adopting criminal law for the protection of the environment. we have seen various environmental disasters, such as the recent sinking of the prestige off the coast of galicia. the necessary measures must be taken against pollution from ships to prevent the recurrence of such disasters. i agree with the rapporteur that the proposal for a directive on the criminal protection of the environment should be adopted as soon as possible, so that provisions can be introduced to harmonize criminal and other penalties against serious pollution in breach of community rules. this framework decision aims to strengthen the criminal law framework through measures to approximate the laws and regulations of the member states on ship-source pollution, and it contains provisions on jurisdiction (to prevent conflicts of jurisdiction) and provisions to facilitate cooperation between member states (to establish contact points for the exchange of information). it is important to eliminate the current disparities in the level of penalties which may distort the possible - especially financial - consequences of a pollution accident depending on where it occurs, since such pollution may affect several member states of the union.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) i have followed this debate with great interest, partly because of the disaster of the oil tanker prestige and partly because of the proposal adopted by the european parliament on the initiative of the undersigned to establish a community programme whose sole purpose is to develop instruments for the protection of the external borders of the european union, particularly at sea. all measures to improve safety at sea should be supported as they meet a well-defined collective need. it is appropriate to take action not only against accidents but also against the main sources of pollution of the seas caused by those who systematically violate the community rules in force in this field. such action shows political awareness of the environmental problems that affect us. i therefore voted in favour of the reports on safety at sea, with the exception of the pex report, because i do not agree with the rapporteur's proposal to set up a european coastguard. the eu has a duty to promote safety at sea and should not under any circumstances shirk this responsibility. however, the creation of a european coastguard is going too far and a better solution would be to make cooperation between member states stronger and closer, in order to ensure better interoperability and compatibility between the available means at intra-european level and to avoid unnecessary duplication and overlap.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this report is part of the package of proposals on safety at sea following the disaster of the oil tanker prestige. it can be said that oil pollution of the seas is not only caused by accidents but also by illegal discharge. the directive therefore aims to transpose existing international rules, such as the marpol convention, into community law and to establish guidelines for the penalties to be imposed for infringements of the discharge provisions. however, we should remember that combating illegal discharges not only requires more legislation but above all effective implementation and monitoring, which requires appropriate resources. i reject the proposal to create a european coastguard (amendment no 6) not only because of the sovereignty problems it raises, but because it is not the best solution to ensure that the rules are respected and that they are monitored, and because it does not answer the crucial question of resources, where the present proposal shows political aims that go beyond merely fighting pollution. the need for effective cooperation and exchange of information between the various coastguards and for the necessary financing of adequate means of monitoring and combating marine pollution by each member state is one to which the community budget can make an important contribution.

in writing. - (pt) having such a clear memory of the ecological disaster caused by the sinking of the oil tanker prestige in november 2002, i believe that the illegal dumping of oil and other harmful substances is a very serious act that puts people and the environment at risk and should therefore be subject to criminal liability. the principle of 'the polluter pays' should therefore apply in this field, as is shown by the adoption in december of a proposal for a directive laying down stricter community rules on environmental liability. however, i think that from a strictly legal point of view the situation is rather complex, since the directive is proposed with reference to article 80, which concerns transport, but also defines criminal offences. it is therefore appropriate to consider the appropriateness of the procedure. i also have some reservations about the creation of a european coastguard, because i believe that this area is within the exclusive competence of the member states, which does not prevent close intergovernmental cooperation and the community taking responsibility for providing modern and efficient facilities and equipment. i therefore unconditionally support the objectives pursued, but i have had to abstain because i believe that further consideration should be given to this matter so that an appropriate solution can also be found to this important problem.

in writing. - (pt) in voting on the three reports on nuclear energy, i have followed the political line which i consider to be the most sensible for those who, like me, are in favour of developing this source of energy, provided it is carried out with the greatest possible safety. safety of the installations - and not just of those who work there - and safe handling of spent fuel and radioactive waste, both the final location and the transport to the site of disposal. all member states and candidate countries produce radioactive waste from nuclear power stations, experimental reactors and from many medical and industrial applications. if it is serious that these materials are not permanently deposited, it is even more serious that there are no immediate plans for deposition in the member states. the commission's proposals stress the need to ensure an adequate level of safety in the commercial exploitation of nuclear energy and the need for the countries concerned to implement a number of provisions in this area. with such a commitment, these proposals go further than the existing international conventions. that is why i voted in favour of these reports.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) all member states and candidate countries produce radioactive waste, most of which is not permanently landfilled. no member state currently has permanent landfilling facilities and there are no immediate plans to do so. it is therefore urgent to provide good solutions. instead of a solution based on a common timetable, the rapporteur has rightly proposed a two-step approach which will be more effective and more feasible. each member state shall propose to the commission by 31 december 2006 a time limit for preparing and submitting to the commission the long-term management of all types of radioactive waste on its territory, in accordance with international standards. once the programmes have been submitted, each member state must set its own deadlines for the implementation of the programme, the choice of the site and the construction and operation of the landfill. this approach will make it possible to achieve the objective set with the flexibility necessary to take account of the diversity of the situation in the union. this solution, which respects the principle of subsidiarity, is an important step in responding to the demands of european citizens for regulation in this sensitive area, by creating a responsible framework by means of deadlines, steps and objectives. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - (pt) the it is a question of establishing a legally binding legal framework for the safety of nuclear installations, since nuclear safety measures still vary widely between member states. the aim is to ensure that a high level of nuclear safety is maintained in the eu and the system to be introduced will be the responsibility of the national safety authorities. the community system is intended to complement national systems. community control will be concerned with the way in which the national safety authorities carry out their tasks. it is not responsible for inspecting the safety of individual nuclear installations. the commission's proposal seems well founded. objections may be raised by certain member states who may feel that the commission is interfering too much in matters which fall within national sovereignty as regards the power to decide on the conditions for the construction and operation of nuclear installations. the provisions concerning cooperation with the national safety authorities and the way in which community surveillance is to take place have therefore been very carefully formulated, which we welcome. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. - (pt) the i voted in favour of this important report for the same reasons as i have explained in my explanation of vote for other reports on this 'nuclear package'. there are wide differences between member states in this sensitive area and public acceptance of nuclear risks varies considerably from one member state to another. fortunately, the importance of promoting and sharing 'best practice' seems to have gained a decisive foothold in many aspects of life in europe. the commission's aim in this proposal is to guarantee the implementation of best practice in nuclear safety in all member states and in all civil nuclear installations. i do not think that this proposal is intended to replace the convention on nuclear safety - which was concluded under the auspices of the international atomic energy agency (iaea) - and to which all the member states of the european union are parties, but rather that it is intended to maintain the principle of a high minimum level of safety under the responsibility of the member states, on the basis of enhanced cooperation and solidarity, which is precisely what is expressed in concrete terms in the 'best practices'. i would have voted against if the proposal in question had meant that a power which has traditionally been exclusively national should be transferred to shared competence. it has been part of the rapporteur's deliberations and has always served as a "seam" that has clearly guided the legislator in the moderating direction.
the commission has already taken a number of decisions on the basis of the information available to it, and it is therefore proposing to amend the decision on the basis of the information available to the commission. there seems to be no need for technical nuclear considerations in this amendment. the second question is whether the principle of these loans is acceptable. however, this is a question which would arise independently of the amendment now proposed. it should be noted that the loan scheme was introduced in 1977, at that time only covering the member states, and was amended in 1994 when the question arose whether the eu should contribute to promoting better safety conditions for nuclear installations in third countries, in particular soviet-origin reactors in the former eastern bloc countries.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in view of the critical situation in which tuna fishing is found, the european parliament has decided to proceed with an own-initiative report in defence of both the community fleet and the tuna canning industry. tuna, in all its species, has become a fishery resource with a high commercial and socioeconomic impact, to the point of recently recording strong growth rates. in numbers, tuna represents more than 60% of the eu's canned fish production, generating some 40 000 direct jobs. led by spain, italy, france and portugal, the european tuna fleet is the most significant in the world, accounting for more than 20% of total catches. this is an industrial activity with historical traditions. with this report, the european parliament has no ambition other than to demand a precise and exhaustive assessment of the current situation and to outline the future prospects for this fisheries sector. the report therefore begins by focusing on two key problems in the tuna fisheries sector: the loss of competitiveness of the community fleet and industry in relation to imports from third countries and the preservation and sustainable management of resources. first of all, let us agree that these features are common and widespread in almost all types of fisheries, and not just in tuna. in order to ensure that the european union clearly shows its support for its industry, this report calls for the development of a specific action plan and a framework for structural support for the tuna sector. the european union should use this instrument to require that products from third countries meet the same health standards of quality and food safety as community products. the european union also calls for the intensification of inspections of products in order to ensure full compliance with the conservation standards. in relation to the conservation and management of fisheries resources, tuna has the characteristic of being a migratory species particularly vulnerable to illegal fishing in international waters. in this case, therefore, the european union must, more than ever, prevent the transfer of community vessels to countries flying the flag of convenience. similarly, the capacities of the fishing fleet should be better adapted to the available resources. finally, i would like to take this opportunity to congratulate the rapporteur, mr daniel varela suanzes-carpegna, on his brilliant work, which will certainly help to shape the future prospects of this sector.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as i had the opportunity to say during the debate on the first reading, i believe that the regulation under consideration represents progress, particularly for producers, consumers and also in terms of environmental protection. in fact, we are on the way to a very positive modernisation of the legislative framework for the control of the biodegradability of detergents which dates back to the early 1970s. let me, however, express my dissatisfaction with two points which i consider particularly important and sensitive. the first concerns the need to harmonise additional labelling rules, in particular as regards the prohibition of images which may increase the risk of ingestion of detergents, such as images of fruit or other foodstuffs. these are particularly dangerous for children as they increase the risk of ingestion of detergents by the attractive element they contain. the system currently in force restricts this prohibition to dangerous substances and preparations, which is clearly insufficient. i therefore call for greater protection of consumers, especially the most vulnerable. i would also like to express my disapproval of the imposition in the regulation of non-harmonised national test methods without any provision for their publication as an integral part of the regulation. i think in any of these respects we fall far short of the best solutions.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fisheries sector is not left behind. portugal accounts for 6% of the eu's canned tuna production, which represents approximately 40% of portugal's canned fish production. this reflects the importance of the tuna fleet and the enterprises located in less developed peripheral regions, which are highly dependent on the fisheries sector. the sector has lost competitiveness in the face of pressure from foreign imports as a result of bilateral and multilateral trade agreements, and it has also been affected by the last reform of the common fisheries policy in december 2002. i therefore support the basic idea behind this report, which is that the commission should undertake a study of tuna stocks, the fleet and the sector as a whole and then present an action plan for the tuna sector, setting out a comprehensive framework for structural aid and a plan to protect the sector against competition from third countries. we have always stressed the need for compensation or consumption aid to support the canning sector and to control imports so that we can ensure that imported fish meets the same food safety and quality criteria as community products.
in the case of the mediterranean, the commission has already taken the initiative in the form of a proposal for a regulation on the conservation of fishery resources. the report says that the member states will only be able to benefit from this if the eu decides to do more for this fisheries sector. such a conclusion is impossible, given that the eu tuna fleet and the sector as a whole have lost competitiveness and at the same time make one of the most significant contributions to the eu - the canning industry accounts for some 40 000 jobs in the eu and tuna accounts for almost 60% of the total production of canned fish. i support the proposal that the commission should draw up a specific action plan and an overall framework of structural support for the tuna sector. i recognize that it is important for the eu to ensure that the fleets of regional fisheries organisations are adapted to the available resources, so as to create stability and renewal. this adjustment should include combating overfishing by illegal vessels flying flags of convenience and, as the report suggests, drawing up a list of vessels which comply with the relevant rules and are eligible for fishing authorization, as well as possible sanctions against vessels which do not comply with the rules.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this regulation aims to update the current eu legislative framework on detergents, which dates back to the early 1970s and is spread across many different legislative instruments. despite certain limitations and the fact that it is not sufficiently far-reaching, the regulation does contain some excellent proposals aimed at protecting the environment through controls on biodegradability and protecting consumers by ensuring that they are informed about the composition of products, content lists and effective labelling. we therefore support the compromise amendments tabled to the report with the support of seven parliamentary groups. we regret, however, that the regulation does not require explicit warnings about the risks, especially for children, of the ingestion of detergents and cleaners and prohibitions on the use of images which may be misleading, such as images of fruit. we must not forget that behind the harmonization of legislation there is always a political desire for greater market integration and the removal of obstacles to the free movement of goods. this means that we have serious reservations about the regulation, because it risks undermining the right of member states to introduce effective legislation on crucial issues such as the protection of human health, the environment and consumer rights by introducing restrictions on products which do not comply with these provisions.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the introduction and maintenance of universal service obligations is one of the cornerstones of the european development model, since they ensure, within the framework of a market economy - or rather a social market economy - the full protection of certain fundamental rights. the individual citizen has rights and is not just a unit of production or a piece of the free market. i agree with the rapporteur that we should pay particular attention to rural areas and socially disadvantaged areas, especially the outermost regions. i also agree that social services in the field of social security and social inclusion should continue to be exempted from the competition rules. i support the idea that, under the treaties and in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, the eu should remain neutral in relation to the choice of ownership by the member states. the proposed clarification of the concept of universal service and of the criteria for distinguishing between the different categories of universal service should not lead to greater centralisation or to artificial standardisation. it is of the utmost importance that the public authorities responsible retain their freedom of choice. in view of the vote in plenary on the subject in question and in view of the fact that the proposals for a framework directive were not adopted, i decided to vote in favour.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, following the conclusions of the tampere european council in october 1999, the commission has drawn up a number of proposals to control migration flows and combat illegal immigration. but the truth is that the image of a strong europe that the european union has created with its profoundly restrictive measures on immigration clashes with the real economic needs of immigrant labor. this commission proposal therefore presents immigration as a response to the ageing of the european population and the decline in its working population. i regret that the commission gives priority to the economic and demographic aspects rather than to the social and human aspects that lead to emigration and also to the improvement of the living and working conditions of immigrants in the european union in its various countries. the fight against illegal immigration and trafficking in human beings cannot result in a repressive policy directed against irregular immigrants. it must be against the traffickers and employers who take advantage of this situation. we therefore put forward a number of proposals which we consider important to improve the moraes report, and we hope that they will be adopted. among these i would highlight the opposition to the content of the council directive on family reunification, which is opposed to the fundamental right to live together as a family including an inadmissible proposal to subject migrant children of at least two years of age to a test before deciding whether they can be reunited with their parents; i would also stress our call on the member states to ratify the international convention on the protection of the rights of all migrant workers and members of their families, adopted by the united nations general assembly in its resolution no 45158 of 18 december 1990. but, in addition to calling on the member states to ratify this convention, it is essential to take account of the fact that in the overwhelming majority of cases it is necessary to regularize automatically immigrant workers who, although not holding a residence permit, pay taxes and social security contributions in the host country. we also hope that it will be taken into account that the overwhelming majority of immigrants are third country nationals who migrate to the countries of the european union to escape extreme poverty in their countries of origin and that they should therefore be treated as victims and not as potential criminals. finally, i regret that the european people's party wants to call into question in the moraes report approved political rights, in particular the right of immigrant workers to vote in local elections to the european parliament. immigrants must not be regarded as disposable workers who are thrown away after being used. immigrants, and women in particular, must be considered worthy of receiving conditions of welcome which respect human rights, fundamental freedoms and equal economic, social and cultural rights.
mr president, commissioner antónio vitorino, ladies and gentlemen, the report we are now discussing, 'immigration, integration and employment', clearly reflects the contours of a multifaceted and uncontested problem of current concern in the european union and in each of the member states. the treaty of amsterdam and the tampere european council laid the foundations for immigration policy in the union. today, more than ever, there is an urgent need to attach greater importance to this issue for reasons that are mainly related to a significant increase in the flow of immigrants to europe in recent years, the need to maintain the levels of economic development of europe due to the growing demographic deficit and the shrinking of the labour force and the enlargement and changes in the dynamics of migration resulting from it. to illustrate, according to the united nations, italy will need 6,500 immigrants per year for every million inhabitants. my country, portugal, currently hosts 400 000 legal immigrants, representing 8% of the working population, and in the next 50 years it may have a 17% decrease in its current population. immigrants are thus a resource for the labour market. but not only that. their rights are inseparable from the fundamental rights of the human person. each member state, in coordination with the union, must therefore define migration flows in accordance with the needs of its labour market, along with a response based on solidarity, humanism and integration in welcoming those who come to us in search of better living conditions. the member states therefore face a common challenge: to improve the management of migration flows by improving integration policies for new immigrants and those already settled, always in collaboration with the countries of origin. finally, as regards the rights of citizenship which must always be present in this matter, we believe that it would be premature and perhaps excessive to grant the right to vote in european elections. as regards local elections, each member state should retain the prerogative to grant or not grant the right to vote to immigrants it receives.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner antónio vitorino - whom i congratulate on his birthday - we are witnessing an increase in illegal migration movements, usually managed by criminal networks which mislead potential migrants who end up being forced to work in conditions which are totally contrary to what they were promised, including sometimes physical and/or psychological abuse and violations of their human rights. this initiative is therefore very positive and i congratulate the rapporteur, mr claude moraes, because it addresses three fundamental and interrelated issues in a balanced way. firstly, the management of migration flows. there should be a common immigration policy with common conditions and rules for the entry and residence of migrant workers which should always take account of the real needs of the labour market and of the economy itself in each of the member states. it should be up to each member state to assess and decide whether or not it needs to increase its labour force, by how much, in which sector, taking into account its actual needs as well as its capacity to welcome and integrate such immigrants. there should be a fight against illegal migration flows by offering economic migrants the possibility to use clearly defined and transparent legal channels to compensate for any labour shortages in each member state. the proposal for a directive on the admission of third-country nationals for the purpose of employment should help to make it clear to potential immigrants how to obtain legal access to the territory of the union, and the fight against illegal work should be strengthened and those who benefit from it should be penalized. secondly, the improvement of the integration of immigrants into the european union. there should be a common approach to ensuring the integration of third-country nationals into our societies, with rights and obligations in the field of residence, access to education and employment, and promoting their non-discrimination at economic, social and cultural levels. and thirdly, and lastly, the need for cooperation with countries of origin in order to strengthen their capacity to manage mr president, a community policy on the movement of non-nationals from the member states of the union must be innovative and responsible. the report also stresses the need to ensure that the european union's policies are in line with the objectives of the lisbon strategy, which is to promote the integration of the citizens of the union into the european union. the promotion of common asylum and return policies, the introduction of more secure documents and information campaigns in countries of transit and origin of illegal immigration are areas where innovation is taking shape. what, then, is responsible politics? it is not just about consolidating the union's external borders and making them a fortress, but also about opening them up without rules, leaving the expectations of those who demand our countries to their fate. reality has shown us that neither of these methods is capable. we therefore want entry rules so that we can be generous in our integration. this is where our social concerns come in. we do not want these people to live without being integrated, without participating, benefiting and obliging themselves to the community to which they are becoming a part of. it is this dialogue between rights and obligations that defines the existence of the human being in society that we want to preserve. realistically, we consider that the reception is mutually beneficial for the person and for the host member state. this common policy will, however, be less effective if it is promoted by only one of the parties. we therefore welcome the cooperation agreements that have been concluded with the countries of origin and transit. we cannot agree to the proposed creation of a european border guard corps, which merits further discussion. but we also agree with the option of including in these agreements measures of an economic or commercial nature which would only come into force if the agreements were respected. it is about respecting the commitments made. i would like to conclude by congratulating the rapporteur on his excellent contribution to the defence of a community policy on the movement of persons which is responsible, demanding and generous, with the participation of the various parties concerned.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking commissioner philippe busquin for his presence and to stress the quality of the commission's communication on the future of the textile industry in an enlarged europe. we are, however, very concerned and have many questions. i will now mention a few of them, which have already been mentioned by my colleague, mrs concepció ferrer. how will the commission translate its proposals into specific measures? what is the timetable and budget for their implementation? i would like to recall the optimistic words of commissioner pascal lamy in regard to the textile and clothing industry, which he described as a sector with a future in the european union and of the greatest importance in the european trade agenda. commissioner lamy recently said that 'in 2005 there will be no more import quotas, but our interest in industry will remain'. we must face the challenges of the present and the future, but we must also make a firm commitment to safeguarding jobs in this sector. to this end, we are aware that it is essential to promote the competitiveness of enterprises through innovation, productive flexibility, training and retraining of the current workforce in this industry. i would like to stress a few points from mrs concepció ferrer's motion for a resolution: - first, the vital role of the structural funds. i support the request that the financial framework of the structural funds include a specific regional initiative for the sector to deal with the difficulties that will arise after 2005 and to adapt workers to the new requirements of the labour market; - secondly, the creation of a textile and clothing observatory. this measure would allow the analysis of the development of trade between china and the european union and ensure the respect of the rules in force in both regions. the commission is not prepared to accept the amendments tabled by the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy. all bilateral trade agreements of the european union must incorporate the principle of corporate social responsibility, respect for the fundamental rights of the international labour organisation and sustainable development.
mr president, it is well known that the textile and clothing industry remains very important in the enlarged european union, employing some 2 700 000 people, mainly women, after having lost some 850 000 jobs and many thousands of businesses between 1990 and 2001. the threat of total abolition of import quotas on 1 january next year could thus cause serious problems for development and worsen unemployment, especially in areas with a high concentration of these industries, as is the case in portugal, particularly in the north and the beiras. and it is noted that there is already a serious problem of relocation of multinationals. for example, at this moment in my own city, vila nova de gaia, a company with german capital, brax portugal, is threatening to close within days and to put 450 workers, mostly women, out of work. it's a difficult situation that we're living through a little bit all over the country. it must be borne in mind that this textile and clothing sector is strategic for the european union, with great potential for the future, and that it can make a huge contribution to promoting economic, social and territorial cohesion. on the other hand, it can cause serious problems of unemployment and development blockages if these situations are not prevented by appropriate measures. the commission has already made a number of proposals to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not disrupted by the introduction of new technologies. that is why we consider it essential that the commission should present a concrete, coherent and explicit action plan with regard to instruments, financial means and timetable, and that it should give particular emphasis to these points: the promotion of innovation and the use of new technologies in the sector, the strengthening of interaction between all the branches of industry, the implementation of a broad vocational training programme, the modernisation and strengthening of support for small and mediumsized enterprises in the sector and the protection of the environment. it is also necessary to define a community programme - with adequate means of support - for the sector, particularly for the disadvantaged regions which depend on it. and yet, it is important to take account of a sectoral negotiating perspective for the textile and clothing sector, particularly in the context of the world trade organisation negotiations.
mr president, i would like to welcome these initiatives, both the oral question and the legislative resolution which we are voting on tomorrow, and say that we will support them as well as some amendments tabled by colleagues on this subject. our vote is for greater emphasis on the question of free, equal and fair trade and the principle of reciprocity in international trade relations, which, as we know, is not the case today, and the textile and clothing sector is a case in point. we also believe that it is essential to pay more attention to the case of china, to treat it objectively and realistically, because a mere observer is not enough, very concrete measures must be taken to prevent that country's hegemony in terms of international trade in textiles and clothing. china already has a world share of almost 25%, which is truly frightening, particularly for countries which are really developing countries, such as bangladesh or vietnam, and which may also be victims of china's role as a compressor in this sector. we believe that china cannot continue to be treated as a developing country, its weight in industry must be taken into account, otherwise we risk killing the entire textile and clothing industry in the world, wherever it may be. finally, on the question of access to markets, we would consider it interesting and useful if the resolution could mention - it is no longer possible at this stage - the need to put into practice a concrete set of commercial measures to be taken by companies to conquer new markets. it would be essential to create support mechanisms for participation in trade fairs, for the opening of representative offices and distribution platforms, for market prospecting missions, etc. - measures which we leave to the commission's consideration.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, it was in the textile industry that the industrial revolution began in the last quarter of the 18th century in england. it has a pioneering history, an active present and a future full of challenges and uncertainties. the european textile industry is now threatened by competition from countries with very low prices for their products, where there are no environmental concerns or constraints. the exploitation of labour, especially child labour, reminds us of the dramatic beginnings of our industrial revolution. the european textile industry survives, modernizes and renews itself in spite of everything, bridging the gap between industry, crafts and art, contributing to a way of life. the liberal dogmas which prevented the european union from adopting an industrial policy, and which even feared a deindustrialization of europe, have been overcome, and european leaders are now opening their eyes and proposing to defend the european textile and clothing sector. we therefore welcome the commission's communication, although i consider it to be quite lengthy, and we support the motion for a resolution tabled by mrs concepció ferrer, which contains the essential elements of a european policy for the sector. as trade policy is a matter for the european union alone, it is imperative that the commission does not use the textile and clothing sector as a bargaining chip to obtain concessions in other areas which are considered more attractive. it would be a serious shortsightedness to do so and ethically unfortunate. on the contrary, the negotiators of the doha development agenda must strive to achieve conditions of access to third country markets which are fair, requiring in particular the application of the principle of reciprocity and the opening up of new markets. portugal, as everyone knows, is a country where employment and economic and social cohesion are very much dependent on the textile and clothing sector, and is therefore very sensitive to crises or the decline of that industry. there are even portuguese regions with a high industrial concentration that are already in crisis at the moment. the commission is therefore asked to act and not to rely on rhetoric.

in writing. - (pt) the this report is intended to support the first proposal for a regulation on financial and technical cooperation with the occupied territories. it does so to a certain extent, so that the few amendments are limited to clarifying the provisions in terms of content. the report is intended solely to improve and clarify the commission's text at the technical and legal level. this is a matter on which there seems to be general agreement. the aim is to provide assistance in the event of occupation not only to states and regions but also to local authorities, regional organisations, public bodies, local or traditional communities, business support organisations, private operators, cooperatives, mutual societies, associations, foundations and non-governmental organisations. i can give my full support to this cause. the committee on industrial policy, external economic relations, research and energy adopted this proposal unanimously at its meeting on 12 january 2004. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
the commission's proposal, which has been examined by the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection and has resulted in only one amendment, is of the utmost importance for plant genetic resources. this long-debated issue was incorporated in 2001 into the international treaty on plant genetic resources for food and agriculture. the purpose of this proposal for a council decision is therefore to ratify the international treaty on behalf of the community. the importance of adopting this report is shown by the fact that 33 countries - out of the 40 co-signatories - have already ratified the international treaty covering 35 food crops and 29 fodder crops, which establishes a legally binding overall framework for the sustainable conservation of plant genetic resources in the food and agriculture sectors. another clear sign is that the report was adopted unanimously by the committee responsible. the aim is to give all the signatories of the treaty access to such resources, while allowing them to share the commercial and other benefits of such access. i voted yes.
mr president, i would like to say that what is particularly at stake in the vote on these reports by mr fava and mr sanders-ten holte on the single european sky is the adoption of rules for the framework and organisation of european airspace aimed at greater operability, safety and punctuality of the air navigation services provided daily to thousands of consumers, most of whom are ourselves members of parliament. the interinstitutional agreement reached shows that it was possible not only to improve this regulatory framework in compliance with the treaties, but also to accept the rights of the member states concerning the exercise of their sovereignty over the airspace overlying their territories, to safeguard existing international agreements - such as the one which delegates control of air traffic in the north atlantic to portugal - to define, in agreement with the member states concerned, flight information areas, known as 'functional blocks', or to choose the providers of air navigation services. the most important of all air safety interests were thus taken into account: the strengthening of technical cooperation and interoperability, coordination with the military aviation authorities and the sovereign rights of the member states in the field of air navigation. my vote in favour was bound to accompany this convergence, which has resulted in such a general agreement being reached, extending from the trade unions to the operators, from the national authorities to the commission, the council and the european parliament.
in writing. - (pt) although i fully agree with the objectives set out in the proposals before us, namely to reduce delays in european air traffic by making more efficient use of the airspace of the member states while maintaining high safety standards, i have always expressed concern about their content. i would therefore like to mention three points which i consider particularly important in the agreement just concluded, namely that the definition of the functional airspace blocks is a matter for the member states alone and cannot be changed by the eu, that it is recognised that a more efficient use of airspace requires closer cooperation between civil and military authorities, and that each member state is free to designate service providers within its own airspace, under the responsibility of the national surveillance authorities and without being subject to any other body.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour because i believe that an effective common policy on air transport must also involve improving the current safety standards and generally making air traffic in europe more efficient. the fact is that, without effective guarantees of regularity and safety of air services at european level, there will be no free movement of goods, persons and services as provided for in the treaties. optimizing capacity to meet the needs of all airspace users and minimising flight delays also justify my position. i welcome the realism of the joint text, which is a clear step forward from the commission's original proposal, which restricted too much the sovereignty of states over their airspace and which was somewhat vague on the common transport policy and the military sphere. in this respect, prudence requires that the powers of the states and the international agreements which bind them be strictly observed, leaving it to their initiative and decision whether to extend cooperation further. i therefore believe that it is justified to introduce provisions to ensure that each member state can take the necessary measures to protect its national interests in the field of security and defence policy.
in writing. - (pt) the the proposal which the conciliation procedure has resulted in meets some of the concerns we have expressed since the beginning of the matter, first and foremost with regard to sovereignty over airspace, since it has been decided that the functional airspace blocks should be defined by agreement between the member states. in the event of disagreement, they may choose to refer disputes to the single sky committee, whose opinion they must take into account, but on this point it would have been possible to go further by clarifying the relevant principles and provisions. the council also adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia, which calls for the establishment of a european union-wide police force. the control of the santa maria flight information region by portugal (assigned by icao) has also been secured. it has also been established that the provision of air services falls within the exercise of the prerogatives of public authorities and is not of an economic nature justifying the application of the treaty's competition rules, and that each member state is free to designate a service provider (public or private) within its own airspace. however, there are points on which we had tabled amendments which were not adopted and we have therefore voted neither for nor against.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) - this joint draft regulation is the part of the legislative package on the single european sky which immediately gives rise to the greatest amount of consideration. it thus provides for a functional separation between the national supervisory authorities and the service providers, since the different authorities may choose different service providers under a non-discriminatory charging scheme. although it is recognised that these services are clearly in the public interest, private operators may also be selected. in its proposals, the commission understood and treated airspace management as a simple economic service, similar to the liberalised telecommunications markets or transport services under the supervision of a european regulatory body. the agreed text departs from this line of thinking, since it does not merely expressly provide that each member state has the right to designate a service provider within its own airspace - under the responsibility of the national supervisory authorities and without being subject to any other body - in order to ensure full freedom in terms of both the means and the procedures for doing so. that is why i voted in favour. i would also like to emphasize the concept of 'experience in the field' as a criterion that national authorities should apply in their recognition procedure, as well as the mutual recognition of licences and the implementation of training programmes for air traffic controllers.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this proposal for a directive of 12 july 2002 on public procurement aims to open up public markets and create a genuine internal market for public procurement in line with the objectives of the lisbon strategy. public contracts represent a significant market which is very attractive to the private sector, but they are also an important tool in economic policy which can have socio-economic consequences. once again, with reference to transparency, non-discrimination and equal treatment and with a prejudiced attitude towards public undertakings, it is insisted that the decisive factor in the award of public contracts is 'price'. this opens up these markets to foreign companies, which can jeopardize employment, regional development and the economy of a country, as is the case in portugal with the former sorefame and the shipyards of viana do castelo. instead, public contracts could be a tool for selective support to specific enterprises and regions in order to achieve economic, social and environmental objectives in accordance with the political choices of each country by virtue of other public contract award criteria. as regards the latter, the provisions of the regulation are very limited, although it is positive that the court has recently ruled that the contracting authority has the right to define criteria. we have therefore voted against the common position of the european parliament and the council.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) both proposals, one in general and the other specifically, aim to simplify and modernise the eu rules on public procurement procedures, a simplification which i of course welcome. the new rules are designed to improve the single market and to ensure greater transparency in this area. i therefore welcome the outcome of the conciliation procedure, particularly on the last point on which there was still disagreement, namely how the criteria for awarding contracts should be defined. i think that the provisions have been considerably improved and are therefore easier to understand. they will promote the free movement of goods in the award of public supply contracts, the freedom of establishment and the freedom to provide services in the award of public service contracts and public works contracts on behalf of the state, municipal and regional authorities or other public bodies. i also agree with the call for the use of electronic signatures as a means of ensuring and strengthening the confidentiality of tenders. finally, i agree with the call - also made by the conciliation procedure - that member states should be obliged to implement the directive through effective, accessible and transparent mechanisms.
in the light of the recent developments in the field of public procurement, the commission has decided to extend the scope of the directive to cover public contracts for the supply of water, energy, transport and postal services. the commission proposal for a directive of 12 july 2002 is a continuation of the liberalisation already begun in the energy, postal and transport sectors, in line with the objectives of the so-called lisbon strategy, and is intended to open up the water supply to private operators. public contracts in this area conflict with public services and, in the case of water supply, their purpose is to provide a legal framework for the award of contracts to private parties, a common practice in various portuguese municipalities. it is therefore strange - to put it mildly - that in the report on services of general interest in the last plenary session parliament spoke against the opening up of the water supply market, but that this parliament implicitly accepts this opening up. we have therefore voted against the common position of the council and the european parliament, although we note that some improvements have been made in relation to the original proposal.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) i support this report, which deals with an issue of great importance for the lives of the citizens of the member states of the european union. the new legal instrument, a directive, aims to reduce the amount of packaging and other polluting waste by setting a number of targets which are more ambitious than those of the previous directive, which is still in force. particularly noteworthy are the changed minimum recycling rate, with 55% of packaging waste to be recycled by weight in 2008 compared to 25% today, and the range of very concrete measures to be taken to recover and recycle the different types of materials used in the manufacture of packaging. i support the idea that the member states' return, collection and recovery schemes should be open to participation by all interested parties and that any discrimination against imported products and heavy materials should be avoided. although i understand that the targets are quite unrealistic due to insufficient infrastructure, i very much regret that portugal, together with greece and ireland, will not have to implement the new directive before the end of 2011. i voted yes.
