mr president, portuguese newspapers have reported the situation of serious exploitation, ill-treatment and genuine slavery to which portuguese workers have been subjected in several countries of the european union, such as france, the netherlands and england. today, a portuguese newspaper, the jornal de notícias, states in its headline 'more portuguese are being mistreated in the netherlands', adding that the dutch authorities are already aware of the situation. but, the report points out, in the dutch case the reports are characterized by unprecedented violence against the portuguese. it is said that there are cases of assaults on workers in some companies in the netherlands or at the hands of recruiters, it is said that the most elementary rights, namely food and housing with a minimum of dignity, are not respected, it is said that there are real organized networks with branches in several countries that are engaged in recruiting workers, which is a real scandal. the question therefore, mr president, is whether we should act immediately to put an end to these situations. i ask you, mr president, to inform the commission and the council and to take immediate action to solve these serious problems and violations of the rights of workers and of people in general.
mr president, i too share the praise that has been given to this report. this is an excellent initiative and i also hope that, as most of my colleagues have said, it will be possible in the course of the work, particularly in the course of the plenary, to arrive at what was the initial philosophy of mr giorgios katiforis, because, as he said, the essential question that arises today in connection with this owninitiative report is whether or not the activity of rating agencies should be regulated and, if so, whether it should be regulated at national or european level. as the rapporteur himself said in his explanatory statement, this is clearly a political decision and this debate has been very enlightening on this point. the rapporteur, however, initially chose, without any doubt, the need for regulation, favouring regulation with a european dimension, despite the fact that some voices, particularly those closest to the sector, had expressed themselves in the opposite direction. the representatives of the sector understand that their activity is in the field of economic information and that it is therefore important to ensure full freedom of economic information. it is obvious that the need for information is not incompatible with the need and the interest of regulation, and while it can be said that the rating agencies have generally done their job well under the present system, it is also clear that - and there are many examples of this, as the honourable members who have spoken before me have already mentioned - new problems are arising today which require new solutions and, probably, a new system. the rapporteur's choices are also in line with the legislative approach developed by the european union in the financial services area. the protection of the public interest therefore justifies the introduction of regulatory bodies for this activity, in my view, because the legitimacy and eligibility of certain financial assets for certain types of applications for the benefit of the general public already depends on their outcome. i therefore believe that the rapporteur's first initiative, which was not fully welcomed by the committee on economic and monetary affairs, should be taken up and supported by the house because, although it is a healthy bold move, it is absolutely justified.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, as is well known, this 1993 directive, which lays down minimum conditions for the organisation of working time and which aims to ensure the highest level of protection of the safety and health of workers, should have been transposed into national law before 1996, providing for limited possibilities for derogations. the fact is that several member states have used and abused these derogations and have failed to comply with several of their requirements, in particular the maximum limit on working hours in sectors such as health, the hotel and catering industry. and once again, after the seven-year deadline, the commission unfortunately does not have clear options for solving the problems identified. i therefore support the general proposals in the cercas report, in particular the call for an amended proposal for a directive to solve the existing problems and ensure a high level of protection of the health and safety of workers, and for a comparative study on the effects of long working hours on the family and health and their effect on both sexes, and on the protection of employees and others who are harmed and put at risk by exhausted workers due to long working hours. the court of justice itself has taken a position in some cases, including the time available in working time, thus confirming the fundamental principle that hours which are not fully available to workers due to work duties should be considered as working time. as the rapporteur, alejandro cercas, who deserves my praise for his work, has suggested, we must put an end to the derogations in the form of the individual opt-out clause and avoid the increase in pressure on workers and abuses that threaten family life itself. my group, the gue, is putting forward proposals which will allow us to go a little further in the development of these rights. and i would stress our call for a revision of the directive which initially reduces the maximum weekly working time from 48 to 42 hours; and secondly provides for a gradual reduction of the working week to 36 hours over the next seven years, in order to encourage a further reduction in working time and redistribution of work in the member states as an effective way of reconciling working life with private life, of promoting equality for women and of combating unemployment. finally, i regret that the ppe is insisting on distorting the report adopted by the committee on employment, showing its intention to maintain unacceptable situations which call into question the effective protection of workers' health and safety. so you can be sure that we will continue to vote against these proposals, as we did in the committee on employment.
mr president, we are all well aware of the effect and impact on the world population of atypical pneumonia during much of the past year. the prolonged helplessness of the experts in the face of this epidemic has generated a new kind of insecurity which has resulted in a high number of victims in the first place and in a climate of instability in society because it has highlighted the risk to the lives of all those who could contract the disease. because i understand that life and health are the most precious things we have, i have come, mr president, to express my concern about this new epidemic: the flu whose virus comes from chickens and for which no solution has yet been found. according to studies recently revealed by the scientific community, there is only one certainty: it is highly contagious. and what can you do to counteract it? give him shots? how effective? delimit and isolate neighborhoods, cities or countries from communication with the outside? that was the act 80 years ago and the results are known. and the imports of this meat from all over the world, what security do they have? we all need more complete information so that at least the general population does not panic. we have a duty to act to contribute to a certain accountability in health policy in relation to this new disease against which we feel powerless. it is urgent that we understand whether other animals in our food chain are not exposed to the same risks, as only a few days ago pigs were mentioned as being among the most vulnerable to this type of virus. given these legitimate concerns, all the necessary means should be made available for the prevention and treatment of this epidemic.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the modernisation and harmonisation of social security systems are important issues for member states and we must therefore support initiatives that can help them achieve their objectives. the social protection committee, which is to promote cooperation on social policy between the member states, the candidate countries and the commission, is an example of such an initiative and that is why i voted for it. the committee shall monitor the social situation in the member states and developments in this field. it is responsible for presenting reports, mainly on poverty and social integration, issuing opinions, and establishing contacts and cooperation with the relevant bodies in this field. i would like to stress that the role of parliament must be given priority. the committee should effectively inform parliament so that parliament can follow up on cases and parliament's position should be taken into account in all activities of the social protection committee. finally, i would stress the need for a balanced gender balance in the committee's delegations.
in the case of the social protection committee, the council has adopted a decision on the basis of article 100a of the treaty on european union. it is the result of the entry into force of the treaty of nice on 1 february 2003 and, in particular, of the new legal basis under article 144 thereof. the commission and parliament have taken the opportunity to make some changes to the previously adopted procedure. one of the proposals adopted by the european parliament, which i put to the committee on employment and social affairs, is to ensure that the joint report on social protection pays particular attention to 'poverty situations and developments in social integration in the member states of the european union and in the acceding countries'. in addition, proposals were adopted to integrate the gender dimension in all areas of the committee's work and to report on the specific problems facing women, in particular the feminization of poverty and changes in family patterns. i therefore believe that it is important to work with gender-disaggregated indicators and to focus on the individual rather than the household.
in writing. - (pt) the the treaty of nice provides for the setting up of a committee on social protection, which is to be consultative and to promote cooperation on social protection between the member states and between the latter and the commission. a committee on social protection with a similar status and objectives was established by council decision of 29 june 2002 and has been functioning since then. the report must therefore meet a basic procedural requirement: to set up the committee in accordance with the new legal basis. nevertheless, we should welcome the fact that the committee has also been given the task of monitoring social conditions, promoting the exchange of good practice and establishing the necessary contacts with employers and employees. we also welcome the fact that there is talk of drawing up a joint annual report on social protection to be submitted to the council and the european parliament. in this connection, we believe that an effective procedure for informing parliament should be ensured so that it can regularly monitor matters relating to social protection, primarily poverty. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) as you know, the treaty of nice provides for the setting up of a committee on social protection, which is to be consultative and to promote cooperation on social protection between the member states and between the member states and the commission. a committee on social protection with a similar status and objectives was established by council decision of 29 june 2002 and has been functioning since then. the report must therefore meet a basic procedural requirement: to set up the committee in accordance with the new legal basis. nevertheless, we should welcome the fact that the committee has also been given the task of monitoring social conditions. it shall promote the exchange of good practice and establish the necessary contacts with employers and employees. it will also work towards a more structured involvement of ngos and will pay particular attention to poverty-related issues. i welcome the rapporteur's proposal for a joint annual report on social protection to be submitted to the council and the european parliament. the report shall include a specific chapter on parliament's position on social protection issues. an effective information procedure should be established to enable the european parliament to follow up on a regular basis and the candidate countries should be informed and consulted. i have of course voted in favour of the report.
in the case of the mediterranean, the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's fishing fleet is not affected by the catastrophic effects of the mediterranean sea. there is a clear need for international cooperation, because no state is able to combat the consequences of a major pollution of the sea on its own, and the aim of cooperation must be to prevent and effectively combat such pollution. i therefore support the conclusion by the eu of this protocol on cooperation to combat pollution in the mediterranean, one of the protocols to the barcelona convention (a regionally based initiative to which 14 mediterranean countries have acceded). with its long coastline, portugal should always support any initiative which promotes international cooperation to prevent and combat marine pollution. compatibility with eu legislation is not a problem, as this is even stricter than the protocol, as the eu has stepped up and strengthened its efforts to prevent and combat marine pollution. the initiatives we adopted at the last partsession are an example of this.
in the case of the united states, the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's environmental policy is not distorted by the threat of pollution. the terrible accidents of the last few decades have shown that no state is capable of combating the consequences of a major pollution of the sea on its own. like the other eu member states not bordering the mediterranean, portugal is not a signatory to this regional convention or to any of the eight additional protocols. article 29 of the barcelona convention requires a country to have signed the convention in order to be able to sign one of the protocols. regional initiatives include the un strategy for the implementation of the montego bay convention (un convention on the law of the sea) and are reflected in the lisbon agreement for the protection of the north-east atlantic. but as everyone knows, the lisbon treaty has not entered into force because it has not been ratified by spain and morocco, which cannot agree on the demarcation of the border between their two countries.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) parliament was asked to give its opinion on control measures to ensure a comprehensive monitoring and inspection system which would make it possible to exploit resources in the area covered by the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries on a sustainable basis. the stevenson report calls on the commission to be more consistent in the management of sustainable fisheries and calls for clarification of the eu's powers of control and inspection. the report also calls for more information on the costs of the controls and inspections carried out in the member states. the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries (neafc) provides for the establishment of a mechanism for the control and inspection of fishing grounds. the eu has chosen to divide the task between the commission and the member states. in practice, however, this situation has led to implementation problems, as well as certain limitations which are to be expected when responsibility is shared. without rejecting the system chosen by the eu, parliament must press for greater clarity in the powers of the commission on the one hand and the member states on the other. this could be done, for example, by setting up a european monitoring body.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the purpose of this regulation is to reduce the incidental catches of whale species such as dolphins and guinea pigs in fishing nets, as this poses a threat to the species. there are insufficient data to make an accurate calculation of the number of by-catches of whales in fishing nets and the importance of these catches for the populations. however, there is scientific documentation showing that most of the common fishing nets in europe result in by-catches of whales. by setting new targets to prevent the bycatch of whales, this proposal for a regulation is not merely a response to the scientific literature. it also makes a significant contribution to putting an end to the whaling of whales whose existence is otherwise threatened. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - (pt) the i support this proposal for a regulation on measures to combat the unintentional catching of whale species such as dolphins and porpoises in fisheries and amending regulation (ec) no 88/98. although the protection of whales is covered by the habitats directive, the measures provided for in this directive have not proved sufficient to ensure the necessary protection. as the most serious problems seem to be caused by the use of fishing nets and drift nets, i think it would be appropriate to lay down rules and restrictions on the use of these techniques and i therefore support the proposals which go in that direction. however, despite the conclusions of certain scientific papers, i regret that there are no more precise data available to enable the number of by-catches of whales to be calculated accurately. the eu should work to address this lack of information - and urgently. we need to have reliable data on the populations and on unintended by-catches of whales in various fishing areas and then we need to develop more far-reaching protection measures.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken the necessary steps to ensure that the community's fishing fleet is not affected by the fishing activities of the united kingdom. the integration of environmental requirements into the cfp also includes the adoption of measures to minimise the impact of fishing on marine ecosystems. recent scientific reports have shown that certain deep-sea areas need protection against mechanical erosion caused by fishing gear. i therefore support the commission's ban on the use of driftnets in the darwin mounds. the measure will bring major environmental benefits without any significant impact on the fishing sector, as fishermen will continue to be able to use driftnets outside the fishing zone where the darwin mounds are located and within the protected zone they will be able to use vessel-built gear that does not come into contact with the seabed.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the outermost regions have specific structural and socioeconomic conditions which may create persistent economic handicaps, including economic dependence on very few products and limited market access. their economy is based mainly on tourism, agriculture and fishing, as is the case with the autonomous region of the azores and madeira. this own-initiative report, which many people will welcome, is therefore important. i agree that article 299 (2) of the ec treaty should be the legal basis for all measures concerning the outermost regions, including fisheries. i also agree that it is important to compensate for the extra costs of marketing certain fishery products and that the budget for the posei programmes should be increased. we must continue to support the renewal and modernisation of the local fleet, extend the instruments made available by the commission to a greater number of new fish species and support the active participation of fishermen in the common fisheries policy. the most urgent need in the context of the conservation of the fisheries sector in the outermost regions is, however, the management of fish stocks and the guarantee that only local fleets may fish in the exclusive economic zone, which the rapporteur also recommends to some extent in article 12. we need detailed information on the fish stocks in the outermost regions, especially the stocks of black swordfish.
in writing. - (pt) the this report is based on the fact that the common fisheries policy does not take due account of the special interests of the outermost regions. the rapporteur rightly believes that there is a conflict in many ways between the common fisheries policy, which is based on continental interests but which also applies to the outermost regions because they are an integral part of the european union, and the specific needs of the outermost regions, which are due to their specific geographical, economic and social conditions. it should be added that the reform of the common fisheries policy has not taken sufficient account of the needs of these regions. in this connection, a number of priorities must be identified, which are reflected in various measures that require our attention. first of all, we must make the instruments available to the commission cover a greater number of new fish species from the outermost regions and maintain aid for the construction of new vessels after 2006. secondly, there is an urgent need to increase scientific research into fisheries resources and, finally, to create fishing zones specifically for local fishermen. i voted in favour of the report because i want to support this consistent policy of responding to the needs of the outermost regions.
in writing. - (pt) i agree with this own-initiative report which raises the question of the impact of the common fisheries policy on the outermost regions of the european union. as the rapporteur rightly points out, and as article 299 (2) of the ec treaty also states, the outermost regions have special structural, social and economic conditions, due in particular to their topographical and climatic conditions, geographical location, small size, remoteness and economic dependence on a few products. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that we must systematically adapt the common fisheries policy to the needs of these outermost regions and that there is a great need to develop a coherent and structured policy in this area. financial support should be provided to these regions to compensate for the additional costs of marketing their fishery products and the funds made available should be better used. i also strongly support the idea of setting up a fisheries monitoring body in each of the outermost regions, both to monitor fisheries and to monitor the state of fisheries resources and the environment.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the recent accounting scandals, such as enron and parmalat, are further evidence of the consequences of the liberalisation of capital markets and the role of credit rating agencies, which gave these large transnational companies a clean bill of health in terms of creditworthiness, even though they did not disclose information about their activities. this could only happen because credit rating agencies are a product of the private sector, a self-regulating product of the market that creates mechanisms to assess the creditworthiness of entities that fund themselves by raising money from third parties, such as companies that go public on the stock exchange, and even states, in the case of public debt issuance. credit rating agencies exercise a great deal of power in financial markets, as credit ratings are a legal criterion for qualification for investment portfolios. moreover, the credit rating 'market' is highly concentrated and the largest institutions, two of which are headquartered in the usa - one of which gave parmalat a positive credit rating - operate as an oligarchy. as a self-regulatory instrument, credit rating agencies serve to further the liberalisation of capital markets. in order to be considered as a significant regulatory body, they must be regulated by public bodies within the framework of national legislation and case law. the report is capable of asking questions and diagnosing, but it does not prescribe medication, which serves only to promote these self-regulating instruments. the question is more political than technical, and politically speaking the final product justifies our vote against it.

in the case of the mediterranean, the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's fishing fleet is able to compete with the other member states in the world market. the concern is mainly related to the reliability of the information, which is often questioned, creating undue tensions between controllers, researchers and fishermen. the following two questions are therefore of crucial importance: - first, fishermen should play an active role in the management of fishing effort and participate in the review of resource surveys in cooperation with inspectors and scientists. fishermen are the main beneficiaries of sustainable exploitation and recovery measures. it is therefore important that we establish appropriate bodies which allow for effective communication between the parties involved; - secondly, a comprehensive assessment of the socioeconomic impact of measures to restore resources or to reduce fishing effort should be carried out. the implementation of these measures, which are sometimes voluntary for fishermen, as is the case in portugal with sardines, requires compensation at public, national and community level. it is also necessary to increase eu support for research in the fisheries sector and to create the material and human conditions necessary to improve scientific advice.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) scientific research has become a very important instrument in the implementation of the common fisheries policy and is essential for the sustainable management of resources. the fishing quotas in the eu have had serious socioeconomic consequences. portugal has been particularly hard hit by these measures, particularly in the context of the conversion of activities and the dismantling of large parts of the national fishing fleet. i see the impact of fisheries management measures every day in the ports and at fish auctions in my region and i am furious that the commission continues to follow the same policy without evaluating the socioeconomic impact of implementing these measures. it is therefore important that these special arrangements, which are irrevocable, can be justified by scientific reports containing highly reliable information on the development of resources. the lack of objective information means that the current scientific reports give rise to conflicting interpretations in the different member states, which counteract the effectiveness of the measures to protect fishery resources. i would like to take this opportunity to welcome the work of the rapporteur. i share his concern about the lack of scientific advice on fisheries and the scarcity of financial and human resources. i also support the need to strengthen the links between scientists and the fishing industry, which can make the final results more feasible.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fisheries sector is not left behind. eu measures based on scientific advice can have serious consequences for fishing communities. it is against this background that we see the importance of this issue and the need to improve the quality of this advice. the warning given by mr lage thus gives the community the opportunity to base the common fisheries policy on more accurate and timely advice, which should provide a stronger scientific basis than has been the case so far. it is unacceptable that we continue to see that 'the commission seems unwilling', as mr lage puts it, to take account of all the available scientific advice. this only increases the suspicion of a lack of objectivity in their decisions, which often do not take into account fishing communities that are already completely unprotected. my support for this report is therefore also an expression of my solidarity with the portuguese fishermen who have been so seriously affected by the commission's - and in particular commissioner fischler's - fisheries policy.
mr president, i begin by regretting that commissioner franz fischler is not here. it is truly incredible that this should happen in the face of such a major debate. farmers have the right to a decent income, and the guarantee of a fair price for their produce should be the basic premise of the common agricultural policy, in order to guarantee a standard of living adequate and equal to that of other sectors of activity in order to maintain agricultural activity throughout the european union. it is true that these are objectives enshrined in the common agricultural policy, but the mechanisms of the policy are in complete contradiction to the objectives, giving priority to a policy of reducing producer prices and to the external and internal liberalisation of agricultural markets. it is known that this policy is responsible for the disappearance of thousands of farms and jobs, and has promoted the concentration, intensification and verticalization of production, the centralisation of land and the increasing desertification of the rural world. it has also exacerbated the unfair distribution of agricultural aid between producers, production and countries. it is this model which, 12 years after the 1992 cap reform, still maintains the profound injustice of 20% of large farmers getting almost 80% of the support. it is recorded that in portugal 1% of large farmers received almost half of this aid, which we have always contested. the truth is that the current reform of the cap, with the dissociation of production aid from historical reference values, freezes these asymmetries. it was a lost opportunity not to move towards genuine modulation and the setting of limits on aid which would not be a mere transfer of funds to rural development but would serve to bridge the deep inequalities in the distribution of aid between farmers and countries. it should also be noted that the reduction in the selling prices of products and the increase in production costs, even with partial compensation for production aid, led to the disappearance of some 16% of agricultural holdings between 1995 and 2002 without consumers experiencing a reduction in food prices. in fact, these increased over the same period by about 11%, while the producer price index fell by more than 1%. the gradual deregulation of the cap market mechanisms is therefore a determining and worrying factor, in addition to the existing discrimination between continental and mediterranean production. given the volatility and specificity of the agricultural sector, effective mechanisms for market regulation and stabilisation of supply are indispensable to ensure agricultural incomes. it is also important, as the rapporteur calls for, to provide adequate external protection for the agricultural market and to set up community intervention mechanisms in the event of disasters affecting this sector. we also think that rural development needs to be strengthened, but that means an increase in the agricultural budget and not a freeze until 2013, as the copenhagen council decided. the strengthening of the agricultural budget would make it possible to guarantee compensatory payments to farmers in less favoured regions or to farmers with lower incomes. this is essential to maintain a multifunctional agriculture and good quality agricultural products.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, after a first recovery plan for cod, the commission has decided to move forward with a new initiative, this time on the northern fisheries. another one is already in sight covering the southern fishery. if sustainable management of aquatic resources fully justifies the protection of endangered species, fishing limitation measures should be duly justified by sound and up-to-date scientific advice and by integrating the pragmatic observations of fishermen. the gaps in scientific assessments are public knowledge. parliament had the opportunity to denounce them in its lage report this week. in this context, the souchet report is par excellence in calling attention to the need to update data on the basis of information provided by international bodies in the fisheries sector. such restrictions have very serious socioeconomic consequences for the seafarers, further restricting the already very limited fishing activity. the figures presented by the commission to limit the catch of the fish are such that their application would have dramatic social consequences, economically unsustainable and impossible to manage commercially. it seems obvious that the socioeconomic consequences should be assessed prior to the submission of any recovery plan. however, this was not the case. such measures are therefore acceptable only if they are strictly proportionate to the objectives of sustainable resource exploitation and also take into account their economic impact. large variations in total allowable catches, or tacs, can in some cases lead to the transfer of fishing activity from one species to another, thus indirectly causing further imbalances. parliament has already drawn the commission's attention on several occasions to the excessive rigidity of its recovery plans. therefore, a multiannual, flexible and gradual approach is undoubtedly more appropriate, allowing for a perfect adjustment of fishing effort to the state of resources rather than through rigid instruments with irreversible and socially dramatic consequences.
mr president, the presentation on the financial perspectives of the union which we have just heard from mr prodi allows us to make some brief reflections on the policy of economic and social cohesion. i do not want to say at this stage whether the financial perspectives proposed here by the commission represent a percentage gain for this or that cohesion country. that is not the perspective of my intervention. moreover, even in this perspective, it is important to stress that the countries which aspire to be beneficiaries of community funds from 2007 onwards have not yet won the most important of the challenges: that of overcoming their own structural backwardness and that of ensuring the economic and social cohesion of their populations. i therefore prefer to focus on the political significance of the commission's proposal in this area. by maintaining, or rather taking the risk of maintaining, the level of the union's financial resources by 2013 at 1.24% of the community's gross national income, the union is decisively betting on the european policy of solidarity as the only way of achieving homogeneous growth for the whole of the european union in the wake of the lisbon strategy. as the enlargement to ten more countries comes to fruition, it must be stressed that this is a primary objective to which the capacity of the beneficiary countries, both old and new, to carry out the indispensable structural reforms that solidarity with the others implies and presupposes must correspond. the position of parliament on this matter can therefore only be one of political support for the commission's proposal. in doing so, it is also helping to prevent the six richest member states of the union from adopting the same position, which has proposed that the community budget be reduced in future from 1.24% of european gross national income to 1%. we must therefore denounce those political leaders who speak of europe and solidarity and have national interests in their pockets.

in writing. - (pt) the this report deals with the current crisis in agricultural incomes in a number of member states. the crucial question is whether the cap is meeting the objectives which it has set out in the treaty in terms of ensuring fair living conditions for farmers and the agricultural community. the fact is that although the income of farmers as a whole increased by 7% between 1995 and 2002, this result was achieved as a result of a reduction in the number of holdings of 18%. we know the cost to portuguese farmers of having to abandon or change the profession they have always practised. the problem is also that agriculture is lagging behind other economic sectors. the aggregate data also conceal large differences, since 20% of farms receive 73% of agricultural aid. these holdings cover only 59% of the total area and employ only 25% of the agricultural workforce. this is a politically and socially unacceptable situation, which nevertheless explains the behaviour of certain countries, which want to preserve their privileges in the common agricultural policy. we therefore support the position expressed in the report in the recommendations on the newly strengthened second pillar of the common agricultural policy, which is to promote rural development. (parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the number of holdings under the cap has decreased considerably (15.7% from 1995 to 2002), which has meant that the average income of farmers has increased in the eu as a whole. the increase in income has thus been conditional on a reduction in the number of holdings and an increase in their size. more diversified activity and differentiation have also helped to maintain farmers' incomes. if we look at the real situation in agriculture in the various member states, we find that farmers very often depend on public support and on fluctuating prices and markets, which gives them a feeling of uncertainty resulting in a low level of investment in both crop modernisation and diversification. the increase in the concentration of farms, if left unchecked, will lead to the depopulation of rural areas, which will also endanger all the (not always quantifiable) concomitant phenomena which today owe their existence to agriculture. the objectives of 'competitiveness' and 'multifunctionality' must be reconciled, so that farmers are guaranteed a certain minimum of security and can be confident that they can maintain acceptable living conditions and stable incomes, and so that an economically sustainable farming community is created throughout the eu that can maintain the greatest possible number of farms and jobs. i vote for it.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not disrupted by the effects of the crisis. it is a socioeconomic and cultural activity of great importance, which must ensure high quality agricultural products. the food and animal health crises that have occurred in the eu show that the current agricultural model based on the cap is not sustainable. it is a model which leads to intensification of production, which is profoundly incompatible with a multifunctional agriculture. the development of a sustainable agricultural culture therefore requires the development, implementation and financing of an agricultural research culture which makes it possible to identify the importance of agriculture for both the development and functioning of rural areas and for high-quality nutrition. the mere 2% of the sixth framework programme's resources are not enough to finance research into, for example, more sustainable agricultural production, food quality and safety, rural income alternatives (non-food production), the gender dimension, new forms of market regulation and improved organic farming methods. other areas where research is needed are in relation to gmo crops and biotechnology, not least the coexistence of gmo crops with conventional and organic crops, the possible risks of releasing these crops into the environment and introducing them into the food chain.
in writing. - (pt) the this report shows that the funding for agricultural research should be increased in the light of the trend towards multifunctionality, greater emphasis on rural development and the need to make certain specialised forms of agriculture, such as organic production, more market-oriented. the rapporteur therefore recommends that the funds of the sixth research framework programme be used to support projects and initiatives in the field of agriculture and rural development, given the considerable potential in areas such as food science and the development of products to promote local production and the economy. we fully agree that the increasing consumer demands in terms of traceability, hygiene control, ingredient quality, etc., require significant investment to improve quality levels and maintain competitiveness. since such investments are not easily made in small and medium-sized enterprises, conditions must be created for them to be made available in industry as such or at regional or national level through public funds. i therefore voted in favour of the report.

four years after the illusion created by the so-called 'lisbon strategy' adopted during the portuguese presidency, what we have at community level, and in portugal in particular, is a much more serious socioeconomic situation in which not a single social objective has been achieved. the only decisions that have had a positive response have been liberalization and privatization, the precariousness of employment, the attack on public services, that is, the neoliberal agenda of the big european employers, the agenda of unice, the table of the big industrialists, which has become the alpha and the omega of the economic and social policy of this european union. the commission's report shows that the economic revenue will be 'more of the same': the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a good example of the need to ensure that the protection of workers from the risks related to asbestos is not jeopardised by the introduction of new technologies. we have more unemployment, and the jobs created have been scarce, increasing the number of workers on fixed-term contracts by four million and part-time workers by two million. the relocation of multinationals continues, exacerbating unemployment and stifling the development of many regions, as is happening in my country at the moment, affecting especially women and young people. that is why we insist on a review of the lisbon strategy, a moratorium on liberalization in order to achieve economic recovery and sustained demand. but that is also why we insist on suspending the stability pact and replacing it with a pact for social progress and employment, in line with the objectives of full employment, sustained economic development and economic and social cohesion. only then will we have more training, more education, more innovation and more research, which are essential conditions for sustainable development in the european union.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the importance of this memorandum of understanding between the european community and the national tourism administration of the people's republic of china, which will enable chinese citizens to visit the eu as tourists, lies in the fact that china is one of the main starting points of world tourism and represents a market with many expansion opportunities. the bilateral tourist agreements between china and certain eu member states mean that these tourists can only visit specific destinations in the eu. this restriction will be removed if the new agreement enters into force. it is of the utmost importance that the agreement includes a readmission clause requiring tour operators who are to process visa applications to inform the issuing member state and the chinese authorities of any tourists who are no longer in the group or who have not returned to china. these agencies are thus obliged to cooperate with the competent authorities of the contracting states in order to contribute to the return of tourists who have remained in the eu after the expiry of their visa. i agree with the rapporteur that this unprecedented acceptance by the chinese authorities of a readmission clause may open the way for the conclusion of a genuine readmission agreement with china at a later date.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this proposal aims to update the implementing regulation on the system of own resources of the european communities, following the council decision of 29 september 2000 which suspended the contribution of 'gnp resources' to the financing of the budget and codified the so-called british cheque with adjustments to its financing for the main net contributors, germany, austria, sweden, the netherlands, and the consequent increased contributions from the other member states, including portugal, which is unacceptable. we have always said that imbalances in net transfers cannot be solved on the revenue side and that the principle of 'fair compensation' must not be sacrosanct. national contributions to eu financing should at least correspond to each country's share of community gdp, or there should be harmonisation of member states' per capita contributions to this financing. the central question in the report is whether to include an audit provision for a general review of the system with a view to introducing european taxes instead of the current system of national contributions for the adoption of the financial perspective, an objective which is also included in the commission's proposal. the objective of gradually granting fiscal sovereignty to the eu will not only indirectly support the federalist path towards european integration, but will also have implications for the tax policies of the member states and for the tax burden of citizens. it will not, however, lead to a more equitable financing of the budget.
in writing. - (pt) i share the view that any new system should focus on the abolition of existing compensation schemes, the financing of the budget by the member states according to uniform criteria and the transparency and democratic provision of own resources. the system of own resources has undergone numerous changes - sometimes blocks - largely as a result of the very development of traditional own resources (customs duties and agricultural levies) which have fallen. in 1988 a fourth revenue was added (in addition to vat), namely gdp (gross domestic product), which i believe means that a more transparent system can now be introduced. the commission has also endeavoured to simplify the financing structure by introducing a system based more on the gnp contribution and recommends that the correction mechanisms be phased out. i wholeheartedly support the wish for reform and the declared principles of transparency. i am still awaiting the proposals which the commission has put forward, and as far as this measure is concerned, my doubts as to the impact and nature of a single own resource - that is, the eventual inevitable european taxes - make me neither vote for nor against it.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we all know that the treaty of amsterdam directly confers on every citizen of the union a primary individual right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states, irrespective of whether or not he is engaged in an economic activity. this right is also enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. this implies that citizens of the union must be able to move between the various member states in the same way as nationals of a member state move or change their place of residence within its own territory. we all recognize, however, that there are still many obstacles to the exercise of this fundamental right today - a situation which has been confirmed by numerous judgments of the court of justice on this subject. it is therefore essential that this directive be adopted as soon as possible in order to simplify the exercise of the right of free movement. i therefore support the recommendation of the rapporteur, mr giacomo santini, whom i congratulate on his excellent work, that we adopt this common position as it is presented to us. it covers a large part of the amendments proposed by the european parliament at first reading and seems to me to be fairly balanced in general. furthermore, any further amendment would imply the reopening of negotiations and would call into question the urgency of adopting this directive, especially in view of the proximity of enlargement. i would like to highlight the main proposals, which i think are the most important: firstly, to reduce administrative formalities to what is absolutely necessary; secondly, the right to free movement without any formalities being required for a period of three months; thirdly, the introduction of a right of permanent residence after four years of uninterrupted residence in the host member state; fourthly, the imposition of limitations on the possibility of refusing or withdrawing the right of residence in respect of a union citizen on grounds of security and public order; and fifth and lastly, as regards the definition of the concept of family, i would like to stress that the harmonisation of the conditions of residence applicable to union citizens should in no way impose changes to the legislation of the member states and their definitions of family status. the treaty excludes family law from the scope of union competence, so this is an area of national competence.

proposed. i agree with that view, the fact that an agreement has been reached on this matter is in itself valuable. at least we have taken a step, albeit a small one, which is decisive in that it can serve as an incentive for the european union to cooperate in criminal matters. i know that my country, portugal, welcomes this draft framework decision, which does not raise any particular difficulties in relation to our law. the definitions used in the framework decision are based on existing un conventions on the fight against drug trafficking, and it can be said that these definitions are not the strictest, they are the lowest common denominator that could be reached. in this way, all forms of trafficking, cultivation and sale are penalized. furthermore, the penalties provided for by the member states should be effective, proportionate and dissuasive, including custodial sentences. in determining the level of penalties, the amount and nature of the drugs involved in trafficking are of greater importance, and the fact that they were committed within or outside a criminal organisation is of greater importance. on the other hand, the phenomenon of drug tourism must be discouraged, and the news from the dutch minister of justice that his government intends to discourage drug tourism by making its legislation more stringent in restricting sales in coffee shops to residents only is welcome.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we have been lamenting here the lack of attention paid to the questions of external borders. they are one of the weakest links in the system, which has negative consequences not only for the effective protection of internal security, in particular with regard to the threats of terrorism, illegal immigration networks and trafficking in human beings, but also for the full application of the principle of free movement. it is therefore urgent to adopt coherent measures in the field of border security without jeopardising the member states' own competences. a common policy on the control of the present and future external borders should be developed, which implies the application of common standards and the establishment of common structures in order to establish an integrated management of those borders, including the establishment of an independent agency ensuring a high and uniform level of control and surveillance. i therefore welcome the commission's initiative, which is generally quite positive. my colleague von boetticher must be expecting me to make a reference to his excellent report, and i cannot help but congratulate him on the excellent work he has done and say that, like him, i find it regrettable that it has not been given a more community character, following what had already been requested earlier by the european parliament. we also continue to await a proposal on minimum standards for return procedures and mutual recognition of return decisions. i am convinced, however, that this will be a positive step towards strengthening mutual trust between member states in the control of the external borders which are common, which means that weakness in the control of one state will inevitably have a knock-on effect on the security of all the other member states. this is all the more relevant if we take into account that with enlargement the union will have ten new states which will become responsible for controlling thousands of kilometres of the union's new external borders.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) in december, parliament approved the 2004 budget - both the community budget for the 15 eu countries and, in cooperation with the council, indicative figures for the enlargement of the 10 new member states. the focus was therefore on a community budget of 25 million, even though enlargement will not take place until may. the purpose of this draft amending budget is to set out the fixed amounts for the 25 member states. the question here is not only technical, but it is not primarily procedural either. the main issue is the content of the first budget for an enlarged union, including countries where the average per capita income is considerably lower than the current eu average, a budget with payment expenditure raised to the level of inflation, the lowest budget in constant prices since 1987, a budget which not only fails to contribute to economic and social cohesion but also institutes discrimination against the new member states, a budget which is a poor example of parliament's role as budgetary authority, accepting year after year cuts and realignments which, despite considerable protests, are in line with the objectives of the 'charter of the six'. this budget does not bode well for the financial framework for 2007-13. it is characterized by political objectives dominated by the fierce focus on competitiveness, and where social issues are replaced by military and security issues. it would be difficult for a budget to be more explicit.

in writing. - (pt) when an official vessel of a member state detects and pursues on the high seas a vessel suspected of illegal drug trafficking and sailing under the flag of another state, the legislation currently does not allow it to intervene without the prior authorization of the flag state. the need for prior authorization and the time it takes to obtain it mean that many operations to combat drug trafficking on the high seas end in failure. the basic objective of the spanish initiative must be seen in this context. the aim is simply to increase cooperation between the customs authorities of the union in combating the trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances by enabling, in cases of special urgency, an official vessel of a member state to enter the high seas against a vessel flying the flag of another state where there are good reasons to believe that the vessel is being used for illegal drug trafficking, without the prior authorization of the flag state concerned. although this initiative is limited to offences arising from the illicit trafficking of drugs on the high seas and in the light of the amendments tabled by the rapporteur - although we do not approve them all - i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - (pt) the as the report states, the most effective guarantee of the proper implementation of community law begins with the quality of legislation. only legislation of the highest quality can be understood and applied correctly. appropriate control depends on information which is both qualitative - concerning the practice adopted in the application of the law - and quantitative, reporting on the number of directives whose implementation or actual application is delayed by reference to fixed deadlines or is otherwise insufficient. as regards this measure, it is important to stress the importance of close and reciprocal cooperation between the commission and the member states. as the commission's communication rightly points out, it is not enough to simply punish infringements. it is also important that we prevent such violations before they occur. such preventive measures shall involve closer cooperation with national parliaments and strict observance of the principles of subsidiarity, proportionality and appropriateness.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the question of attacks with biological and chemical agents in the eu countries has been discussed in particular since the terrorist attacks of 11 september. a joint programme was adopted to improve cooperation between member states in chemical risk assessment, alarms, intervention, storage of intervention products and research. however, we must be realistic and rational in the measures we decide to take if we were faced with the threat of this type of attack. i believe that the adoption of budgetary and legal initiatives must be based on a clear risk analysis of the real probability of terrorist attacks in the eu. i therefore support the recommendation that a realistic analysis of the threat be carried out, which will form the basis of the eu's response. it will make use of european cooperation between national police forces, including europol, and take account of the results of cooperation between intelligence services in the fight against terrorism.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this question was almost unanimously adopted by the committee, with only two members voting against. the report aims to improve the preparedness and response to attacks by biological and chemical agents. it concludes that an effective system against such an attack should be based on four pillars: an effective early warning system, an effective early warning system, a well-developed public health system and emergency response plans. what is required is an effective disaster response framework that is far more far-reaching than a stockpile of vaccines, which at first sight seems a simple solution but is no guarantee of success. that is why i voted in favour. terrorism has become a real threat since 9/11. the unpredictability of the fight against terrorism means that it must be prevented. i congratulate mr schmid on his report, but i would also like to suggest a somewhat different approach. measures should be taken to counter biological and chemical attacks. citizens will be protected from terrorist attacks of any kind if such attacks can be neutralised in time.

in writing. - (pt) the the question dealt with in the report is a difficult one because of its historical aspects and its far-reaching implications. we are strongly opposed to counterfeiting and piracy and we want to see rules introduced to promote the use of inventions and discoveries which all people should enjoy in these free and fair times. the first consideration is therefore the protection of intellectual property rights. should authors' rights, trademarks and patents be treated in the same way? while we are opposed to the misappropriation and commercialisation of human knowledge and human heritage, we recognise the difficulty of striking a balance between the legitimate rights of property and the social and common benefits of the subject in question. at least that's the theory. while the mechanisms for protecting these rights cannot stop trafficking and abuse, they must not be so lenient as to enable or even encourage piracy and counterfeiting. an example is port wine and other designations of origin of this type, which should be established and preserved, since they represent a heritage which is universal and therefore local and national. in the context of artificial liberalisation, it can have very serious economic, social and cultural consequences and a detrimental effect on health. the rapporteur has been cautious and it is better to be on the safe side on this issue. we have nevertheless voted against the report because certain amendments were rejected - and this is certainly not a sign of caution - particularly those proposals which deal with 'federalist' tendencies.

in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the drug problem is not simply a problem of the drug trade. in 2001, the commission agreed to take action to combat trafficking at european level in the light of the crossborder problems associated with drugs. the final agreement made major changes to the commission's original proposal, such as the introduction of new sanctions more in line with those laid down in the un conventions on drugs, as opposed to the limited definitions proposed by the commission. we welcome the fact that personal use of drugs is not criminalised, even though the issue is not dealt with as thoroughly as we might have wished. we are opposed to the european arrest warrant, and that is the explanation for our final vote.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the italian presidency was able to reach an agreement on minimum standards for the fight against drugs at european level. the main objections - both in the european parliament and in the council - came from the netherlands, where the consumption and sale of small quantities of soft drugs is permitted. it is therefore understandable that the oostlander report proposes that the council framework decision be accepted in the version presented without amendments, since the text was adopted unanimously after a year of negotiations. that has not prevented me from voting in favour of the proposed measures. i would like to highlight two of these measures, which involve the prohibition of the trade, cultivation and sale of opium, cocaine and hashish, and the prohibition of the manufacture of synthetic precursors when the purpose of the manufacture is the illicit production of drugs. application of the principle of subsidiarity allows member states to use the framework decision to sanction personal consumption, but does not oblige them to do so, thus respecting the different national legal and criminal systems of the member states.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) after many years of discussion in the council, an agreement was reached in november on the establishment of minimum rules for the fight against drugs at european level, and this agreement has now been submitted once again to the european parliament for its consideration. all forms of illicit trafficking, cultivation and sale of opium, cocaine and hemp should be punishable, and the manufacture of synthetic precursors should be prohibited when the purpose is the illicit production of drugs. on the other hand, drug-related activities for personal use only, as defined by national law, are not covered by the framework decision. this means that member states can, on the basis of the principle of subsidiarity, make personal consumption a criminal offence if they so wish, but the framework decision does not oblige them to do so. illegal drug-related activities shall be punishable by a minimum of one to three years' imprisonment and the incitement, complicity and attempted commission of any of these offences shall be punishable. i regret, however, (and all the indications are that this is the result of pressure from the netherlands) that there is no more focus on judicial cooperation and expulsion. i voted for the motion.
in writing. - (pt) the this report must be seen in the context of the proposal to gradually develop a genuinely integrated management system for external border control in the draft european constitution. although the report contains some contradictions due to the transnational perspective - the report supports the role of the commission in the agency - it correctly states that the surveillance of national borders must remain a matter for the sovereign competence of the member states. one of the more positive aspects of the report is the criticism of the proposal to leave the task of deporting immigrants to the agency. what is being proposed is basically to create an agency with the responsibilities that the member states currently have, which will highlight the aspect known as 'outside europe' and help to eradicate immigration and expel immigrants. i accept that there must be cooperation between national bodies to combat networks exploiting immigrants, trafficking in human beings, organised crime and money laundering. however, mechanisms for this purpose already exist and there is no need to establish new instruments which are entirely within the competence of the national authorities and which fall within the sovereign competence of the member states. it is not a question of creating new agencies, but of changing existing policies. that is why we voted against the report.
in writing. - (pt) due to the increase in external borders in air, sea and land that will have to be monitored after the enlargement of may 2004, the eu needs an effective system for the management of external borders, in particular to combat international terrorism and organised crime, illegal immigration, trafficking in arms, drugs and human beings and to combat maritime crime. i therefore support the creation of a european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders. it was in this context that i proposed - and parliament adopted the proposal in november - that when the next financial perspective is negotiated, community programmes should be established to support the re-establishment of defence, in particular a programme exclusively aimed at developing equipment for the protection of the external borders of the european union. in view of the intergovernmental nature of border control and in the light of the experience gained by each member state in the performance of this task, i believe that each member state should be represented on the agency's board of directors in order to ensure that the agency can benefit from the skills of each country and the knowledge that each has acquired in practice at its own borders. since this question is not dealt with in the text, i have had to vote against the report.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the idea of creating a european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders, which is expected to start on 1 january 2005, was born out of the overwhelming need to strengthen the management of control at the external borders, which - and this should be taken into account - now cover 6,000 km in length. the enlargement of the european union must also be taken into account. i disagree with the rapporteur's view that the agency should have a 'more community-like' character, but i agree with the view expressed by the rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs, human rights, common security and defence policy that intergovernmental action on border control should be maintained. this is in line with the commission communication - without prejudice to a system of majority voting in the agency (for operational reasons). on the one hand, this is a result of the community legal system - and the present distribution of powers - but on the other hand, the experience gained by the member states in solving these tasks (whether in air and sea or on land or in all three) has improved the possibilities for safeguarding mechanisms. it is therefore appropriate that the management board be composed of one member from each member state and two members from the commission. i have therefore voted against the report.

mr president, in portugal most farmers are concerned about the commission's proposals for reforming the common organizations of the market in mediterranean products: olive oil, tobacco and cotton. these are bad proposals, either because they continue to discriminate against products with mediterranean specificities, which are always poorly treated by the cap, or because they encourage the abandonment of production, with the disconnection of aid and without any increase in appropriations and market regulation mechanisms that would allow the slightest correction of any injustices in the distribution of aid between countries, productions and producers. the stated objective of the cap reform last july is to achieve budgetary savings, more specifically €113 million of annual savings by 2013, and to aim at liberalising agriculture in the wto negotiations. that is an unacceptable position. mediterranean production is found, for the most part, in cohesion countries and the least-favoured regions, incorporating a strong labour-intensive component such as the harvesting of olive or tobacco leaves, and is often the main source of income for these regions. they therefore deserved fair treatment from the commission. it is unacceptable that the social and environmental consequences are not taken into account, particularly in mountain regions and other lessfavoured areas, as in portugal, where alternatives to these olive oil, tobacco and cotton crops are scarce and where fruit, vegetable and wine production is experiencing serious difficulties. it is mr president, we are aware of the serious socioeconomic problems facing the european union, which are causing distrust among the citizens of most member states, particularly in my own country, portugal, where unemployment is still rising, where there is an economic recession and where the gap with the european union average is still widening, without any reversal by the commission in the face of the deficit problem. it is therefore essential to change the policies responsible for this situation, and it is important that the commission and the council clarify three issues which i consider essential and urgent. firstly, are these institutions ready to make the necessary adjustments to the economic and monetary policy guidelines immediately with a view to replacing the stability pact with a pact for social progress and employment, in line with the objectives of full employment, economic development and economic and social cohesion, in order to ensure more public investment, more and better employment, greater social inclusion? secondly, will they demand that the european central bank lower interest rates to support economic recovery and exports, a crucial issue for weaker economies like portugal? thirdly, will they approve a moratorium on liberalisation, review the lisbon strategy and carry out a thorough analysis of the consequences of what has already been achieved in the various economic and social sectors, in particular in terms of employment, quality and universality of the service provided, degree of user satisfaction and further democratization of the operation of services and their management, also taking into account the difficulties and shortcomings of most enlargement countries? without these measures, it is not possible to implement a policy of economic recovery and sustained demand in the short and medium term. a revaluation of production and labour is therefore required to promote economic development, employment and social cohesion, based on a sustained increase in national and community public investment, in particular in basic infrastructure, education, skills and vocational training, research and innovation, the environment and support for small and medium-sized enterprises. these are the real priorities for which the citizens of our countries expect to have an answer before the european elections on 13 june.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the objectives of the commission's proposal could not be clearer, namely to remove the crossborder tax obstacles which naturally particularly hinder the crossborder mobility of multinational companies within the eu, and to enable a policy of business restructuring and localisation which promotes tax reductions or, from another point of view, greater tax benefits. this is also clear from the common tax rules implemented in the context of the statute of the european company, which are intended to ensure that their activities are not hampered by 'discriminatory' tax rules or by restrictions or distortions resulting from the tax provisions of the individual member states. at a time when there is so much talk of tax relief for labour, tax relief for capital is being given free rein. the central issue is indeed the sovereignty of the member states in the field of taxation and the danger of a shift in the tax burden. however, the possibility of using taxation as an instrument for controlling and monitoring the operations of companies is also relevant, not least in the context of mergers - in this case crossborder mergers - and business restructuring among the major economic groups in the eu. the main purpose of this directive is to extend its scope, which puts the financial interests of the member states at risk, and we therefore reject it.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) in line with the objectives set out in the lisbon process, which aims to increase the crossborder mobility of businesses, the commission has put forward a proposal aimed at eliminating the obstacles associated with the taxation of businesses in the internal market (cross-border tax obstacles). directive 90/434/eec (the so-called merger directive) already provides in some cases a solution to a common taxation system for mergers, divisions, transfers of assets and exchanges of shares concerning companies in different member states, but it is necessary to improve the directive and to extend its scope. the new proposal aims to amend the merger directive in order to reduce the occurrence of international double taxation when companies are involved in business restructuring involving companies from different member states. these specifically targeted measures aim to address the most pressing practical tax problems faced by internationally active companies until a common tax base has been established. that is why i voted in favour.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) continued production aid for olive oil, tobacco and cotton is essential if widespread production cuts are to be avoided and if the specific characteristics of mediterranean agriculture are to be taken into account. the commission's proposal to decouple production aid, which the european parliament now supports, is unacceptable and sends a bad signal before the discussions in the agriculture council. the proposal will have very unfortunate socioeconomic consequences and will promote desertification, especially in the less favoured eu member states such as portugal. the proposal particularly affects portugal, where a ridiculous 360 hectares of eligible area is retained for cotton despite the potential for exploitation in alqueva and the conversion of dryland to irrigated farming, and where, for olive oil, the agreed financing package and the method of development in the olive sector, despite the 113 million euros which it is hoped to save, are counteracting the modernisation of portuguese olive growing and the new planting rights obtained in 1998. this would require an increase in the appropriations for portugal of some eur 20 million. the most serious, however, are the devastating consequences of the massive cessation of production which the proposal will entail, as shown by several studies. that is why we voted against.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the main change is the eu ban on mixing olive oil with other oils of fatty substances, which is very important to ensure the quality of the oil. the second is the prohibition on the use of the term 'olive oil' or any other reference or image which recalls this product, olive trees or parts thereof, on the label or in the consumer information given on all fatty substances, which is contrary to unfair competition. it is also important to introduce compulsory indication of the origin of the oil on the basis of the place of harvest and to maintain production refunds for preserved fish and vegetables. it was essential that the council followed the european parliament's opinion in this area. the council does not, however, propose effective market regulation mechanisms and accepts the cessation of production aid. we regret that the proposal of our group, which sought to maintain at least part of the production-related aid, namely that linked to the actual production and not to the area, has been rejected. i am glad that our proposal to maintain the current control bodies has been adopted, but i am sorry that the others have been rejected.

in writing. - (pt) under article 23 of the act of accession, the eu may make any amendment to the provisions of the act relating to the common agricultural policy which may prove necessary as a result of changes in eu regulations. in other words, the acts of accession ratified by the 10 countries joining the eu on 1 may 2004 can be amended in the agricultural field by decisions taken by the 15. the result of such regulation is that the situation which already entails discrimination against the acceding countries in the agricultural field is further aggravated for them. it should be noted that direct payments to farmers in the acceding countries were already to be phased in, starting with only 25% of the direct payments of the present member states in the first year. now they are also subject to economic discipline mechanisms, which means that they may be subject to further cuts in agricultural payments. in addition, the new direct payments for energy crops and nuts introduced by the reforms of the cap will be covered by the same phasing-in schemes. the accession countries are no longer subject to land payment derogations, which imply greater discrimination, and this has already led to objections from the czech republic, poland, slovenia and estonia. it's just another...
