(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the commission proposal proposes to abolish the vat exemption for services provided by public postal services. the adoption of the proposal would have an impact not only on suppliers but also on consumers and would, inter alia, lead to higher prices for the services provided. the proposal also has to be seen in the context of the current wave of liberalization of postal services in the eu, and this is linked to the creation of a common vat system. i would remind you that although parliament rejected the proposal for a directive on 18 december 2003, the commission has insisted on maintaining the proposal. the rapporteur put forward a number of compromise amendments to the directive, but even if they were to mitigate its effects, they did not call into question the very logic of the vat system or the post-liberalisation directive.
in the light of the above, the commission has decided to extend the scope of the vat exemption to postal services provided by public postal operators. the report was referred back to the committee responsible in accordance with the rules of procedure and it is the new report that is being put to the vote today. the commission proposes to abolish the vat exemption for public postal services, so that they are treated on the same footing as services provided by private competitors, which are subject to full vat. the commission therefore proposes that all consignments over 2 kg be taxed at the standard rate, while allowing member states to apply a reduced rate of vat to addressed postal consignments of less than 2 kg. the rapporteur, however, proposes that the objections which led to the original rejection of the report be taken into account this time, and proposes that the weight limit for standard consignments at the reduced rate be raised from 2 kg to 10 kg and that the entry into force of the directive be postponed until 2007. the proposal is, in my view, a considerable improvement on the previous report and therefore deserved my vote in favour.

in the light of the recent developments in the european union, the commission has decided to extend the scope of the programme to include bulgaria and romania. the report is particularly instructive on economic issues, as it 'congratulates bulgaria on the functioning of its market economy', 'encourages the government to continue its economic reform programme', 'welcomes the increased importance of the private sector' and 'is concerned that any delay or abandonment of strategic privatisation processes may result in a fall in foreign direct investment'. in other words, capitalism is welcomed and any criticism is limited to reservations about the privatisation process and any obstacles to the current large-scale, self-interested capital transfers of eu countries to bulgaria's strategic economic sectors. the report cynically calls on bulgaria to 'abolish the requirement for eu citizens to have a permanent residence permit to work in bulgaria', without any reference to the unacceptable restrictions imposed on bulgarians in their right to travel and reside in the eu countries even after accession. the report also refers to bulgaria's membership of nato, scheduled for 2004, as an implicit precondition for eu membership.

in writing. - (pt) the this report concerns the commission proposal for a regulation following the court of justice ruling on bilateral open skies agreements between eu member states and the united states. the relevant part of the decision is that these agreements were contrary to community law, since the member states had neither the right nor the competence to conclude such agreements. the commission has proposed three measures: to provide a legal basis for community-us relations in the field of air transport; to provide a legal framework for ongoing negotiations and for all other agreements; and to ensure an appropriate division of competences between the community and the member states. from a legal point of view, the commission's proposal is very well founded, provided that it succeeds in closing a loophole in the legislation created by the court's decision. the measures adopted in the council's common position, which were supported by the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism, do not make the political constraints imposed on member states in the negotiation and conclusion of air services agreements with third countries nearly as strict, and i could therefore vote in favour.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this proposal for a regulation follows a ruling by the court of justice following a complaint lodged by the commission against member states which had concluded open skies agreements alleging infringement of the community's external competence and freedom of establishment. the commission proposed that the member states should initiate procedures for the termination of the agreements they had concluded and asked the council for authorization to open negotiations at community level with all the bilateral partners. for matters which fall partly within the competence of the community and partly within that of the member states, the commission proposed a community strategy, that is, close cooperation. in its common position, the council accepted the views of the european parliament. the member states will thus retain the right to negotiate and conclude bilateral air services agreements without prior authorization from the commission, even if the content of these agreements falls partly within the community's competence, provided that they incorporate certain types of provisions which are determined jointly by the commission and the member states. this approach will continue to guarantee the freedom of action of the member states, which is why we voted in favour.
in the light of the above, the commission proposes to extend the scope of the regulation to cover the whole of the european union, including the united states, and to include the european union in the scope of the regulation. the commission proposes a set of rules to be observed by member states when negotiating and implementing air services agreements for this type of joint agreement, which requires the participation of member states' governments. these are to support specifically the community's negotiating strategies and objectives and must not initiate negotiations which fall within the exclusive competence of the community. the council's common position included parliament's basic request that the member states should retain the right to negotiate and conclude bilateral air services agreements without the prior consent of the commission, even if the content falls within the community's competence. it is stipulated that 'standard clauses' drawn up jointly by the commission and the member states must be included in any agreement. the measures adopted in the council's common position and supported by the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism reduce the constraints on the freedom of action of the member states, which is why i voted in favour.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) on 1 january 2004, directive 2003/96/ec restructuring the community provisions on the taxation of energy products and electricity entered into force. this amendment is intended to ensure that the new member states have longer exemption periods because of the risk they face from sudden increases in the cost of living. however, we believe that there is more to it than that and we reject the directive for three reasons: firstly, harmonised energy taxation is not a prerequisite for the proper functioning of the internal market. there are certain advantages to tax competition, but the main one is that this is a question of tax sovereignty with far-reaching implications for a state's social and environmental choices and tax structure. that is why member states have submitted many requests for exemptions. secondly, an increase in the lowest rates will lead to an increase in the cost of living, particularly for workers and the least well-off sections of society. it will lead to injustice and it will not punish those who consume the most. this is typical of flat-rate and direct taxation. thirdly, there is no need to shift the tax from labour to 'consumption' of the environment, where the price is always passed on to the consumer. the burden must be shifted, but to the "use" of capital, otherwise taxation will continue to be unjust.
in the light of the above, the commission considers that the proposed directive should be amended to take account of the new requirements of the directive on energy efficiency and the new requirements of the directive on energy efficiency. harmonised taxation is without doubt a basic prerequisite for the proper functioning of the internal market. the rapporteur believes that 'in order to avoid harmful competition in taxation, the acceding countries should align their excise duty rates with the minimum rates in force in the european union'. this explains why the report calls on 'all member states, including the present ones, to respect the deadlines laid down in the directive and to contribute in general to the development of an environmentally friendly internal market'. although this report deals with a difficult subject - energy taxation - for environmental reasons in particular, and taxation still requires unanimity in the council, i voted in favour of the text.
in writing. - (pt) the although i have great reservations about the tax harmonization process, i believe that we must establish methods of coordination, particularly with regard to tax avoidance on crossborder capital flows, and i am therefore a strong advocate of abolishing banking secrecy and putting an end to tax evasion. the ultimate objective of directive 2003/48/ec is to introduce effective taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments made in a member state for the benefit of owners, thereby guaranteeing a fair taxation of interest income from savings and the right of member states to tax resident persons on their income throughout europe, while removing artificial incentives to capital flows within and outside the union. however, the desire of some member states to undermine the tax base is at odds with their desire to attract capital savings. this is particularly true for states with direct links to tax havens. the best way to effectively tax savings income is through the automatic exchange of information between tax authorities. in order to prevent capital flight, other countries must follow the established arrangements, and in this particular case it is switzerland. unfortunately, there are still difficulties in negotiations with other countries. however, we must go further. we must work on methods of tax coordination to tax capital movements and crossborder transfers of securities at community level.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this proposal for a directive is part of the original monti package of 1998, which paved the way for greater tax harmonisation in the eu. whatever one thinks of the proposals as a whole, and given that we are trying to create a single market, it is understandable that there is a need to create a certain degree of tax harmonization in order to combat tax evasion and double taxation. however, we have a fundamental objection to the approach outlined, because the concept of tax harmonization is federalist and touches on one of the cornerstones of state sovereignty: a state's ability to tax households and companies and thus ensure its autonomy. we are also not convinced of the economic benefits of tax harmonization compared with the benefits of maintaining healthy tax competition. for this very reason, this directive and the rest of the package were only adopted in june 2003. the directive concerns interest and royalties paid between associated companies, with the aim of abolishing taxation at source on these. the amendment aims to extend the list of companies covered by the directive and to incorporate the directive on parent companies and subsidiaries and the merger directive. our concern is that the directive should not facilitate tax evasion or deprive member states of the resources needed to combat fraud and abuse.
the commission's proposal for a council decision on the establishment of a court of first instance for staff cases is part of the reform of the judicial system enshrined in the treaty of nice, which aims to solve the problem of the increasing workload of the european courts. it responds to the call made at the nice summit, where the court of justice and the commission were asked to 'prepare as soon as possible a draft decision establishing a special court with jurisdiction to hear and determine at first instance disputes between the community and its servants'. the creation of this court would mean that these disputes, which represent about one third of the workload currently assigned to the court of first instance, could be removed from that court. in future, it will be limited to acting as a court of second instance in respect of decisions of the new court of first instance, while the court of justice will only intervene in very exceptional circumstances and will review the judgments of the court of first instance. despite the staff and operational costs of this new court, which are estimated to total eur 2 453 000 per year, i voted in favour of its creation because it will speed up the processing of cases in the community.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) pursuant to the provisions of article 245 (2) of the ec treaty and article 160 (2) of the euratom treaty, the court of justice invites the council to amend the protocol on the statute of the court of justice as follows: article 17 of the protocol provides that decisions of the full court are valid only if the court is composed of 11 judges. with the increase in the number of judges after enlargement - from 15 to 25 - it is proposed that this quorum be changed to 15. under article 16 of the protocol, the grand chamber, which is convened, in particular, at the request of a member state or a community institution which is a party to the proceedings, is to consist of 11 judges. it is proposed to increase the number of judges in the grand chamber to 13 and to maintain the present quorum of nine judges. the rapporteur and the committee on legal affairs and the internal market say in the explanatory statement of the proposal on which parliament is being consulted: 'this proposal, which seems to be the subject of consensus in the council and the court of justice, is fully sufficient and can therefore be adopted without amendments.' we see no reason not to support this conclusion and that is why we voted in favour.

in writing. - (pt) this report amends regulation (ec, euratom) no 2728/94 establishing a guarantee fund for operations in respect of third countries in the light of the accession of the new member states on 1 may 2004. the guarantee fund covers guaranteed loans to third countries and the guarantees for these loans. with 10 new member states joining the eu in 2004, the fund will be affected by the fact that various countries have been granted loans from the european investment bank (eib) guaranteed by the community budget and which will therefore be covered by the target amount from the moment they join the eu. the guarantees will remain in place, but the associated credit risk will now be transferred to the eu budget. the amendment lays down rules to take account of all these situations and to ensure an orderly transfer of responsibility from the fund to the budget. as regards the financial implications, this is a unique and unavoidable financial operation because it is linked to the enlargement process and i have therefore voted in favour of the report.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the guarantee fund was originally set up to protect the eu budget against potential risks associated with the growing external borrowing. the guarantee facility covers three different types of loans to third countries: guarantees for eib lending, eu loans for macro-financial assistance and euratom external lending. in this context, the fund is also an important instrument for our cooperation policy with third countries. the aim of this proposal is to ensure that the new member states no longer have to be covered by the fund if they become members of the eu and to establish a uniform framework for future enlargement rounds. we have no objection to that. however, we share the rapporteur's view that the fund's parameters should be more appropriate, as they may be too cautious. among the amendments we find it useful, but somewhat unrealistic, to moderately ease the rate of transfer to the fund before the expiry of the current financial perspective. as the rapporteur confirms, the commission should carefully evaluate the financial parameters of the fund and make proposals more in line with the real risk in the context of the period after 2006.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this proposal for a regulation was drawn up in the light of the need to amend regulation (ec, euratom) no 2728/94 establishing a guarantee fund for operations in relation to third countries in the light of the accession of 10 new member states on 1 may and their new status as a result. the guarantee fund was originally set up with the 1993-1999 financial perspective to protect the eu budget against potential risks associated with the growth of external borrowing and therefore only covers risks relating to loans and guarantees to third countries. in the context of this proposal, the commission drew up an overall report on the operation of the guarantee fund, concluding that the fund continued to meet its main objectives for the period 1998-2002. i have therefore voted in favour of this proposal, which, as a technical budgetary instrument, follows a policy with which i fully agree and which aims to ensure that the eu carries out consistent external action, supports development and promotes the well-being of peoples and nations beyond europe's borders.
- the commission proposes that the mandate of the european investment bank to grant external loans be revised to take account of the new neighbourhood policy in an enlarged union, as contained in its proposal for a political and financial framework for 2007-13. if we look at the loan ceiling of eur 20.260 million, we will quickly conclude that the report accompanying this proposal for a legal act adds little to the underlying geopolitical considerations and objectives - in particular the objective of creating a free trade area between the pan-european and the mediterranean area, in which the eu can exert political, economic and military influence at regional level. the neighbourhood policy includes russia as a priority, for which the rapporteur proposes an increase of eur 500 million in the provisional allocation, as well as the mediterranean countries. these loans will clearly serve the eu's own interests and result in increased regional influence and involvement. that is a goal which we reject. more worrying, however, is that this policy of good neighbourliness is at the expense of the eu's cooperation and development policy - in particular with the acp countries, latin america and asia.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this proposal concerns the revision, at the end of the last mandate, of the community bank guarantee for the european investment bank (eib), which is intended to cover loans granted by the eib to non-member countries on the basis of the community's own resources. the eu's enlargement on 1 may 2004 will increase the eib's lending capacity without raising the ceiling on its external lending mandate, which is particularly favourable at a time when the eu is increasing cooperation with the potential candidate countries of the western balkans and is preparing to gradually expand relations with other neighbours to the south and east. according to the eib's business plan, the planned use of the various regional packages for the remainder of the mandate amounts to a total loan greater than the total amount allocated. in the light of these forecasts, the commission has proposed a new geographical distribution of the volume planned for the mandate and the maintenance of the current limit of eur 19.46 million. given the need to improve the eu's relations with its nearest neighbours, i voted in favour of the amendments.
in writing. - (pt) this is a report of a theoretical, conceptual and even ideological nature. when you read the explanatory statement, you get the impression that we live in an idyllic world. this world can be divided into "donors" and those who benefit from the philanthropy of the "donors". nevertheless, the 'donors' must be accountable to their taxpayers, who rightly impose conditions on them for providing aid. there is therefore a real need in the world to ensure that this aid is not misused, and that is why the world bank introduced the concept of 'good governance' in 1991 with a definition of its main aspects. both in the commission's communication and in the critical assessment in this report (which extends the idea beyond the scope of the state, seen as merely a 'supplier' to 'civil society'), 'good governance' is understood as a terminological concept that is more pragmatic than, for example, democracy, and it is believed that this concept should support the eu's development policy. the real world, however, is far from idyllic. there are conflicting interests and no amount of 'good administrative practice' can hide the low importance attached to cooperation in all community policies, the lack of solidarity with or respect for what is 'different', and the constant presence of conditionality imposed by economic and social models. we therefore feel that this report is dangerous because it portrays the world as those who act in good faith would like to see it and not as it is.
in writing. - (pt) the i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european union must continue and strengthen its efforts to promote democracy as a vital part of its development policy. it is also important to promote genuine democratic governance at local, regional and national level. this cannot be stressed enough, and without it we shall not see the desired harmonization of public authorities. for this reason, i would stress the great need for greater involvement of civil society, which will enable us to implement sustained electoral and parliamentary reforms to ensure that political activity becomes more thoughtful and more effective. in this respect, i support the rapporteur's statement on the need to put an end to impunity, which will only happen if independent judicial systems are established or strengthened and civil and political rights are fully respected. finally, subject to the greater or lesser capacity of individual states, i would agree that refusal to provide aid should be limited to cases where governments ignore or are responsible for continued violations of the basic universal rights of men, women and children. this should not, of course, exclude dialogue, humanitarian aid or food aid.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the proposal for a community regulation should comply with the obligations laid down in the white paper on food safety, provided that it lays down requirements for a complete system of registration of all feed business operators and requirements for feed production. the proposal lays down requirements for feed hygiene at all stages of the use, production, processing and distribution of animal feed and maintains certain requirements for imports from third countries, according to which these countries must comply with standards at least equivalent to those laid down in the regulation (measures to be implemented under the comitology procedure). i do not wish to minimize the importance of food safety, but in my view we must avoid measures which are excessively restrictive or harmful to feed producers and which are unreasonably much stricter than those applicable to food producers. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - (pt) the this regulation aims to update the rules on materials that come into contact with food and establishes a framework regulation setting out the rules that should cover packaging and materials, the safety standards to be achieved and the procedure for the approval of both materials and methods. it also contains new provisions on active and intelligent packaging. this regulation is part of the overall package of measures to improve food safety. food safety depends on packaging, which not only protects food from light, microorganisms and air, but also helps to preserve the taste and freshness of food and prolong its shelf life. therefore, special care must be taken with regard to the materials that come into contact with food and the function of these materials. as regards the central premise that all packaging must comply with eu food safety legislation and must not mislead the consumer, we have a major reservation about active packaging. active packaging means changing the composition of food by adding flavourings, removing odour or adding preservatives to prolong the shelf life of products. all of this can obscure the true nature of the food. we therefore agree with amendment no 6, but believe that more thorough studies should be carried out on the use of this type of packaging and its active materials.
in the light of the above, the commission has decided to extend the scope of the directive to include the following products: this is an attempt to better protect consumer health and promote the free movement of goods by introducing a legal basis for technological development, currently regulated by a 1989 directive which is currently under revision. the draft defines 'active' packaging as something designed to interact with food in order to maintain the quality of the food and prolong its shelf life, while 'intelligent' packaging is defined as something that can provide information on the quality of the food. other new materials and products are also taken into account. in conjunction with the proposed concrete traceability measures, these food quality assurance measures will contribute to a real improvement in food quality, to greater confidence among european consumers and, of course, to higher food safety standards. that is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. in 1998, the eu and its 15 member states signed the so-called aarhus convention on access to information, public participation in decision-making and access to justice in environmental matters, whose main objective is to improve the public's ability to participate in environmental matters and to actively contribute to improving the conservation and protection of the environment. signature of the aarhus convention requires the adoption of measures legally binding on the institutions and bodies of the union, and this provision does so specifically with regard to the three pillars of the convention, access to information, public participation in decision-making processes and access to justice and to judicial review in environmental matters. access to high-quality information (preferably made available in public databases) must now be regarded as a basic right of citizens. only by establishing rules on such access will we be able to make an effective contribution to ensuring public control in an area which concerns everyone - genuine environmental citizenship, including access to justice in environmental matters at eu level.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this proposal follows two other initiatives - public access to environmental information and public participation in the preparation of certain environmental plans and programmes - which are intended to contribute to the implementation of the aarhus convention of the united nations economic commission for europe (ece) on access to information, public participation and access to justice in environmental matters. the european parliament's report contains certain aspects which i welcome, in particular the extension of the definition of 'qualified body' (specifically to include local authorities), the possibility of involving private organisations as it says 'to take account of the increasing privatisation of functions which have traditionally been public', or the guarantee that bodies which do not have the financial means to bear the costs can participate. this is a final instrument which could help to strengthen the actions taken by societies to protect their living conditions and the environment in which they live.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this report should be seen in the context of the important package on the environment and more specifically on the incorporation of the aarhus convention on access to information, public participation and access to justice in the field of the environment (three pillars) into eu law. it also aims to address shortcomings in the monitoring of the implementation of environmental legislation. the proposed directive sets out minimum requirements for access to civil and criminal proceedings in environmental matters and explicitly defines the criteria which can ensure better implementation of environmental legislation with the least possible impact. as i said, particularly in my explanation of vote for the korhola report, there must be effective public control in an area which concerns us all, genuine citizen control in order to protect our environmental heritage. this proposal formalises the conditions under which this control can be carried out in a democratic way. however, i did not vote for or against in the final vote, because the report does not specify its position on the convention, which has already been signed by the member states, and this gave me some reservations.
in writing. - (pt) the following the commission communication, which addressed, inter alia, the treatment of mine waste in the light of the specific characteristics of mines and the considerable differences between the sub-sectors of the extractive industries, work has been undertaken to re-examine eu environmental policy in the light of recent mine accidents, such as those in baie mare in romania and aznacollar in spain. i naturally support this proposal because it sets out some minimum requirements to improve the treatment of waste from the extractive industries including the environmental and human risks associated with waste treatment and disposal. in addition, the kind of recycling of waste advocated by the proposal aims at conserving resources, thus reducing the pressure on the exploitation of natural resources. the measures in the directive therefore seek to cover sectors which pose serious risks to the environment and health or which pose potential risks of serious accidents, taking particular account of the structural aspects of an environmental policy which, as the eu proposes, should be sustainable. finally, i would like to highlight some important amendments which aim to protect small quarries which must comply with the requirements of the directive. i voted yes.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) in order to comply with its international obligations, the eu must formally approve the decision to conclude the aarhus convention. the purpose of the convention, which was adopted at the ministerial conference 'environment for europe' held in aarhus on 25 june 1998, is to facilitate access to information on the environment and to improve public participation in decisions which may have an impact on the environment, and we could add a 'third pillar', namely access to judicial review in the field of the environment. the stockholm declaration on the human environment of 16 june 1972 stated that everyone has the right to live "in an environment of a quality which permits a life of dignity and comfort" . . . the maastricht treaty commits the eu to mainstreaming environmental protection in all its policies. this initiative is therefore in line with article 175 (4) of the ec treaty, which expressly states that member states are to ensure that environmental policy is implemented, and this is also another important step towards the desired sustainability of the eu's development.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european satellite navigation system is as efficient and reliable as possible. the commission therefore proposes the creation of two bodies: a supervisory authority and a safety centre. the proposed supervisory authority shall be a commission institution. as the owner of the galileo infrastructure, the commission is also responsible for controlling the satellite navigation system. the security centre shall guarantee the operational and external security of the system. i agree with the rapporteur's suggestion that the know-how found in existing structures should be incorporated into the new institutions, in particular by transferring knowledge from the european space agency (an organisation which had been very closely involved in the programme) to the supervisory authority. i also agree with the rapporteur that it is important to strike the right balance between the independence of the supervisory authority and the transparency of its appointment procedures. i particularly agree that an annual report by its director to the european parliament would not in itself provide a sufficient guarantee of this transparency. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - (pt) i support this initiative because it is a step forward towards establishing a system of judicial and police cooperation which is necessary if the area of freedom, security and justice is to become a reality. this framework decision aims to replace simple cooperation in criminal matters with the principle of mutual recognition. it should therefore allow for faster and more efficient cooperation, while at the same time making the european arrest warrant more effective. it will make it possible to issue a european evidence preservation order for certain objects, documents and information for use in criminal proceedings, provided that these objects are already present in the executing member state. however, measures such as the european arrest warrant and the european arrest warrant will only be effective if they are implemented in all member states. we can therefore only regret that the framework decision on the european arrest warrant has not yet been fully implemented in the eu as of 1 january 2004. only eight member states have implemented it. i am therefore pleased that the recent summit set a deadline of june for the implementation of measures to combat terrorism already adopted, including the european arrest warrant. i hope that the measures adopted in the wake of 11 september 2001 will now finally be implemented. it all depends on political will, and the political will seems to be there!
in writing. - (pt) it is regrettable that the european parliament has not adopted the position of the committee on legal affairs and the internal market and has rejected this initiative of the commission. this proposal is in line with the federalist model, which attempts to remove from the member states fundamental competences which are central to their sovereignty. this would jeopardize the rights, guarantees and freedoms of their citizens. the european arrest warrant is a cousin of the european arrest warrant, which was adopted, let us not forget, under the pretext of 'fighting terrorism'. as has been stated, the commission's main objective is to replace the current legal aid mechanisms based on international conventions with a system of mutual recognition, which requires that a decision in a member state be recognised directly without the need to convert it into a national decision. as has been pointed out, the process is proceeding without the creation of safeguards to protect the citizens of each state, because if the prospect of cooperation between states is jeopardized, the guarantees secured at this level are also in danger. it is also regrettable that amendments seeking to ensure that the rights, guarantees and freedoms guaranteed under the sovereignty of each people in each state are respected have been rejected.
in writing. - (pt) the this report deals with a proposal to enable a member state to issue a european arrest warrant which can be executed in other member states. in other words, the european search warrant is a judicial order issued in a member state for the specific purpose of securing documents and information for use in criminal proceedings which can be executed in other member states, without it needing to be converted into a judicial order in that member state. in the form proposed, the european preservation order will make it possible to secure evidence already available in the executing state. however, it cannot be used to initiate actions or to request the carrying out of investigations in the form of interrogations, hearings, interception, surveillance, etc. i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report, which is a very good report. what i do not welcome are the references to procedural guarantees in amendments nos 5 and 7. this report is about the european arrest warrant and as this is not the place to discuss the issue of procedural guarantees, i have no choice but to vote against it.

disappearances of children and young people, with some mutilated bodies found in the meantime, must be fully matched by us. we cannot give in to counter-information, nor be daunted by the apparent obscurity. it is possible that there are several tragic realities in nampula or elsewhere, and not just one, perhaps also trafficking in people and children, perhaps organs for witchcraft or other non-clinical uses, and perhaps the suspected trafficking of human organs feeding international networks. we don't know, but that's why we can't rest until we know everything. and all of this is worth fighting for, because in any case, it is abject crime and trafficking, which no one can rest easy. sometimes the authorities' behaviour in dealing with these terrible cases is embarrassing, falling into contradictions or seeming to hesitate in the face of complaints. no one likes to see the name of their country internationally mentioned in this regard. we have to understand that. and we will always treat any country with respect. but, with patience and perseverance, we must be able to say that the problem is not embarrassment, the problem is trafficking, the drama is crime. and this kind of crime has to be investigated and fought by everyone all over the world, because this crime has no country, this crime is treacherous and piratical, this threat is international and it affects us all. whether it is to israel or south africa, to asian circuits, to europe or america and whether it is originating in mozambique or poor regions of brazil, whether in moldova or albania, in the torn balkans, in the vastness of africa, in depressed central asia or in the poorest suburbs of asian or latin american cities, we know where this trafficking strikes. like vultures, this organized assault on the human body watches over regions of human misery and where the authority of the state is weak. it pursues lands where the individual and the community are most vulnerable. that's when he attacks where he sees the poorest, where he senses the weakest. so here too we must act by cooperating with the competent authorities, raising awareness, encouraging them, making our loans available, confronting and cross-referencing information, promoting the full clarification of the truth, protecting the peace of mind of the people and dismantling the networks wherever they exist. we are counting on the diligence of the commission and the council, and i would like to see the council acting with the level of diligence that the commission has already shown here. whether it's mozambique or wherever in the world these complaints come from.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the revision of the fourth protocol on fishing conditions between the european union and greenland is a good thing because it is based on truth, transparency and reciprocity. we no longer have, as the commissioner said, paper fish or virtual fish, but we have a relationship between the financial contributions of the european union and the fishing that can really be done because there are fish to be caught. i therefore welcome this revision and i welcome even more the report by mrs rosa miguélez ramos, which is a correct report, a very well structured report, and above all her words, her speech, which has allowed us to really situate the central political problem of this issue. i also welcome the intervention of commissioner antónio vitorino, whose knowledge of fisheries matters does not surprise me, since his many talents enable him to speak about fisheries with a wisdom that amazes me. and here i was convinced that he only appreciated the good fish on the plate... but i really hope that commissioner vitorino will still come and give us lessons in particle physics and molecular biology. (laughter) he has the intelligence and the talent for all of this. but, returning to the political question raised by mrs rosa miguélez ramos, there is the unjust and there is the 'anti-historical' - now that historicism is out of fashion, let me say the anti-historic - removal of spaniards and portuguese from greenland's fishing grounds. because if the spanish and portuguese were the first to discover routes to this world outside, they also discovered centuries ago the fisheries in greenland, from which they were removed. there is now an opportunity to correct this injustice, and this opportunity to correct the injustice consists in allowing the quotas not used by the states which have them to be used by countries like portugal and spain without this signifying a kind of submission of these countries to the authorities of the countries which have the quotas. we are not dealing here with some kind of feudal law, a modern feudal law that has been invented with quotas allocated to a country and then ceded or not to the european union country which, within the framework of the community fisheries policy, wants to use them. i therefore wholeheartedly support the position of mrs rosa miguélez ramos that the european union and the commission should be able to allocate unused fishing quotas to countries such as portugal and spain that wish to use them.
in writing. in 2003, a new protocol was agreed with greenland for the period 1 january 2004 to 31 december 2006, as part of the mid-term review of the fourth protocol laying down the terms of the fisheries agreement between greenland and the european community. this revision introduces a number of adjustments without altering the amount of the financial compensation of eur 42 820 000 per year, but it provides greater clarity in the division between the part intended to compensate for fishing opportunities and development support. we welcome the increase in the alabat quotas, in particular the possibility for the national fleet to catch 800 tonnes of greenland alabat. however, it is recalled that at the time of accession portugal was excluded from this agreement, despite its historical fishing rights in the region. however, given the degree of under-utilisation of quotas, it is important to ensure the principle of sound financial management, i.e. that the fishing opportunities offered by international fisheries agreements are effectively used, without jeopardizing the principle of relative stability. the report and the commission proposal open up this possibility of redistributing the quotas which were under-used in the year in question, but we think that amendment no 5 is a more acceptable text which should be adopted in plenary.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud and the illegal trade in stolen vehicles. theft of cars amounts to about 1.2 million vehicles a year in the member states of the union and has exceeded this figure in previous years, which implies considerable losses amounting to at least eur 15 billion a year. it is therefore essential to combat this form of crime, which causes not only material damage but also physical and psychological damage when accompanied by various forms of violence and which interferes, as the commissioner has just said, with the sense of justice and the feeling of security of citizens. more than 3,300 vehicles are stolen every day, which means that one is stolen every 25 seconds. since i began this speech, two vehicles have probably been stolen, and i hope that none of them belong to any of the members present. it is therefore intended that, by means of an amendment to the schengen convention, public car registration authorities should have direct access to certain categories of data contained in the sis, the schengen information system, while private car registration services should only be entitled to request indirect access through an authority with access to sis. this will help to make sis an even more important tool in the fight against crime, as these authorities will be able to check quickly and effectively whether a vehicle whose registration is requested has been stolen, misused or lost. the functioning of the internal market is thus improved by strengthening the principle of free movement and, consequently, by favouring the progressive establishment of the area of freedom, security and justice and the implementation of the common transport policy. why the direct access? so that vehicles stolen in one country can be registered in another and thus legalized in good time. it is estimated that 30% to 40% of vehicles are stolen by criminal organisations which transform them and export them to other countries inside and outside the union. in large numbers, the operation is achievable in less than 48 hours. there are thus two main arguments: first, efficiency. there are several million vehicles registered in the european union. it would be a huge job for the police to systematically check all these vehicles in sis. some 15 million vehicles are submitted for registration each year. direct access thus allows for an easier and faster way of checking the legal status of a vehicle, which translates into efficiency. secondly, the question of transparency. at present, all member states have found ways of trying to check, at the time of registration of the vehicle, whether it has been stolen, with more or less reliability in the information. all these forms, however, are relatively opaque and complicated. the inclusion of an article in the schengen convention would make everything more transparent than it is at present. and what kind of data are we talking about? data may only be accessed for motor vehicles with a cylinder capacity of more than 55 cm3, for trailers and for caravans with a dry weight of less than 750 kg. i proposed that access be added to data which are not yet in sis, namely vehicle registration documents and registration plates for stolen, misappropriated or lost vehicles, because it is only with this data in sis that the desired objectives can be achieved. the spanish initiatives on the new functions of the sis, in particular on the fight against terrorism, which we have approved here, already provided for the introduction of these data into the sis, but due to a reservation from denmark they have not yet been approved. it is expected that this will happen very soon. i also propose that the proposal for access to data relating to identity documents, as recommended in the opinion of the common supervisory authority, and to data relating to blank official documents, which is too broad and vague a concept, be withdrawn. the data set to which the competent public authorities will have access is thus clearly defined and limited to what is necessary and appropriate, with any access to data that could be considered as more sensitive being withdrawn, limiting access only to data on objects: vehicles. i therefore ask the house to support this initiative and at the same time to reject the proposal put forward by the socialist group's shadow rapporteur, mrs pacciotti, who advocates that the current situation of indirect access be maintained. if this bill passes, everything will go on as before and we will not see any improvement in the fight against these crimes. i think i have been clear about the evidence of the values involved, which demonstrate the need for us to find new ways of combating motor vehicle crime, because the situation as it stands cannot be maintained. mrs paccioti is concerned that by giving direct access we are multiplying the risks of personal data breaches. i have always advocated the strictest protection of the fundamental rights of our citizens, including their right to the protection of personal data. but i do not believe that the amendments i tabled to the commission's original proposal, all of which were approved by the committee on civil liberties, put the protection of personal data at risk. public car registration authorities will have clearly defined and limited access to what is necessary and appropriate, that is only in relation to objects - the vehicles - by asking the system whether or not the vehicle in question is listed as stolen. to refuse to take this step, mr president, would be, in my view, a wrong decision, because it would be ineffective in this fight, and would send the wrong signal to our fellow citizens who require more cooperation and more effectiveness in fighting crime and ensuring their safety.
the rapporteur. mr president, i am aware, as are we all, of the serious problems affecting our tradition of asylum today. in a world that is becoming ever closer together, ever more interconnected and ever more connected by sophisticated means of communication, in which islands of wealth, peace and well-being coexist with worlds of poverty, war and misery, it is only logical that there should be enormous migratory pressures from disadvantaged areas to the more affluent areas. but this large mass of migration, whose main component is economic, is endangering the survival of the asylum system, as many economic migrants, unable to find another legal way into rich countries, try to use the asylum route to secure their entry into the european union. i therefore welcomed the two commission communications. it is essential to develop the european asylum system as called for by the tampere european council. however, new policies must be developed taking into account new realities and facts that were not taken into account at the time because mixed flows of refugees and economic migrants did not exist in such large proportions as today. it is clear that asylum seekers will continue to arrive freely at the external borders of the union. the present tampere system is largely designed for them. it is therefore essential to maintain what is already in the acquis and adopt the directives still awaiting agreement in the council in order to complete the first part of the tampere agreement on refugee status and asylum procedures and move on to a new second phase of development. it therefore proposes that the council be urged to adopt the directives i have just mentioned as soon as possible, as was repeatedly requested at the laeken, seville and thessaloniki councils. it is clear that the present system has many dysfunctions: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rights of asylum seekers are respected, and that the right to asylum is guaranteed. i therefore agree with the commission's position that new methods of asylum should be considered, new methods more suited to reality. a new policy for managing the arrival of asylum seekers in the european union should be developed, mainly through a system of refugee resettlement at union level and through the protected entry procedure. asylum and immigration are two phenomena which, although distinct, are closely linked, but which must be examined together. i repeat that economic aid for the development of the regions of origin of migratory flows must be increased unequivocally with the aim of reducing them and also for reasons of solidarity with the poorest countries and those most in need. i therefore ask that the union develop a legal immigration policy so that economic migrants do not resort to seeking asylum as the only way of legally entering european territory, thereby seriously jeopardising the survival of the institution. europe, mr president, is a land of asylum. protecting it is the best way to maintain this humanitarian tradition.
mr president, madam vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, as the rapporteur, mr luís marinho, has already pointed out, more and more people are seeking better opportunities or protection outside their country, trying to escape persecution, war, violations of human rights or simply poverty and unemployment. in accordance with the amsterdam and nice treaties, and taking into account the results of the tampere summit, we have been adopting various measures and legal instruments in relation to three different realities that exist, namely asylum seekers, temporarily displaced persons and economic migrants. it can be said that all the member states are currently facing, as the rapporteur has already pointed out, a crisis in the asylum system, caused by the misuse of their procedures and the increase in mixed flows, often fuelled by trafficking networks, which are having a negative effect, manifesting themselves in a growing malaise among the public. as such, it is essential that we develop a policy which includes the three essential aspects: first, respect for the geneva convention; second, the legitimate aspiration of third country nationals to seek better living conditions; and third, the reception capacity of each member state and of the european union as a whole. at the heart of this balanced policy should always be a common framework of related measures, detailed in tampere, and harmonized, transparent, efficient and rapid procedures should also be adopted. we must say that although the commission has drawn up proposals on basically all the areas of asylum policy referred to in these conclusions, and parliament's opinion has been requested, after five years we are still awaiting the decisions of the council, which has failed to meet the deadlines set by the european councils of tampere, laeken, seville and thessaloniki. the need to adopt rapidly the outstanding proposals for directives on minimum standards in the field of asylum and immigration was stressed in thessaloniki and the commission was also asked to explore all the criteria likely to ensure that the entry into the european union of these persons in need of international protection can be processed in a more orderly and better managed way and to consider how the regions of origin can better guarantee the safety of these persons. today's debate thus focuses on the report by mr luís marinho, whom i congratulate on the quality of his work, and which is based on two commission communications which, although with different motivations, nevertheless address the basic premises and objectives of a possible redefinition of asylum systems characterized by better management, more accessible and equitable, adding new ways of completing the approach gradually adopted in tampere. in my view, mr president, in order to maintain a general and coherent approach in the establishment of a common european policy on asylum and immigration, it is essential that the following aspects are always taken into account: the existence of legal immigration channels, an integration policy, joint management of migration flows, an intensification of external border controls, a european asylum system, the negotiation of readmission agreements and a common return policy, an effective fight against trafficking in human beings and illegal immigration and support for the victims.
mr president, our colleague mr oostlander, who has worked so hard on this report, raises a number of politically relevant questions concerning the process of turkey's accession to the european union. i would like to highlight two: the first concerns the level of preparation of the european union itself for the future integration of this great eurasian country. what is the impact of your eventual accession? what are the geopolitical constraints arising from the assumption of new external borders for the union, which would become not only non-european borders but also neighbouring borders of armed conflict? how should we view the demographic dimension of turkey's application and the effects it will have on the existing institutional balances? and does turkey's accession strengthen the security of the european union and make its foreign policy more credible and effective in the region? as for the cap, can this common policy be maintained? in what ways? what about the structural funds? these findings do not represent any lesser appreciation on our part for the great turkish nation, quite the contrary. they simply mean that, from our point of view, there is still no public, open and calm debate on this matter, which we consider absolutely essential, at european level. that is why we support the proposal by our fellow rapporteur to ask the commission to undertake a comprehensive study of the impact of turkey's accession to the union, informing parliament and the council of the internal changes that will have to be introduced in the union and the need to reform the current policy in the various key areas we have listed. the second question is, in a sense, the reverse of the first and concerns turkey's political will to continue in full with the necessary reforms of its structures and its institutional and legal framework in order to meet the copenhagen political criteria, as has happened with the other candidate countries. the rapporteur rightly believes that it is up to turkey at this stage to decide sovereignly whether it wants or can adopt as a precondition for the opening of negotiations the political principles and values of the union as being appropriate to the turkish state and society. in this respect, we must recognize that the present government has shown a strong political will and motivation to carry out important reforms in this area, reforms which are difficult and in many cases incomplete, because they clash with the traditions and practices of civil, judicial and military administration consolidated over decades, especially in the field of human rights. the choice of the so-called 'legislative harmonisation packages' has brought its legislation closer to union standards more quickly than would have resulted from a general revision of the basic legal codes on which the turkish political, judicial and legislative system is based, which is positive. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council and parliament, and the council will be consulted on the matter. we conclude by saying that the stage we are at must therefore be understood as one of mutual preparation for turkey's eventual accession to the european union: preparation on the part of the union, which must adapt itself at all levels to welcome the great turkish nation, and preparation on the part of this country, which must continue its efforts to implement effectively the necessary reforms in accordance with the copenhagen criteria. the outcome of this process must therefore be the natural result of this effort of mutual preparation and adaptation and not the result of any voluntarism which does not take account of the realities with which we are faced on both sides.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the internal market with free movement of goods and capital must necessarily be accompanied by close cooperation between member states to combat smuggling and tax evasion. these provisions are part of a package of legislation designed to strengthen mutual assistance between the competent authorities of the member states, in particular in the field of excise duties, where tobacco smuggling is of particular importance. the rapporteur regrets, however, that it is not possible at present to harmonize indirect taxes by means of legislation and therefore considers that cooperation is a temporary solution. we could not agree more, since cooperation is an effective way of combating tax fraud and organised crime, not only in the case of excise duties but also in the case of vat and other indirect taxes. it is above all a way of preserving national sovereignty. harmonisation would create other problems of an economic nature and for the tax bases of the member states. decentralised cooperation is therefore a good solution.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it gives the eu the green light to adopt the convention on the conservation and management of highly migratory fish stocks in the western and central pacific. this convention is part of the objective of conservation and sustainable management of resources which the eu has pursued and seeks to promote. the western and central pacific ocean contains 60% of the world's tuna stock and is therefore of particular interest to community tuna and longliner vessels. to strengthen its fishing capacity and the resources available, the eu has signed various bilateral agreements with pacific coastal states, giving it access to new exclusive economic zones. by acceding to this convention, the eu will be able to participate actively in regional fisheries organisations, which are the most appropriate multilateral instrument for the effective conservation and management of fish stocks and the fight against illegal fishing. i support the european parliament's insistence that the eu should become a member of all existing regional fisheries organisations in which the community sector has a legitimate interest, in order to promote responsible fishing and defend the interests of the fisheries sector.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's fishing fleet is not depleted. this instrument is intended to ensure the long-term conservation and sustainable exploitation of highly migratory fish stocks in this area through the establishment of a fisheries commission, the western and central pacific fisheries commission (wcpfc). the importance of the wcpfc's remit speaks for itself. the area covered by this regional fisheries organization covers 60% of the world's tuna stock and currently has five large community tuna trawlers, with a catch of some 15 000 tonnes per year. in addition, the european parliament has repeatedly stressed the growing importance of regional fisheries organisations, 'as multilateral bodies for the management of resources and as ideal fora for settling disputes between parties and for the implementation of sound management through the fight against illegal fishing'. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that it is of great importance for the member states that the community should also become a full member of this regional fisheries organization in order to defend the interests of the community fisheries sector in these areas as well.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's genetic diversity is not lost. the commission is now proposing to establish a new community programme on the conservation, description, collection and exploitation of genetic resources in agriculture. the programme follows the rejection by the european parliament and the council of the commission's previous proposal in 2001 to fund national measures in this field, which was unacceptable, also because it removed the strategic importance of ensuring the conservation of genetic diversity, particularly in the light of the community's obligations under various international un conventions. this was and is even more incomprehensible when one considers the threat to genetic diversity posed by the possible lifting of the de facto moratorium on genetically modified organisms. the european union must also take the necessary steps to ensure that the european union's genetic heritage and the diversity of food crops, including local and regional specificities, are preserved. this requires local measures to support farmers in maintaining their traditional species and breeds and marketing their products on local and regional markets. we regret that the proposed financial framework for the programme is very narrow in view of the needs identified by the member states and also by the european parliament.
in writing. - (pt) in view of the political and economic situation in guinea-bissau, we understand the importance of the rapid adoption of the amended protocol as a signal to support the efforts of the authorities of guinea-bissau to normalize the situation in the country. we also know the situation of the fish stocks off the coast of guinea-bissau, due to overfishing and the lack of measures and means of control. we find acceptable the objectives of the amendments to the current protocol, agreed in may 2003, which include reductions in fishing effort and support measures to promote sustainable fishing. although we do not wish to jeopardize the adoption of the proposal, we have strong reservations about its distribution among the fishing fleets, since we note that the portuguese fleet's capacity for discarding trawls is reduced by 65%, which is more than the average of the overall reduction in brt. in addition, a licence for longliners with a flight line is missing, so that the agreement will cover only four longliners. it is therefore not clear what kind of assessment of the socioeconomic impact the commission has made of this proposal and what compensatory measures it intends to take. that is a question which we shall certainly pursue.
in the case of the gulf crisis, the commission has already taken the necessary steps to ensure that the agreement is implemented. guinea-bissau's waters, traditionally rich in fish and shellfish, have been suffering from overfishing. in addition, political instability, corruption and lack of control measures have affected the conditions of fishermen. in addition to extending the current agreement until 2006, the amendments are aimed in particular at reducing fishing effort, in particular by non-eu fleets, making better use of community funds and strengthening control measures. these changes will finally enable the guinea-bissau authorities to modernise the fisheries sector in order to improve the monitoring and patrol of the sea and to combat the over-exploitation of its resources. i also agree with the rapporteur when he stresses the importance of keeping the european parliament and the council informed of how the agreement is being managed so that a general evaluation can be made. finally, i hope that this fisheries agreement will make a modest contribution to the improvement of the economic and political situation in the republic of guinea-bissau. the european parliament is thus sending a positive signal by supporting the efforts of the authorities of guinea-bissau to normalize the situation in the country.
in the light of the recent events in guinea-bissau, i would like to ask the commissioner to give us an assurance that the situation in guinea-bissau will continue to be the same. i recognize that the political authorities have sought to implement measures to improve the governance of the country, in contrast to the obvious breakdown under president kumba ialá. in this context, and as a country with few resources and many needs, the income from fisheries is of particular importance and therefore deserves special consideration. it is therefore essential to provide assistance to guinea-bissau to modernise its fishing sector in order to improve the monitoring and patrol of the sea and to combat the over-exploitation of its resources. i share the rapporteur's view that it is important for the european parliament to send a positive signal in support of the efforts of the authorities of guinea-bissau to normalize the situation in the country. despite the recent reports of unrest and riots in connection with the elections under way, i believe that with the support of the european union this african nation will be able to regain its stability. that is my sincere wish. it goes without saying that i voted in favour.
- the commission has found it necessary, as a follow-up to the strategy for sustainable development in the community aquaculture sector presented in september 2002 in the context of the revision of the common fisheries policy, to amend regulation (ec) no 2792/1999 on community structural measures in the fisheries sector, which contains specific provisions on support measures for community aquaculture, in order to clarify the definition of aquaculture, increase community aid for extensive fish farming, develop methods to reduce the environmental impact, support applied research and ensure financial compensation for shellfish producers in the event of the cessation of harvesting. although the proposals appear to be positive, especially with the improvements brought about by the rapporteur's amendments, there are two aspects which give rise to serious reservations. the first is the emphasis on the development of aquaculture, not as a complementary activity to fishing but as a substitute for fishing, which gives rise to serious reservations. systematic disposal and cessation of fishing activities should not be encouraged in order to replace catches with production which creates other problems in terms of the environment, food security and protection of coastal zones. the commission has also proposed a number of measures to combat fraud. secondly, the opportunity could have been taken to revise the regulation in general by raising the maximum amount of individual aid, which the amendments of the european parliament seek to meet, even if they are not far-reaching enough.
