in writing. - (pt) i have had the opportunity to express my concern in the european parliament about the ineffectiveness of fisheries controls. illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is a daily reality in portugal. this initiative allows member states to apply for a community contribution to part-finance specific projects aimed at improving the monitoring of fishing activities. it is just another building block in the development of a policy for sustainable fisheries. in this context, i support the introduction of crossborder exchange of information, as it is a simple and useful instrument for imposing effective, proportionate and above all dissuasive sanctions within the whole of the eu. it is also unfortunate that there is such a wide disparity in the sanctions applied in the eu for the same infringements. this problem is all the more serious since there are no indicators to assess the effectiveness of monitoring. the eu has no information on the number of inspections or infringements found, infringement procedures initiated, etc. i also support the rapporteur in saying that surveillance should not only be carried out on board vessels but also on land. finally, the community's incentives to member states to acquire heavy-duty fisheries control equipment must be strengthened. at the same time, the initiative to simplify and tighten up the allocation of aid must be welcomed.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the adoption of the regulation on the conservation and sustainable development of fisheries resources has broadened the objectives of the common fisheries policy and has therefore also brought new implementing provisions, which not only involve the development and introduction of effective monitoring tools, but also professional training and technical and administrative cooperation between all the sectors and institutions concerned. the commission now wishes to extend and amend the previous scheme for two years in order to strengthen and streamline the means and methods of monitoring and inspection in an enlarged union and to prepare the new common inspection structure for its operation. the problem is the availability of community aid for a surveillance operation involving the purchase of 'heavy equipment', which the commission has not wished to address in its proposal, but would rather give the new member states access to the available funds. since this is particularly important for portugal, which has the largest exclusive economic zone in the eu and a large number of vessels to monitor, it is necessary to ensure that portugal is not excluded from this aid, or at least part of it. i voted in favour of the report because it meets that important wish.
in writing. - (pt) regulation (ec) no 3069/95 provides for the presence of an observer on board all fishing vessels operating in the north-west atlantic ocean and regulated by nafo. the commission has so far ensured the implementation of this regulation on community vessels operating in these waters and has borne all the costs of the observers, and that is how it should be. however, the present proposal is intended to make the member states themselves responsible for the observers and the associated costs as from 1 january 2004, which we cannot accept in any way. although the recent revision of the common fisheries policy means that the monitoring obligations are incumbent on the member states, we are talking here about monitoring within their exclusive economic zones, which is not in contradiction with community financing of the monitoring effort. i have therefore voted against the report.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the fact that we are voting for these regulations should not be taken as an endorsement of the views expressed by the rapporteur. as regards euro coins, it is essential that the public be protected against any fraud and, in this particular case, from confusion with medals and coin counterfeits. since the introduction of the euro, the use of counterfeit euro coins in coin-operated machines has increased. these regulations set out the degree of equality that should be prohibited in medals and coin counterfeits similar to euro coins. it is another instrument for combating counterfeiting of euro coins and banknotes. although we all agree with these measures, we simply reject the rapporteur's declaration of faith in the success of the single currency and in the european parliament's 'unreasonable' support for the 'historic project of economic and monetary union and the single currency'. not only because the practical problems are beginning to emerge as time goes on, as is shown by the inflationary trends and the rising bank charges, but because, at the economic and monetary level, a thorough evaluation of the impact of the euro on economic growth and employment must be carried out, especially in the less developed member states such as portugal.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) two years after the introduction of the single currency, it is now time to analyse the situation surrounding the euro and, on that basis, to propose solutions to the problems identified. the aim is not least to protect the public against all forms of fraud and to safeguard the currency. the increasing use of counterfeit euro coins in coin-operated machines has been noted and neither the legislation of the member states nor that of the community has been able to contain the problem to the extent necessary. the increase in the number of countries in which the euro is in circulation makes it all the more necessary and necessary to adopt measures in this respect. the proposal prohibits certain degrees of similarity between medals and coin counterparts resembling euro coins and lays down guidelines for the companies producing these medals and coin counterparts. representatives of the sector concerned have been thoroughly consulted and support the proposed legislation. the regulation is also intended to apply to those states which have signed agreements with the eu and use the euro, such as monaco, san marino and the vatican city state. i voted yes.
in writing. - (pt) i thank mrs maes for the report she has drawn up, which i support. it deals with a very important issue, namely the increase in the safety of third country aircraft using community airports. i therefore vote in favour of the joint text at third reading, a text which contains three elements which i consider very important: - the uniform application of inspection procedures throughout the eu, which prevents flights from third countries avoiding other eu airports with less demanding checks; - public access to information on airline compliance with safety rules; - the right of the european authorities to inspect an aircraft and impose a flight ban if it is suspected of not complying with safety rules.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) in its communication on aviation safety published last year, the commission expressed concern about the link between the increasing number of accidents and the increase in air traffic. the council had already tried to draw up a directive on this subject, but the long-standing conflict over gibraltar prevented it from achieving the desired result. the solution to this problem created the necessary conditions for taking an important step in this field. the commission thus took the initiative in the field of aviation safety and, in strict compliance with the safa procedure, sought to ensure systematic checks on aircraft suspected of posing a risk to aviation safety, on three crucial points: the targeted collection and dissemination of information, the checks on crews and third-country aircraft at community airports and the implementation of appropriate measures to correct the deficiencies identified, including flight bans if deemed necessary. in the light of recent tragic events, i believe it is essential to strengthen aviation safety, including through more effective and thorough checks on third country aircraft, which is why i voted in favour.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this report is part of the process of adapting the administration of the european parliament to the increase in the number of official languages which will take place as from 1 may, when the 10 countries of eastern europe and the mediterranean will join. it is claimed that this is to guarantee each member the same quality of service and to rationalise the operation of the european parliament by making the best use of the human and financial resources at its disposal, but it is a fact that the actual rights are being reduced, even if the rapporteur is trying to compensate in part for this. as we have already pointed out, the confirmation and practical implementation of the principle that all the languages of the eu countries should be official and working languages is all the more important in the current situation, where there is a tendency to see only certain languages becoming predominant in practice and to an increasing extent, namely the languages of the countries with the largest populations - the united kingdom, france, germany, spain and italy - to the detriment of the other languages of the countries that are part of the eu. this situation must be dealt with by constant effort.
in the light of the foregoing, i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. the proposed solutions are good, since the obligation to be multilingual as laid down in the treaties is confirmed, although it is provided that this obligation can only be 'bended' with the express or tacit consent of the members concerned (in the case of certain meetings of committees or delegations), namely in article 117 (3a): 'at meetings of committees and delegations outside the three usual places of work, interpretation is provided from and into the languages used by members who have confirmed that they will be present at the meeting. this arrangement may, with the agreement of the members of the body concerned, be relaxed in exceptional cases.' we can only accept the introduction of a transitional provision, which is temporary and expires in december 2006: 'in the application of article 117, exceptionally, as regards the official languages of the countries acceding to the european union on 1 may 2004, account shall be taken from that date until 31 december 2006 of whether there is in fact a sufficient number of corresponding interpreters and translators available.' for these reasons i voted in favour.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) in order to take account of the difficulties which enlargement may cause in recruiting a sufficient number of interpreters for certain languages, this report proposes an amendment to the rules of procedure of the european parliament as regards the existing multilingualism system. the obligation of multilingualism is thus confirmed as laid down in the treaties. it provides for the possibility of 'easing' this obligation with the express consent of the members concerned, and introduces a transitional arrangement for the new member states as long as there is a shortage of interpreters. it is a very sensitive area and no transitional arrangements were needed, since interpretation could well solve the problem. any temporary abolition of multilingualism is a future risk. i voted for the green amendments, which clearly limit the transitional provision, and against in the final vote.

in writing. - (pt) the argument put forward in the report's proposal to reject this regulation is very important because it can be used in other cases such as portugal, which has the largest exclusive economic zone of the community countries. the first argument concerns respect for the specific characteristics of the mediterranean fisheries and fleet, the socioeconomic structure, the species of fish and the size of the fish. the second concerns the need to involve fishermen in the decision-making process and to make use of their experience and efforts. the third is to strengthen dialogue and cooperation with the mediterranean third countries in order to involve them concretely in the efforts to ensure sustainable fisheries. the proposal for a regulation does not meet these conditions, which also, given that the mediterranean is an international sea, constitute good guidelines for the common fisheries policy. finally, there is the link between these conditions and the need for a thorough evaluation of the fish stocks and the measures to be taken to ensure their conservation, where the question of liberalizing access to them and the contradictions inherent in it are very similar to what is happening in portugal.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) as in other common policies, other areas and other member states of the union, the commission does not want to take into account the specificities of the different contexts in the common fisheries policy, and in the specific case of mediterranean fisheries. in the specific case of the mediterranean, the important role it plays in countless fields and the strategic importance which this sea has, has been given no importance at all, even though the european parliament has urged respect for the specific characteristics of the mediterranean and the development of flexible measures. the commission proposal for a regulation which is the subject of this report maintains a management strategy which is completely out of touch with the reality of the mediterranean and which does not contain a single measure to counter the catastrophic socioeconomic consequences which it will have. the rapporteur has therefore rightly suggested that this proposal for a regulation be rejected and that the commission be asked to submit a new proposal as soon as possible, taking account of the ideas and suggestions which may have emerged from a serious and thorough consultation of all the parties concerned. i fully agree with the rapporteur's views and have therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - (pt) the the rapporteur believes that this proposal, contrary to what was proposed in the green paper on the reform of the common fisheries policy, does not take due account of the specific features of the mediterranean. the proposal follows the approach which has characterized the measures implemented so far, but which have proved inadequate and which, in the light of the failed management policy, have made it clear that a change of course is needed in line with the guidelines set out in the green paper on the common fisheries policy. the rapporteur stresses the need to involve fishermen in order to ensure compliance with the rules, but points out that their experience and concerns have not been taken into account, pushing them to the limits of the law in a legal framework such as the one proposed. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fisheries sector is not left behind. i agree with the rapporteur and have voted against the proposal for a regulation and have supported the referral back to committee.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the report reaffirms a key principle which we have always advocated - good governance in the common fisheries policy - which 'implies the effective involvement of all operators in the fisheries sector in the decision-making process as part of the preparation and management of this policy' and 'this involvement should take place as early as possible in the decision-making process'. we have therefore always argued that the common fisheries policy should be decentralised. the commission's proposal to set up regional advisory councils is an important contribution in this direction. we broadly agree with this report, which improves on the commission's original proposals. the report stresses the importance of involving all the players in the sector, in particular fishermen employed and part-time fishermen and fishermen engaged in small-scale fishing within the 12-mile limit. the creation of subcommittees is another interesting proposal, as it will ensure direct participation at all levels. the report also seeks to make the financing of the expenditure of these councils more efficient and more effective. we are, however, reluctant to see these regional (and therefore supranational) councils transformed into councils with actual administrative powers, as this could endanger the national sovereignty of the member states.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) i have repeatedly expressed in the european parliament the view that fishermen and shipowners should play a greater role in the reform of the common fisheries policy, particularly when plans are being drawn up to restore species through the prohibition and limitation of fishing effort. it seems to me utopian to want to implement effective measures to conserve stocks without consulting the main players, since they are precisely those most affected by the decisions and policies of fisheries management. this is precisely the purpose of this initiative to set up regional advisory councils. while there is agreement that they should be set up, there are divergent views on their composition and financing. i believe that without a corresponding budget this measure loses all justification and that without a majority representation of the fisheries sector in the regional advisory councils the main players will not be able to secure their rights. only at the end of a transitional period should the composition and functioning of the regional advisory councils be reconsidered. if experience shows that these bodies are effective, they should be given a key role in the management of fisheries resources. finally, i would like to say that i do not agree with the geographical distribution of the regional advisory councils proposed by the commission, which divides the territory of the european union into only five regions. the portuguese waters around portugal proper and around the islands are thus included in the 'south-western area'.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the creation of regional advisory councils under the common fisheries policy aims - for the first time - to increase the involvement of fishermen and their organisations in the decision-making process behind the common fisheries policy. i thank the rapporteur for the excellent work he has done, expressing the legitimate expectations of fishermen that the establishment of these councils will not only create an ideal forum for fishermen and scientists to overcome their traditional differences of opinion on the situation of fishery resources. the sustainable management of fisheries resources, the social interests of the sector and the economic survival of coastal communities will depend to a large extent on the involvement of the various representatives of the sector in the formulation of the cfp. these regional advisory councils must therefore be guaranteed a transparent statute and a high degree of independence, perhaps in the form of a 'non-commercial body with its own legal status' registered in a member state, as the rapporteur proposes. it is therefore important that the commission accepts an increase in funding, which the committee and the rapporteur consider ridiculously low, so that the regional advisory councils can really function. these councils are an objective requirement for the european union, both because of the benefits their know-how will bring to the common fisheries policy and to the work of the commission, and because future problems can thus be better prevented.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the euro was created as a scriptural currency in the previous legislature, and in the current legislature it has become the currency of 12 of the countries of the european union. but the creation of the single currency does not imply the existence of a single payments area where the same rules apply. this is one of the major tasks to be carried out in the european union during the next legislature. the commission waited until the banking system became self-regulating following the creation of the single currency. but with the euro in place since 1999, what has happened is that there are two markets for payments: the domestic and the international. there was no internal market with domestic market rules governing payments in the new currency, which, while unique, functioned as a foreign currency with international transfer fees and charges. this situation was partially resolved by regulation no 2560 of december 2001 on electronic payments and transfers. from then on, it has once again been shown that self-regulation has not worked. the directive is also useless, because it needs to be transposed into the law of each country, which is not done at the same time or in the same way. this is a matter which requires secure rules, applied simultaneously and in the same way throughout the internal market, which is why i believe that only regulations can give citizens and businesses the security that a payment system requires.
in the tragedy caused by the sinking of the prestige, there is no doubt that the spanish authorities bear a great deal of responsibility. the report itself, although very insufficient in several areas, strongly criticises the spanish authorities, in particular for the statements of spanish officials and the lack of dissemination of the findings of the investigations. it is also positive that it stresses the need for greater attention to the maintenance and condition of ships, even those with double hulls, which may pose a greater potential danger; the defence of agreements with the imo to carry out rapid and independent investigations into maritime accidents; the request to the coastal member states to create a clear and independent command and decision-making structure in the context of emergency situations; the request for a study on the imposition of compulsory insurance; the request for financial compensation for shelters; the demand for a system of sanctions to counter illegal waste; an audit of classification societies; the transposition by the member states of community directives and the ratification of international conventions; the training of seafarers; the dignification of the maritime professions. however, unfortunately the report does not speak of improving the social conditions of workers and our proposals to ban flags of convenience, to hold all parties responsible for paying for damages and to support the investigation into the validity of the award of nautical certificates have been rejected. we hope that these proposals, which we have taken up again, will still be voted on in the plenary.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) this report follows on from the numerous amendments which parliament adopted at first reading and almost all of which have subsequently been accepted by the council. the common position shows that the solution proposed by the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism is indeed the most appropriate one to achieve the primary objective of interoperability between the various electronic toll systems in some member states. microwave pump systems are the most economically viable, they allow the use of technology already successfully used in the telephony sector, they fully meet the objectives of the directive and they actually make life easier for users of certain motorways. however, it should be stressed that the committee does not exclude a study at a later date, towards 2008, of the applicability of the satellite system, but everything will depend on the technological development on the market and specific needs in connection with other forms of road traffic monitoring. as this report does not change the text of the common position, which ensures compatibility between the different systems of the member states, i am voting in favour.
the amendments proposed to regulation (eec) no 2913/92 establishing a community customs code are designed to establish a harmonised legal framework for uniform customs controls in all member states and commonly agreed standards and risk criteria for the selection of goods and operators in order to combat terrorism, organised crime and the trade in dangerous products. in order to improve the security of the movement of goods across the external borders of the community, traders must provide customs authorities with information on the goods before importing into or exporting from the union. this information must be available in electronic form and must be exchanged between the authorities of the different member states. we would like to stress once again that the fight against terrorism must not be carried out at the expense of the fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens, including the right to privacy, which includes the protection of personal data, as stated in article 8 of the european convention on human rights. the protection of personal data should not be seen as an obstacle to the effective fight against terrorism, which is why we have some reservations about the proposed amendments to the regulation, even though the european parliament's amendments explicitly refer to these rights.
in the light of the above, the commission proposes to amend the community customs code by introducing basic principles for risk management at the external borders and a harmonised risk assessment system. the commission proposes a number of measures to improve the security of goods moving across international borders, including the following: introduction of a requirement for traders to provide customs authorities with information on goods before importing into or exporting from the eu. a more flexible system for the authorization of operators is introduced. a mechanism for the introduction of risk criteria applicable throughout the community is established. a computerised support system shall be established to support risk management. the proposal expresses a positive desire for an integrated and efficient management of the external borders by improving the efficiency of customs procedures and customs controls, partly by simplifying customs legislation and partly by making better use of information technology in customs procedures. i would like to emphasize that the parties concerned support changes which strike the right balance between the increased controls and formalities that security measures entail and the desire to make legal trade more flexible. i share that view and have voted in favour.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's air traffic control system is properly functioning. as in the case of other international organisations, the community and the member states participate in eurocontrol's work, in accordance with the protocol of accession, with voting rights allocated in accordance with their respective competences. the institutional synergy between the community and eurocontrol will certainly bring advantages in terms of capacity, safety and more efficient air traffic thanks to development programmes and the use of new air traffic control technology. as it is a question of establishing rules on international cooperation, the central aim of which is to achieve the objectives mentioned above, but taking into account the powers of the member states in this field, i have voted in favour of this report.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) since the treaty establishes a common transport policy, the commission has put forward a number of proposals for accession to international conventions in order to be able to exercise the powers conferred on it by the member states. this proposal is a follow-up to the initiative on the single european sky, in which the community is given an active role in the context of eurocontrol's technical powers. the protocol of accession contains the legal provisions enabling the community to become a full member of eurocontrol, with the community participating in its work together with the member states, but with a shared voting right. the voting rights are exercised by the community or by the member states, depending on whether the area in question falls within the competence of the community or within that of the member states. however, the fact is that the treaties do not confer on the community powers in the field of defence and national security, and therefore the use of airspace for military purposes does not fall within the community's competence, as we have pointed out in the debate on the single european sky. as always, we are trying to go along a path and at a pace that we are not prepared to follow.
in writing. - (pt) the proposal is for the european community to join the european organisation for the safety of air navigation (eurocontrol). articles 86 and 97 of the rules of procedure provide that parliament must give its assent to this agreement. the negotiations on the agreement were concluded on 8 october 2002 with the signing of the protocol thereto. as in the case of other international organisations, the community and the member states participate in eurocontrol's work, in accordance with the protocol of accession, with voting rights allocated in accordance with their respective competences. the council and parliament have recently adopted the regulation on a single european airspace, which among its provisions also provides for the community to join eurocontrol, and parliament has already expressed itself indirectly on this matter. cooperation between the community and eurocontrol could bring benefits in terms of capacity, safety and efficient air traffic thanks to development programmes and the use of new air traffic control technology, which is why i voted in favour.

in writing. - (pt) the the present proposal is part of a group of legislative initiatives to update and harmonise the rules on small cross-border traffic. in particular, it is intended to facilitate access to the eu for certain third-country nationals residing in border areas. the proposal aims in particular to remove barriers to crossborder workers by introducing a special visa for them. it is emphasized that this type of visa is of limited duration and that only citizens living within 50 km of the border should be able to benefit from these provisions. the amendments and comments made by the rapporteur are relevant, understandable and justified and do not go against the essence of the commission's proposal. i vote for it. however, it is appropriate to draw the attention of the commission to the abuses that could occur if the necessary measures are not taken, in particular to prevent abuses and vulnerabilities that could encourage illegal immigration and criminal activities and increase the risk of terrorist access.

in writing. - (pt) the this report concerns the revision of directive 87/102/eec on community provisions relating to consumer credit. the question is whether harmonized rules in this area will better protect consumers. on the one hand, the need to ensure greater security for intra-eu trade, for creditors, traders and consumers, makes such harmonization advisable, but on the other hand, complete harmonization could weaken the provisions in force in certain member states. it is therefore important that member states retain the right to ensure better protection for their consumers, including those states which believe that total harmonisation could be beneficial in certain areas. without going into detail, and although the report is the result of compromise negotiations in committee, it seems balanced, as it reflects our wish to impose responsibility on both creditors and consumers in a situation where marketing and consumer stimulation are enormously aggressive.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not affected by the effects of pesticides. they must therefore be reduced as much as possible, which is inseparable from the question of the agricultural practice - the agricultural model - used and the environmental risks associated with the use of pesticides, especially for soil and groundwater. the present proposal aims to consolidate and harmonise existing legislation in the field of pesticides and to harmonise standards in the various member states. the regulation sets maximum levels for pesticides in all products, empowers the commission to set import tolerances and gives the european food safety authority responsibility for risk assessment. despite the federalist mentality and the reservations it gives rise to, the views in principle seem to be correct, provided that the member states are still able to implement stricter measures on their own territory and that account is taken of national and regional specificities, in particular different climatic conditions and best available agricultural practices. in addition, we must be aware of the limit values, which should not be aimed at facilitating trade or compliance with wto rules, but should be determined by the health of consumers. it is therefore essential that imported products are subject to the same provisions.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the aim of this proposal for a regulation is to harmonise all the maximum levels at community level, to ensure a high level of consumer protection and to create the least possible barriers to trade. the proposal aims to simplify existing legislation and define the roles of the various parties, in particular the european food safety authority and the commission, in setting maximum levels. the european food safety authority, on the basis of its network of experts and institutions in the member states, will be responsible for the risk assessment and will be required to draw up an opinion on each mrl. the commission will be responsible for risk management and will decide on the setting of maximum levels on the basis of the opinions of the european food safety authority. member states' authorities shall ensure that the european food safety authority receives information on current food regulations, authorisations and agricultural practices. maximum residue limits (mrls) for existing or new substances not yet harmonised but previously established at national level are to be collected by the european food safety authority and set as provisional mrls once their safety has been established on the basis of available data. as it is important to ensure a high level of food safety and as i welcome the better distribution of roles and responsibilities, i have voted in favour.

mr president, the first question to be asked in this debate is whether the financial framework proposed by the commission is sufficient to guarantee economic and social cohesion, to guarantee the redistributive nature of the community budget and the commitments to the least developed countries in an enlarged european union of 27 member states, where community gdp will be reduced by more than 12% and economic, social and regional disparities are known to increase, as the third cohesion report shows. well, my answer is no. these prospects are clearly insufficient. just remember the past. the financial perspectives for 1988-92 and 1993-99 raised the own resources ceiling from 1.15% to 1.27% of the community's gross national product. in both cases the structural funds were doubled in the so-called 'delors i' and 'delors ii' packages. agenda 2000 retained the own resources and funds ceiling, even though it was already envisaged that six more countries would be included. in the present proposal, the commission maintains the limits of agenda 2000, even though the present enlargement involves ten countries plus two with average incomes below 40% of the community average. i am talking about the pressure and lack of solidarity on the part of the main net contributors to the six, who want to limit the budget to 1%. however, commissioner michaele schreyer recognises that this proposal - which is low - is only possible because of the process of budgetary consolidation in the current 15 member states: the stability pact and reallocation. but at the expense of what and at the expense of whom? this table shows the risks for both the countries that are about to join and for the cohesion countries, such as portugal, when it is known that the weight of the structural funds for the current member states will be reduced from 0.31% to 0.21% of community income. it was essential to change this situation, to raise the own resources ceiling, to respond to the serious problems of cohesion and poverty and also to defend greater economic and social cohesion among all the countries of the european union.

in the light of the above, the commission has decided to grant discharge to the european coal and steel community for the financial year ended 23 july 2002. we have no objection to that. the expiry of the ecsc treaty has automatically resulted in the disappearance of the legal order and procedures of the ecsc and the dissolution of the ecsc consultative committee set up by that treaty. in 2002, however, the ecsc continued to finance the retraining of workers within the budget with eur 35 million, research with eur 72 million and with an additional commitment of eur 21 million to the rechar programme for social measures in the coal industry. in view of the crisis in the coal and steel sector and the social and economic costs of the restructuring which has taken place in recent decades, the dismantling of the ecsc - despite the criticism which has been levelled at it - has left a gap to be filled, also at community level, which the new research fund for coal and steel cannot fill. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the point of this report is that the european coal and steel community (ecsc) has paid out some eur 800 million for applied research in enterprises and institutes alone without, as a rule, receiving its contractual share of the revenues obtained by these enterprises and institutes as a result of the patents made possible by the aid, as was expressly provided for in the ecsc research agreements. the commission must therefore maintain its legal right to share in the profits generated by the financing of research by means of a registration procedure and other appropriate measures. i also welcome the successful conclusion of the negotiations with the candidate countries on the terms of their participation in the new research fund for coal and steel, under which their contributions are determined on the basis of the extent of their underground resources and paid in instalments based on their respective economic situation. we agree with the rapporteur's views and have therefore voted in favour of the report. we can also join the rapporteur in praising all those who have created and developed the european coal and steel community and who have done a significant job in uniting europe.

in the light of the recent events, the commission has decided to withdraw its proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. the only thing that parliament has accepted is to obtain an opinion from the court of justice. the commission proposal and the subsequent proposal for a council decision will result in 'access by us law enforcement authorities to pnr databases located on eu territory', which will then result in 'the exercise of sovereign power by the us on eu territory' in eu countries. this agreement will 'leave us legislation in this area in force in the eu and for european citizens' and 'transfer to the eu the discretion of member states ... to authorise the use of information originally collected for commercial purposes for security purposes and to ... impose a legal obligation on european airlines to provide access to such information'. as regards the safeguarding of citizens' rights, freedoms and guarantees, 'the draft agreement does not define the scope and limits of these rights, but merely refers to a unilateral decision of the commission, which itself refers to some unilateral statements of the us government, which finally refers to current and future rules in the us'.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the schengen acquis provides that, for short stays, third-country nationals entering the territory of the member states who fulfil the necessary conditions for entry have the right to stay in the schengen area for a maximum period of three months from the date of first entry. it is therefore necessary to verify the dates on which a third-country national has crossed the external border in order to calculate the total period of stay and to verify whether he is legally present. the common manual on external borders provides for the stamping of travel documents and the relaxation of border controls in specific cases, mainly because of the congestion which occurs in such circumstances. the ambiguity of this provision has led to the adoption of different procedures in each member state, and this should be avoided. consequently, and in view of enlargement, we accepted mrs angelillis's view that this is a first step towards a final harmonisation of procedures, for example stamping the travel documents of third country nationals when they leave the schengen area.

in the light of the recent developments in the field of drugs, the commission has decided to launch a new action programme on drugs, which will be implemented by the european commission in the course of the year. it makes sense that the regulation establishing the emcdda should be recast for reasons of clarity and transparency, in particular to adapt it to the enlargement of the eu and to extend the mandate to cover the use of more substances, covering both legal and illegal substances. however, i cannot accept the attempt to impose assessment tasks on the emcdda. the purpose of the monitoring centre is not only to collect data but also to assess national policies and strategies and to assess trends in drug use. it would impose on an agency powers which member states currently have. the monitoring centre will be entrusted with the task of providing general information, i.e. collecting, analysing and disseminating information on all aspects of drugs and drug addiction, which will provide the eu and its member states with a comprehensive picture of drugs and drug addiction. this task should be without prejudice to the allocation of competences between the union and the member states with regard to the legal provisions on drug supply and demand.
the european union has always been a priority in the fight against drugs and drug abuse, and this has been reflected in its other policies, particularly in the last decade. the council therefore intends in its proposal for a regulation to take this fight to a new level. nevertheless, it has become clear that the many amendments scattered throughout the report are detrimental to this fundamental objective. while i agree that an extension of the powers of the monitoring centre seems to be a welcome measure, i cannot accept the amendments which seek to ensure that parliament is represented by two members of the board and that the number of evaluation tools is increased. the actions proposed in the report, and in particular those of the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, are not, in my view, the best strategy to follow. i could not vote for the report. i would suggest instead that the eu, the european observatory and also the member states join forces, either together or individually, not in the form of tasks that waste resources but in the form of measures that clearly lead to prevention. we need measures that effectively help to combat drug trafficking and abuse.
(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the 2002 discharge process was marked by the eurostat case and the commission's ongoing reform. we have serious reservations about both of these matters. despite recent scandals and in the light of the cases which led to the commission's fall in 1999, the administrative reforms announced seem to be almost exclusively cosmetic. the so-called administrative culture still needs to be changed, as the eurostat case shows. measures are needed to ensure that important information is not withheld. the commission should be given the opportunity to present its proposals to the council and to the european parliament, and to the council and to the european parliament. the eurostat case also highlights the need to review the chain of responsibility within the commission and the relationship between the various key players and commissioners. the report also confirms that it was a mistake to concentrate budgetary and accounting powers for the fight against fraud in the hands of a single commissioner. i would also like to say at sectoral level that i cannot support paragraph 115, which proposes a future european tax to replace national contributions from the member states to the eu budget, nor paragraph 182, which supports the n+2 rule for the structural funds.

theoretical tools such as those resulting from the lisbon strategy or from good practice in the coordination of economic policies. but we also have powerful limitations, such as those resulting from an overly rigid interpretation of the stability and growth pact, which undermine all the efforts made. the question is increasingly political, that is, a question of choice, and if it is true that there can be long-term sustainable economic development only with financial consolidation, it is also true that there will be no financial consolidation, even in the short term, without economic growth. europe needs a new agenda focused on the problems of the economy and employment, rather than the current agenda focused on the budget deficit and public spending, which have become a veritable obsession. europe does indeed need structural reforms, but it also needs the financial means to carry them out. and at an early stage, there will always be increased public spending or reduced tax revenue. this is only possible with a fundamental change in the existing budgetary rules. that is why the commission's announced proposals for the revision of the stability and growth pact are starting to be delayed, especially if these proposals focus on the essentials and do not merely sweeten the regulatory aspects of control. the reform of the cfp is inevitable, particularly as this instrument has been suspended since 25 november. it is no longer possible for the new rules to ignore the evolution of the economic cycle, to disregard the specificities of each member state without prejudice to the budgetary conciliation effort of the euro area as a whole. and above all, they ignore the role of public investment and quality spending in the development framework. the aim of zero budget deficits in the euro area in the long term is a total nonsense which no economic theory supports and which would be the absurdity of a public debt that, at the limit, would be equal to zero. i think these concerns are reflected in the excellent report by our colleague, mrs christa randzio-plath, whom i also warmly welcome, because my association with her over the last three years has shown me that she is a capable, competent, determined and profoundly european woman.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) while i agree with many of the points made in this annual report, i must stress that i believe it is being used once again as a political tool to protect countries considered to be 'friends' while criticizing others that the us or the eu designate as targets - a clear example of double standards. the report states that parliament is 'deeply concerned by the continuing conflict between palestine and israel'. although the israeli government and the palestinian people are held to be almost equally responsible - a position which i strongly oppose - the murders committed by israel and the ongoing israeli settlement activities, which involve allowing settlers to move illegally into the occupied territories, are condemned. there is a mild criticism of the continued expropriation of land for the construction of the so-called security fence. this is the very least we can do, given that the israeli government, with the complicity and support of the united states, is denying the most basic rights to the palestinian people, who are subjected to very brutal violence. the report does not say a word about the brutal attack and occupation of iraq by the united states.
in writing. - (pt) the this is a comprehensive annual report covering a number of subjects. it should be analysed carefully. the original version of the report focused on only three areas and contained some provisions which were completely irrelevant, particularly in relation to terrorism and so-called reproductive health. the rapporteur accepted a large number of amendments which led to this less unbalanced version. the various situations highlighted in the 'new' report are, however, almost all taken out of context. the document contains issues that do not fall within the traditional definition of 'human rights' - in fact, they go far beyond the original meaning. i voted against the report. i object to the way in which the report goes far beyond its scope. i cannot allow the eu to use this method - in its attempt to bring all other types of rights permanently under the umbrella of 'human rights' - to find an easy way to expand its possibilities for action. it is wrong for the eu to try to extend its powers by deliberately blurring definitions, which in turn makes it more difficult to ensure the effective protection of fundamental human rights. what we are witnessing is a clever move that will subtly pave the way for the eu to consider all sorts of different areas as 'human rights' and to intervene in all the areas it wants to.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) we voted against this report because parliament supports the monetary and budgetary orthodoxy - the neoliberal policies - in the eu's economic policy guidelines. the report continues to stress the structural reforms of the lisbon strategy, such as measures to make the labour market more flexible, i.e. to make workers more adaptable and to make the provisions of employment contracts more flexible, which have led to greater uncertainty in employment conditions. but that's not all. the report paves the way for the private sector to enter the pension and health sector at a time when more than 1.5 million workers in the eu have joined the ranks of the unemployed since 2001, when more and more businesses are closing down and others are moving out, and when the long-promised recovery is not coming. the right approach would be a policy of economic regeneration that could boost production and employment with the aim of promoting economic growth, employment and social and economic cohesion. the stability pact and the process of liberalisation and privatisation must be suspended immediately, we must combat the relocation of companies, promote productive investment and stop encouraging risky employment contracts such as short-term contracts. we were therefore very unhappy that our proposal was not included in the final decision.

in writing. the draft amending budget no 7/2004 aims to enter in the 2004 budget the balance of the 2003 financial year, amounting to €5.470 billion, the majority of which is due to under-implementation of expenditure on the structural funds. it is noted that the surplus would have been €10.5 billion in 2003 if €5 billion had not already been cut in amending budget no 6/2003. budget surpluses have been regular since 2000 - €12 billion in 2000, €15 billion in 2001 and €7 billion in 2002 - due to under-implementation of the structural funds. so if money for economic and social cohesion is a spending objective and vital for economic and social cohesion, the questions to be asked are: why is it not being implemented? because of the stability pact? because of a lack of political will? so there would seem to be justification for those who say that there is more money because it is not spent, and the budget should be kept below 1%, the structural funds should be reduced and even the cohesion policy should be renationalized, which is not acceptable. it is no coincidence that the main net contributors are among the worst performers. ... in writing. draft amending budget no 8/2004 concerns the revenue side of the budget and contains several elements affecting the level of member states' contributions to the communities' own resources, notably the correction of budgetary imbalances in favour of the united kingdom for 2000 and 2003 - the so-called 'british check'. although the rapporteur has not seen his demands in the report - from approval of the commission's proposals to the creation of a general mechanism for correcting imbalances in own resources - we must nevertheless reaffirm our firm opposition to the demands of the commission and the main net contributors, because one injustice cannot be corrected by another injustice. in practice, the proposals on the table are intended to apply a kind of new 'british cheque' to other net taxpayers, given that the 'british cheque' cannot be cancelled and the other member states will cover them. the correction of imbalances and injustices requires the approximation of per capita effort, taking account in particular of the relative prosperity of each country. the national contribution based on gnp will therefore be the fairest way, although it can be improved, to address the obvious imbalances in budgetary contributions.

marginalization to which khartoum has been voting, which since the 1980s has been inciting inter-ethnic conflict. we are dealing not with a government that is reluctant to take responsibility, but that the ceasefire be enforced and that the agreement in force be extended to all regions.
council. mr president, last saturday we commemorated the fact that the world suddenly changed three years ago. in this presentation, i would first like to look back and explain the basis for our policy, then address the current situation in the fight against terrorism before going into the work programme of the dutch presidency. i will end with a few words on cooperation with russia. since 11 september 2001, it has become clear that terrorist attacks are closer to us than we wanted to believe. it is a threat that we cannot neglect. we have all seen the horrific terrorist attacks on television. we are witnesses to these attacks and are also jointly responsible for ensuring that they do not happen again. what we have seen, both outside the european union – in jakarta, beslan, iraq, afghanistan and the middle east – and inside the european union – in madrid six months ago – requires action now and in the future. every attack poses new questions which require new answers and pose new challenges that we have to address jointly through concrete action. we need to protect our citizens better. we need to continue to look at our policy instruments in close cooperation with others. there are no quick fixes for terrorism. in the long battle against terrorism, two key words spring to mind: protection and cooperation, as well as the idea of protection through cooperation. on protection, the european union has done a lot in the last three years. we have improved our legislation and widened our policy instruments. we have drawn up and implemented new measures to protect borders, aircraft, etc. we have started to put security first, also at international level. on cooperation, the terrorist attacks have taught us that internal and external security cannot be separated: they are two sides of the same coin. there are two basic reasons for this: firstly, terrorism does not stop at borders and, secondly, terrorism is a global threat: it can happen – and indeed has happened – anywhere in the world. true protection can therefore be realised only through international cooperation. we also have to look carefully at whether our approach matches those of our partner countries in order to create sufficient possibilities for close cooperation. national and international action should be dovetailed for their mutual strengthening. terrorism is an attack not only on our political and economic freedom, but also on our norms and values: liberty, democracy, tolerance and the rule of law, values that we have to defend. terrorism is also not just an attack on western values, it is an attack on universal values which form the foundation for the united nations. the only way to defeat terrorism is to confront it. we must therefore be strong and active to fight this many-headed monster. there might be a temptation to believe that any measure could be used in this fight. but here, we have to be cautious. in our common fight, we should uphold the norms and values that terrorism is seeking to destroy. terrorism to a large extent boils down to security, which is the core of our existence. a new approach to security has been developed, through various processes, with a view to taking more conclusive action against terrorists and preventing new attacks. the un is at the core. un security council resolution 1373 has forced countries to improve their policies on terrorism, not only in word but also in deed, not only by improving old legislation or by drafting new legislation but also by implementing it. the resolution contains inter alia measures to combat the financing of terrorism and promotes efforts that should lead to the prevention of terrorism and the punishment of terrorists. the counter-terrorism agenda, incorporated in un security council resolution 1373, should therefore be considered to be the most important global point of reference for action – action that has to be taken by all united nations member states. within the european union, the european council and the general affairs council – as well as other council formations such as the justice and home affairs council, the transport council and ecofin – has actively worked, from 9/11 onwards, on setting up, implementing and refining an extensive eu action plan. amongst other things, this involved a european arrest warrant, joint investigation teams, eurojust and legislation on terrorist financing. we have also been active as regards external policy. the key issue of security is at the centre of the european security strategy, which should contribute to a stronger multilateral system. it should address various threats – including terrorism – through active, more coherent internal and external action, with stronger capacities and in close cooperation with our partners. we have also decided to include a terrorism clause in new contractual relations with third countries, similar to the human rights clause. this will allow us to hold serious consultations with third countries which are not fully observing their international obligations in the fight against terrorism, including with regard to the implementation of resolution 1373. by adopting the carrot-and-stick approach – carrots taking the form of assistance – we use the political and economic power of the european union in the fight against terrorism. i turn now to the presidency programme. the work programme of the netherlands presidency in the field of counter-terrorism is extensive and wide-ranging. in addition to a strong focus on implementation of eu measures and legislation, it entails new initiatives in many fields. an important tool in this matter is the eu counter-terrorism action plan. it was adopted by the european council after the horrendous attacks in madrid last march. the presidency works in close cooperation with the eu counter-terrorism coordinator, mr gijs de vries, to implement and complement this action plan. key areas in which we, as presidency, want to take substantial steps forward are justice and home affairs, improvement of cooperation between intelligence services, prevention of terrorist financing and strengthening of the eu's external policies and counter-terrorism. on justice and home affairs, we will focus on the implementation of measures like the european arrest warrant. we also need to improve the way our intelligence agencies work together. having good information on what terrorists are planning and preparing to do is our first line of defence. the eu action plan already outlines some of the steps that we intend to take and mr de vries is fully engaged in this process. we are in the process of strengthening the eu situation centre that will be instrumental in pooling analyses on terrorism in europe. we also need to strengthen the role of europol and make sure it can play its role. in the near future, the european union justice and home affairs ministers will sit with their us counterparts to see how we can strengthen transatlantic cooperation in the fight against terrorism. the prevention of terrorist financing is high on our agenda. even though the eu is at the forefront of the fight against terrorism, we cannot sit back and relax. money is the life-blood of terrorism and we need to reinforce our financial systems to make sure that they are not abused by terrorists. the third money laundering directive is a fresh step in this matter. we also need to strengthen our policies to freeze assets of terrorists. we therefore seek to make the eu clearing house more effective and to secure better implementation. finally, we will be looking at ways to prevent cash couriers from circumventing banking regulations by taking their money in cash across borders. in our external policies we want to make sure that the resources of the union are being used to their full extent in order to work with other countries in the fight against terrorism. as i have already said, terrorism is a phenomenon that does not respect international borders. it is our firm belief that we must work with third countries to promote the ratification and implementation of un counter-terrorism conventions and to use political dialogue and technical assistance to support countries willing to cooperate. the eu is already active in indonesia, the philippines and pakistan, where it is implementing specific programmes. the eu also operates other programmes in various countries with a view, more generally, to strengthening their judicial systems. we feel that the eu should do more and therefore we are talking to a number of key countries to explore how we can enhance our cooperation. that brings me to terrorism in russia. russia is very worried about the threat of terrorism, and rightly so. but, more than a mere worry, this is a true problem for russia, which has suffered three major attacks in little more than a week. we must show – and indeed have shown – our sympathy. it is clear that the european union has always systematically condemned all acts of terrorism. the russians deserve all the support we can give them. hence we stand by russia to assist it in its efforts to fight terrorism. in our relations with russia, we already discuss counter-terrorism on a regular basis. we stand ready to increase cooperation on a technical level and to share the counter-terrorism experience that we have gained in the eu. we will use the regular dialogues that we have with russia to discuss how to proceed in this matter. we are willing to discuss anti-terrorism strategies and methods with the russians so that we can learn from each other. this cooperation forms part of our overall strategy to strengthen relations between the european union and russia. it is part of our goal to make tangible progress on all four common spaces at the next summit on 11 november. in the field of external security, we have made progress. but the interaction should go hand-in-hand with building up cooperation in the common space of internal security. the terrorist attacks have prompted moscow to continue to regard chechnya as a predominantly anti-terrorist issue. this gives rise to concern. we have been consistent in our position that human rights should be respected in the fight against terrorism. indeed, the european union has a clear position on the situation in chechnya. we will continue to present this position to russia in future. as to the terrorist attack in beslan, i will be brief. we have fully and unconditionally condemned this attack and have offered our condolences to the relatives of the victims, the russian government and the russian people. we therefore fully supported your initiative, mr president, for schools all over europe to respect a one-minute silence at noon yesterday in commemoration of the victims of this terrorist attack. in that way our children were able to show the world their grief for its victims and their worries about terrorism. it is now up to us, the politicians, to translate these worries into further concrete action and to reinvigorate our fight against terrorism while respecting our core values. (applause)
commission. mr president, let me begin where the foreign minister of the netherlands concluded and make it clear that no-one possessed of any shred of humanity could be other than appalled and deeply saddened by the tragic events at the school in beslan in north ossetia two weeks ago. i reiterate the commission’s condolences to the people of beslan. i also unhesitatingly and unreservedly condemn terrorist acts wherever they are perpetrated. attacks on civilians are always contemptible. when they deliberately target children, they plumb new depths of atrocity. sadly, this event, as the presidency noted, was not isolated. in recent months, russia has suffered several terrorist attacks, with targets ranging from the moscow metro to domestic passenger flights. the sequence is deeply disturbing, and the commission has of course expressed its readiness to intensify our work with russia to combat the very real terrorist threats that it faces. we are, to take one example, already working with russia to combat the financing of terrorism, by helping russia to improve its efforts to tackle money laundering. we want ideally to pursue those efforts as part of our much-vaunted 'strategic partnership' with russia, as part of a process of dialogue. dialogue inevitably involves questions. real help comes only with understanding, and understanding comes only with clarity. what happened in beslan is still not fully clear, at least to the outside observer. who were those involved? how did the hostage-takers plan and execute this horrific act? what provoked the storming of the school? why was the number of casualties so high? however, the link with chechnya is clear. events in beslan followed an intensification of rebel attacks in both chechnya and ingushetia since the spring. the current conflict, now in its fifth year, has been a vicious affair, with widespread human rights abuses and the targeting of civilians by both russian armed forces and rebels. many civilians have simply disappeared. the conflict has caused a massive humanitarian crisis and has laid the economy waste. we should all recognise, however, that this is not the time to read russia lectures about chechnya. this is a time of grief and shock. we have had, and will continue to have, our differences with russia over chechnya. we have made, and will continue to make, those differences clear in our meetings with the russians, and to discuss them. that is what partners do. for the commission, there are two principles that guide cooperation with russia on terrorism. first, it is equally – if not more – important to work together to prevent terrorism, by which i mean addressing its root causes. second - and i strongly endorse what the foreign minister has just said - human rights are paramount and must be respected. the fight against terrorism does not justify or excuse the violation of human rights. rather, it is strengthened by a demonstrable respect for the human rights of all citizens. i noted a remarkable statement the other day by the chief justice of the supreme court in israel. he was giving a judgment on the security barrier. what he said reminded me of what we share fundamentally with israel, whatever our criticisms of the present government’s policies. democracies, he argued, have to fight with one hand tied behind their backs. that is true. but it is also true that the moment you behave like the terrorists, you undermine your moral authority and you augment the number of citizens who either actively or passively support them. so when we return to discussion of chechnya, we should continue to make clear our support for a political solution to the conflict, which fully respects russia's territorial integrity. but we should do so in a consistent, intelligent way that does not risk changing from presidency to presidency, and that recognises the complex nature of ethnic conflict in the whole of the caucasus. i note in passing that we and our russian partners need urgently to come to a shared understanding of this point. territorial integrity and stability matter throughout russia’s near abroad, in the southern caucasus as much as the northern caucasus. they matter in the near abroad as well as within russia itself. a shared recognition of that would do much to make our common neighbourhood a safer place. for our part we should recognise that no-one sensible in russia could or should want to return to the chechnyan status quo of the years immediately before 1999. they remember what that was like, and what it led to. so should we. it was appalling – a community that exported gangsterism. so the commission welcomes efforts to rebuild properly functioning public health, education and administrative systems, but we have no illusions. this is the start of a very long journey, which will only be lengthened by the siphoning off of reconstruction funds by corrupt officials, by the apparent manipulation of elections and by a failure to protect human rights and the absence of dialogue. the challenge for russia is to put in place a leadership in chechnya in which the population of chechnya has confidence. without this, there can be no lasting, genuine reconciliation, which it is clear the majority of the population wishes to see. we can help in this, in a modest way, supporting efforts to promote reconstruction and institution-building in chechnya. i repeat the commission’s readiness to provide funds for reconstruction and rehabilitation in the north caucasus, as soon as the security situation permits, and once a needs assessment mission to moscow and the north caucasus can be undertaken. but ultimately that, and any lasting resolution of the chechnyan tragedy, depend on the pursuit of far-sighted, humane and resolute policies in moscow. i hope they are forthcoming and that the government of the russian federation will not conclude that the only answer to terrorism is to increase the power of the kremlin. frankly, there is not much good history on the side of that proposition. (applause)
mr president, it is always easier to speak when we can show our agreement with the previous speakers, in this case the presidency and the commission. almost everything has been said about terrorism. after 9/11, and march 11, and now the tragedy of beslam. and it's not just about terrorism anymore, it's about a new situation that i would call hyperterrorism, where not only civilians, but children in writing. i voted in favour of setting up a temporary committee on the political challenges and budgetary resources of the enlarged union for 2007-13 because i think it is essential to follow this process closely, to collect and coordinate the views of the different budget lines which will be evaluated in this parliament through its various parliamentary committees. the political priorities of the european parliament in this negotiation must be in line with the structure of the new financial perspective. i think it is essential that parliament's final position be incorporated into the council's common position so that negotiations can begin on a plan of understanding of the european project for the near future. i believe that this process must be based on internal consistency, which includes all the institutional elements, and that every effort must be made not only to ensure the smooth running of the negotiations but above all to promote the objectives of the lisbon strategy and a vigorous policy of economic and social cohesion which will continue to allow the convergence of the levels of well-being of the populations of the various member states.
