in writing. i voted in favour of the establishment in the european parliament of this temporary committee on the political challenges and budgetary resources of the european union. i believe that the group and conference of presidents' approach was well informed, since they considered that the importance of this historic moment and its practical implications for a europe of over 450 million citizens justified this specific committee. this methodology should allow the views of the different parliamentary committees involved to be gathered, weighted and coordinated, thus contributing to a more precise definition of the political priorities of the european parliament, to be reflected in the future financial perspectives. this should not weaken the positions already adopted by the european parliament, which are clearly opposed to reducing the union's resources or abandoning or simply weakening the objectives and policies of cohesion. it is not a question, in my view, of defining a new starting point. on the contrary, this temporary committee should at least adopt the european commission's proposal on the financial perspective and seek to set more ambitious targets for the eu's budgetary resources and at an accelerated pace for the cohesion objectives. this is the challenge in the era of enlargement and the new constitutional treaty.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr philippe morillon on the proposal for a council regulation on the conclusion of the protocol setting out, for the period from 3 december 2003 to 2 december 2007, the fishing opportunities and financial compensation provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the government of mauritius on fishing off mauritius, because i believe it is essential that the protection of the european union's interests in fisheries should be coordinated with the management of marine resources and the development of the populations dependent on this activity. a proper assessment of the sustainability of the fisheries agreements concluded by the european union with third countries is essential, as specific measures are becoming increasingly important for the proper implementation of community actions in the development of local populations, especially coastal communities that depend on traditional fishing. community shipowners will also be protected by the introduction of measures to impose greater control of fishing activities in order to combat illegal fishing and to contribute to the exercise of responsible fishing in the indian ocean.
in writing. the guarantee of fishing opportunities for community fleets, particularly the portuguese fleet, in the exclusive economic zones of third countries is of the utmost importance, not only for the economy and the maintenance of employment, but also for the survival of the many regions in the european union which depend on fishing, particularly the outermost regions. the possibilities have been reduced and the cost of licences has been increased, which, linked to a common fisheries policy that rewards the killing of boats and will no longer give aid to the renewal of the fleet, of which the portuguese government has been an "exemplary" student, explains why much of the portuguese long-distance fishing fleet has been disappearing. we also do not think that the amendments which seek to pass on the cost of the agreements to the shipowners make sense. these trade-based agreements can also contribute to the sustainable management of fisheries resources and to the development of local fishing communities. this fisheries protocol, which will last until 2 december 2007, will allow the seven portuguese surface longliners to continue operating as they are registered.
in writing. the agreement is the conclusion of a new fisheries agreement between the european union and a number of countries in the indian ocean, in this case mauritius, which will continue, with the necessary adjustments, the successive agreements concluded in this field since 1989. although the agreement is relatively modest in financial terms and concerns only tuna, the highly migratory nature of the species in question underlines the importance of this agreement for community shipowners. in addition, it also makes economic sense as the value of the catches is far higher than the costs of the agreement to the union. i also think that the side benefits of the agreement, such as job creation in fishing vessels, ports, shipyards, processing plants, shipyards and service companies both in the european union and on the islands themselves, are also beneficial. i also have in mind that 7 of the 90 community vessels in mauritius' waters are portuguese vessels, and i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the amendments suggested by the rapporteur add value to the proposal for a regulation in question.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr philippe morillon on the proposal for a council regulation on the conclusion of the protocol setting out, for the period 1 january 2004 to 31 december 2006, the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the democratic republic of madagascar on fishing off madagascar, because i am in favour of responsible and sustainable fishing. this protocol lays down the definitions of the fishing opportunities for the community tuna fleet. in the same vein, the protocol makes it possible to promote cooperation relations based on respect for the legislative and regulatory provisions of madagascar's national fisheries policy. this new protocol represents an overall cost identical to that of the previous protocol. the agreement is of crucial importance to the malagasy economy as it is an important source of foreign exchange and creates jobs for local seafarers as well as for the processing and surveillance sector.
in writing. this eighth protocol to the fisheries agreement with the democratic republic of madagascar will last until the end of 2006 and is limited to defining fishing opportunities for the community tuna fleets - which include six portuguese surface longliners - in line with the other tuna agreements concluded by the community with the countries of the indian ocean, which in general deserves our agreement. however, one issue which raises considerable doubts is the so-called exclusivity clause, which implies that vessels flying the flag of a member state cannot obtain any licence except through this protocol. this means in practice that other bilateral agreements are prohibited, which seems to us to be excessive and represents an interference in the internal politics of each member state, especially when there are traditional and historical relations which are not guaranteed by the community agreement.
in writing. the agreement, which is exclusively for tuna fishing, is one of a number of agreements concluded by the union with countries in the indian ocean, allowing the european fishing fleet to continue operating in madagascar's waters. i believe that the european union's fisheries policy should bear in mind the need for transparency, which is particularly important in agreements of this kind, which are not limited to european interests. the development of the malagasy economy, respect for the environment and the sustainability of the fishing effort in madagascar's territorial waters are three aspects which cannot be ignored in this protocol. i agree with the rapporteur's concern that the malagasy government should take measures to ensure better control of fishing activities, otherwise the balance of resources would be jeopardized, and with his view that coastal populations should be the real beneficiaries of this protocol. so i voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation on the conclusion of the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters concerning the extension for the period 1 july 2004 to 30 june 2005 of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the republic of cape verde on fishing off cape verde, in view of the mutual benefits for the community and cape verde of the conclusion of this agreement. we see this extension as an attempt to improve some aspects of this agreement, given the lack of any reliable study by the authorities of this country of official portuguese expression on the situation of resources and the impact of specific measures on the development of the cape verdean fisheries sector, a situation which must be remedied urgently for the benefit of cape verde and its fishermen.
in writing. this report deserves our approval, given its socioeconomic importance for the republic of cape verde and for the states whose fleets are involved - the spanish, portuguese and french fleets - in total 117 vessels, mainly dedicated to tuna fishing, but also to some demersal species. the extension of the current fisheries agreement for another year - until 30 june 2005 - will allow the owners of community fleets to continue their fishing activities in the exclusive economic zone of the republic of cape verde, in particular the two portuguese tuna seiners and the 10 portuguese surface longliners. in addition, the portuguese fleet may fish up to 630 grt per month in the bottom longliner fishery. fishing opportunities which, however, seem small in view of portugal's traditional and historical relations with cape verde, but are also a reflection of the fisheries policy of a cfp which has gradually contributed to the destruction of long-distance fishing fleets such as the portuguese fleet.
in writing. the agreement extends for the period 1 july 2004 to 30 june 2005 a fisheries agreement between the eu and the republic of cape verde, which mainly concerns tuna and is designed to allow community vessel owners to continue fishing activities in the cape verdean exclusive economic zone (eez). in fact, in anticipation of the continuation of these relations with cape verde and, in particular, the conclusion of a new agreement for the coming years, the commission considers it necessary to carry out an in-depth assessment of the agreement currently in force. like the rapporteur, i think you are warned and welcome this commitment by the commission. given the advantages for community shipowners, the much higher value of the catches compared to the costs of the agreement, the mutual benefits for the eu and cape verde and the usefulness of the catches for supplying the community market, i cannot but welcome the conclusion of this agreement, enriched by the amendments proposed by the rapporteur. i voted yes.

commission. mr president, the commission has been following developments in this situation. according to the information available to the commission, 'women on waves', together with other persons and organisations, appealed against the refusal of entry of the vessel into portugal. on 6 september 2004 the administrative and fiscal court of coimbra adopted a decision on the appeal which has been the subject of a further appeal by 'women on waves'. the commission would recall the principles of community law in connection with the free movement of persons. european citizens are entitled to have access to the territory of other member states in accordance with the various rights to freedom recognised by the ec treaty, subject to the conditions and limitations provided for by that treaty and its implementing provisions. member states can restrict this fundamental right enshrined by article 18 of the ec treaty solely when this is justified on grounds of public policy, public security or public health. where a member state adopts a measure refusing entry to its territory based on one of these grounds, it must respect the general principles of community law. it must respect fundamental rights, including the right to freedom of expression, and in particular the proportionality principle, as well as the provisions of council directive 64/221/eec of 25 february 1964 on the coordination of special measures justified on grounds of public policy, public security and public health, as interpreted by the court of justice of the european communities. when decisions are taken on grounds of public policy or public security, the conduct of the persons in question must pose a real and sufficiently serious threat to the fundamental interests of society. only the diseases or disabilities referred to in the annex to directive 64/221/eec can justify refusals to enter member states on grounds of public health. under directive 64/221/eec, decisions refusing entry or ordering expulsion from the territory must be notified to the person concerned, informing him or her of the grounds of public policy, public security or public health upon which the decision has been taken. the person concerned must be able to lodge a complaint against this decision. it is for the portuguese national courts to rule on the validity of the decision, while respecting the general principles of community law and the provisions of directive 64/221/eec. the commission has not yet received a complaint about this incident from the representatives of the 'women on waves' organisation. however, it intends to contact the portuguese authorities to obtain more detailed information on the facts related by the honourable members. in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1268/1999 on community support for preaccession measures in the field of agriculture and rural development in the applicant countries of central and eastern europe during the preaccession period. the proposed amendments seek to harmonise certain provisions applicable to the new member states by including a new eligible measure enabling rural communities in bulgaria and romania to prepare and implement local rural development strategies, adapting the aid intensity to levels similar to those granted to the countries acceding to the european union in 2004 and finally providing clarification on the limits of the aid rates. in my view, the proposals for revision in question, which are based on extensive experience, meet the objective of ensuring greater effectiveness in the monitoring of community support, which is of the utmost importance in the context of preparing the entry of future member states.
in writing. the experience of successive enlargements of the european communities shows that rural communities are particularly vulnerable to change and integration into more dynamic and competitive economic spaces and rural development strategies need to be designed and implemented to take account of this particular circumstance. in view of this, which is still evident in my own country, i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on community support for pre-accession measures in the field of agriculture and rural development in the applicant countries of central and eastern europe. in this context, and in view of the future accession of bulgaria and romania, i believe that the union has done well in harmonizing the measures to be applied in these countries with those of those which joined the union on 1 may last.
in writing. the commission proposes to give the european parliament and the council the satisfaction they desired by presenting an evaluation report on the application of regulations (ec) nos 2702/1999 and 2826/2000 on information and promotion measures for agricultural products in third countries and on the internal market. the commission is also proposing a number of regulatory amendments which give rise to reservations. these information and promotion measures, which are complementary to national and private measures, are of the utmost importance, particularly for countries such as portugal, which have high-quality agricultural products with added value, such as cheeses, spirits, fruit and olive oil. these measures are all the more necessary when the liberalisation of agricultural trade is being stepped up worldwide. however, the community budget in this area has been reduced over the last two years from €72 million to less than €60 million. this is in addition to a low execution rate, which in 2003 was less than 44%. the reasons are simple: low community co-financing (maximum 50%), the complexity and administrative costs of managing these programmes and a limited list of products covered. the reasons for this are particularly painful for countries such as portugal. the proposed amendments, while allowing for some flexibility, do not provide an effective response to implementation problems or increase existing appropriations.
in writing. i voted in favour of report a6-0008/2004 because i believe that the european union's actions should aim at increasingly effective promotion of european products, while respecting the diversity of european products in terms of production conditions, processing methods, preservation and use. the european union has been implementing and co-financing activities to promote agricultural products through a coherent policy, organised in two regulations: one on promotion in third countries and the other on promotion in the internal market. community policy must add value to national and private initiatives by reinforcing or stimulating the promotion activities of the member states and private enterprises. the need for an active promotion policy is recognized by our major trading partners who have adopted effective promotion policies, with sufficient financial support, to maintain or increase their respective shares in the world market. it is essential that the european union plays a visible and effective role in promoting exports.
in writing. the unanimity achieved in the agri committee demonstrates the consensual way in which the question of information and promotion of agricultural products both in third countries and on the internal market is assessed by this house. in view of the trend towards globalisation of trade, the illegitimate appropriation of designations of origin belonging to european quality products and unfair competition based on cheap labour, this internal and external commitment to the promotion of agricultural products is particularly relevant. i believe that this unusual competitive situation fully justifies the maintenance of community intervention, in a framework of promoting the 'visibility of the intrinsic characteristics and common qualities of european products, while respecting the diversity of these products as regards production conditions, processing methods, preservation and use'. so i voted in favour.
i abstained on this vote because i believe that the process of ratification of the constitutional treaty, which i hope will take place in full, is an eminently sovereign moment for the member states, indeed the most sovereign moment for the member states, since it is on these occasions that decisions are taken which affect their own sovereignty. the european parliament must therefore resist the temptation to express its intention to intervene in the way in which the member states, by virtue of being and necessarily being democracies, carry out this process. i do not think that the council should be asked to define coordinated approaches to the timing of national ratification procedures or to encourage parliamentary control and campaigning practices for the referendums that may take place, or even worse, to issue warnings of any kind, as one of the amendments suggested. as regards the question of the communication strategy, i believe, as stated in recital c of the resolution adopted, that the constitution should be presented to the european citizens of the union in the clearest and most comprehensible way possible, and that the union will therefore finance genuine initiatives for objective, factual, fair and independent information. the peoples, the national parliaments and their representatives will then decide by voting. i thank you very much, mr president, for your attention.
in writing. when such important questions for the future of peoples and states are being debated, it is not right to try to impose the coordination of ratification processes, with a common timetable and strategy, much less to establish guidelines for the dissemination of the content, with the aim of influencing public opinion in accordance with the objective that the majority wants: to approve the draft constitutional treaty. what is required is respect for the national procedures for ratifying the draft treaty establishing a constitution for europe and the right of the different political forces to consider the important and serious political and constitutional consequences for the member states and their citizens. it is up to the citizens of the member states or their representatives in the national parliaments to accept or reject this draft treaty. it is therefore unacceptable that more money should be allocated to a propaganda campaign on the european constitution with a view to its adoption. what is needed is a pluralistic debate in which all political forces can participate on an equal footing.
in writing. the draft treaty establishing a constitution for europe deserves to be known not only by legal scholars but by all european citizens, whatever their views on it. and of course the best way to involve citizens in this process will be through referendums that motivate campaigns that are enlightening, fair and balanced. i would also stress that there will be no european dimension in this process if it chooses to ignore the national dimension of each member state. and finally, i firmly believe that we all have to show confidence in democracy and the sovereign will of the people, by turning away any sick climate of false drama, to the way of coercion the absurd propaganda of an 'end of europe' in the event of a setback distorts the debate, divides us on the essential points and seriously undermines the serious discussion on the construction of europe. in the face of the very low turnout in the european elections, the only real tragedy would be if public opinion were to drift apart again or if the campaigns conducted in this regard by the european institutions reflected and aggravated rather than combated the much-lauded european democratic deficit. the rejection of amendments 3 and 13, which only required freedom and equality in debate, makes one fear the worst. that is why i voted against the resolution.
in writing. a few days before the european council on 5 november, a major struggle was waged in the european parliament in defence of the freedoms, justice and rights of individuals, especially immigrants. our group has sought to improve the bourlanges report, whether by restoring a balance between the requirements of security and the need to respect fundamental rights in favour of these, or by refusing to resort to european charters and to the mass expulsions of immigrants. it is true that some of our views were approved during the vote, but the majority were rejected, so we still have a very weak report and positions with which we disagree in important areas. i would, however, stress the importance of the adoption of the following amendments: - recognition that immigrants cannot be regarded as temporary labour but are essential to the future of our society; - stresses the importance of the decisions and the framework decision on the protection of the rights of migrant workers and members of their families, adopted by the united nations general assembly on 18 december 1990;- acknowledges the bad experience of refugee camps even on the territory of the member states of the european union. unfortunately, many others were not adopted, so i could not vote in favour of the report.

the price of a barrel of oil has crossed the psychological threshold of $50 dollars. despite the fluctuations, the trend is upwards. this increase is the result of a complex combination of factors, such as the invasion and occupation of iraq, political and social instability in some major producing countries, natural disasters, increased demand in countries with large populations and high economic growth, and also speculation. the imf points out that a $8/barrel increase will cause a 0.5% drop in economic growth, so even if the intensity of the shock is less than in the 1970s and 1980s, the risks to the world economy and its expected recovery are enormous. the first sectors to suffer from these increases in diesel are transport, fisheries and agriculture. the sectors, particularly the latter, are already in deep crisis. where not only should there be no, or be no, community restrictions on direct public aid to the sectors concerned, but concrete measures and support should be taken at eu level to minimise the socioeconomic impact of the increase in oil prices. however, the central issue is much broader and structural, and results from the unresolved problem of the world economy's energy dependence on a finite resource and a source of speculation.

in writing. i voted in favour of the giuseppe gargani report (a6-0012/2004) - dangerous substances discharged into the aquatic environment of the community on a proposal for a european parliament and council directive on pollution caused by certain dangerous substances discharged into the aquatic environment of the community. i consider the work undertaken by the commission to simplify and clarify community legislation to be fundamental. i also consider this work to be of great value because it preserves the content of the codified acts in their entirety by merely assembling them. it is essential to make community legislation more accessible and easier for the ordinary citizen to understand, which will open up new opportunities for him and enable him to benefit from the specific rights conferred on him.
in writing. i share the european commission's concern that, in order to make the european union more accessible to citizens, it is of the utmost importance to simplify community legislation. i believe that this will help ordinary citizens to become better acquainted with their duties and, respectively, with the rights conferred on them. the dispersion of community provisions, many of which have been subject to successive amendments over the years, makes it very difficult to identify the rules in force and requires considerable analytical work, which is practically only accessible to those with a legal background. for these reasons, and in order to ensure the clarity and transparency of community legislation, it seems to me that, as defined in 1987 by the european commission and in 1992 by the edinburgh european council, it is essential to codify community rules. i therefore support the aim of this proposal, which is to codify council directive 76/464/eec of 4 may 1976 on pollution caused by certain dangerous substances discharged into the aquatic environment of the community, replacing the previous legislative acts.
in writing. i voted in favour of the giuseppe gargani report (a6-0011/2004) - control of certain diseases in bivalve molluscs on a proposal for a council directive establishing minimum community measures for the control of certain diseases in bivalve molluscs (codified version). i consider the work undertaken by the commission to simplify and clarify community legislation to be fundamental. i also consider this work to be of great value because it preserves the content of the codified acts in their entirety by merely assembling them. the purpose of this proposal is to codify council directive 95/70/ec of 22 december 1995 laying down minimum community measures for the control of certain diseases in bivalve molluscs. the new directive will replace the various acts incorporated in it. it is essential to make community legislation more accessible and easier for the ordinary citizen to understand, which will open up new opportunities for him and enable him to benefit from the specific rights conferred on him.
in writing. i reiterate the conviction expressed by the european commission that the simplification of community legislation will lead to a european union that is more accessible to citizens who are more aware of their duties and rights. the dispersion of community provisions, many of which have been subject to successive amendments over the years, makes it very difficult to identify the rules in force and requires considerable analytical work, which is practically only accessible to persons with a legal background. for these reasons, and in order to ensure the clarity and transparency of community legislation, it seems to me that, as defined in 1987 by the european commission and in 1992 by the edinburgh european council, it is essential to codify community rules, i therefore support the aim of this proposal, as i did with directive 76/464/eec, which is to codify council directive 95/70/ec of 22 december 1995 laying down minimum community measures for the control of certain diseases in bivalve molluscs, replacing the acts incorporated into it, which are currently separate pieces of legislation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the elmar brok report (a6-0023/2004) - partnership and cooperation agreements on the proposals for council and commission decisions on the conclusion of protocols to the partnership and cooperation agreements between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and armenia, azerbaijan, georgia, kazakhstan, kyrgyzstan, moldova, russia, ukraine, uzbekistan, of the other part, to take account of the accession of the czech republic, the republic of estonia, the republic of cyprus, the republic of latvia, the republic of lithuania, the republic of hungary, the republic of malta, the republic of poland, the republic of slovenia and the slovak republic to the european union. these partnership and cooperation agreements (pcas) are 'mixed' agreements which entered into force before the last enlargement of the union and which therefore require a protocol to be added to that agreement allowing the accession of the 10 new member states to the agreement. the council authorized the commission to open negotiations, on behalf of the community and its member states, with these countries with a view to concluding protocols to the partnership and cooperation agreements.

in writing. i voted in favour of the luisa morgantini report (a6-0018/2004) - aid to uprooted people in developing countries in latin america and asia on a proposal for a european parliament and council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 2130/2001 on action in the field of aid to uprooted people in developing countries in latin america and asia. i believe that the work done by the european community in helping the uprooted populations in the developing countries of latin america and asia is fundamental. regulation (ec) no 2130/2001 of 29 october 2001 provides for aid to some of the most vulnerable groups in the world those forced to leave their homes as a result of armed conflict. this regulation expires on 31 december 2004. the regulation provides that its extension is conditional on the possibility of 'integrating this single framework regulation for asia and latin america'. this inconvenience can be avoided by reducing the period of validity to two years, namely 2005 and 2006. i consider this amendment essential for the continuation of the community's work with these populations.
in writing. i welcome the support shown by the deve parliamentary committee to the european commission proposal to extend the application of the existing regulation on uprooted populations (refugees, displaced persons who have been forced to seek refuge outside their region of origin, and former refugees or displaced persons) and 'demobilized former combatants'. this instrument, which forms part of the wider policy of development assistance and aid of the european union, is of the utmost importance and is often the only and last hope of thousands of people in particularly precarious situations. i also welcome the trend in recent years of gradual increases in appropriations. experience shows that such actions play an important role in preventing conflict or in reconciling the parties to a conflict, or in helping uprooted populations or demobilised former combatants to regain their property and property rights, often providing the last hope for a new beginning.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i believe, as it says, that after five years, the emu project can still be considered a great success thanks in large measure to the work of the ecb and the european monetary institute that preceded it. and it should also be recognised because of the commitment of member states, particularly member states like portugal, which have made a worthwhile effort to comply with the stability and growth pact. on the other hand, and in line with what is said in the report, i recognize that the weaknesses of the european economy are not linked to its monetary policy but mainly to the lack of structural reforms in the direction of greater international and global competitiveness.
in writing. the present report, reinforced by the final version rejected by the rapporteur, makes emu a 'success story' and unconditionally supports the monetary orthodoxy applied by the ecb, and that is not the story of reality as we interpret it. so we reject it. success in macroeconomic stability is achieved when it is proven that recent years have been marked by weak economic and employment growth, by the shifting of productivity gains from workers to employers; when high levels of unemployment, poverty, social exclusion and income inequality persist within the eu; when restrictive monetary and fiscal policies have had negative consequences for economic growth and employment, rather than contributing to economic recovery and combating unemployment. the eu is far from a homogeneous economic area, with considerable disparities between member states in terms of the level of economic and regional development, inflation and unemployment, which have been exacerbated by the single monetary policy, and have led to the costs of economic adjustment being borne by wages and employment, workers and populations. the inflationary effects of the euro on basic goods and bank charges are also to be borne in mind. mr president, we are very concerned about the implementation and revision of the lisbon agenda, which was adopted in march 2000. today, contrary to the promise, we have 20 million unemployed and some 70 million people at risk of poverty. these are unacceptable numbers. and if it is true that the lisbon agenda was a great failure, as president prodi recently said at the end of his term, it was only in terms of the expectations and promises he made on the social front with regard to full employment and social inclusion and with regard to knowledge and research, because in the areas of interest to the economic and financial groups this did not happen. liberalisation and privatisation in key sectors such as energy, post, telecommunications, essential public services and the financial sector have advanced, as have more and more legislative proposals in areas which call into question fundamental human rights and workers' rights, notably the proposal for a directive aimed at creating an internal market in services, i.e. more privatisation, and the backward and inadmissible proposal for a directive on working time. a review of the lisbon agenda is therefore needed to change its content and give priority to the creation of jobs with rights and the necessary social inclusion.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr minister, mr commissioner, in the 1980s jacques delors gave the european project a new impetus, a new vision, when he proposed the completion of the internal market and a single currency. in 2000, at the lisbon summit, the european union again set itself a challenge for the next decade: to become the most dynamic and competitive economy in the world. but as we enter 2005, halfway through the calendar, the balance is not a happy one. progress is slow and in a few days' time wim kok will present his mid-term evaluation report, a highlight of the agenda for the next european summit in november. it is not for the house to comment on the conclusions of this interim report. however, i would like to draw attention to two points which i consider to be of the greatest importance. the first has to do with the fact that when a strategy aims to touch everything, it usually touches nothing. it is therefore appropriate to establish clear priorities within the defined strategy. it is not a question of favouring the economic side of the strategy to the detriment of its social or environmental side, or vice versa. it is a question of defining political priorities in all its aspects. these are difficult choices, but they are inevitable. the second point is to emphasize that the lisbon strategy cannot be seen as the sole responsibility of the european union. success will depend to a large extent on the capacity and commitment of member states to the structural reforms they will have to undertake, which means that they will have to show a clear political will to take a leading role at world level. i still believe that the objectives of the lisbon strategy are neither utopian nor unrealizable. by the way, who would have believed in the 1980s that more than three hundred million europeans would now use a single currency? as kohl said, the visionaries ended up being the realists. a final word, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, to welcome the position taken by the president of the next european commission (i hope) in making the lisbon strategy a priority for his mandate.

in writing. in this first draft of the general budget of the european union (or preliminary draft gbs) for 2005, it is already possible to surprise some of the strongest lines. without prejudice to the presentation of future corrections, it can be concluded that a central concern of institutional strengthening (increase in appropriations allocated to expenditure on staff in active employment; increase in administrative appropriations; increase in appropriations for financial control) eventually runs through this budget. the council's draft budget for 2005 is, unfortunately, equal to 1.00% of the gross national income (gni) of the 25 eu member states, continuing the pressure to lower the 1.24% ceiling publicly advocated by several member states, which runs counter to the recent accession of 10 new member states and attempts to move forward with institutional europe. i support in this budget the laudable concern for institutional operability at the level of the various policies, although i believe that we are still far from the real ambition of sustainability, prosperity and integration in which citizens see themselves.
in writing. the budgetary process in the eu has in the past shown a lag between the community's political priorities and their respective financing, leading to some opacity. the commission has adopted a new activity-based management (abm) approach, following pressure from the ep. the idea is good and simple. the first step is to identify the activities to be carried out in accordance with the political priorities and then to allocate the appropriate human and financial resources. the adoption of this method would seem to make it easier to carry out a rigorous assessment of the consequences of certain policies and actions. despite the efforts already made, i have to say that the quality of the declarations of activity is poor and that they are of little use to the budgetary process. they are far from being at a desirable level. information is diffuse, poorly quantified and sometimes omitted in practical information. most of the targets and their indicators are not measurable and their implications for human and financial resources are not well defined. what was fundamental was not reached. if everything that is not measured cannot be managed, there is still no clear correspondence between the objectives and targets and the indicators chosen to measure the degree of achievement of those objectives. there is therefore a long way to go on this issue.

in writing. after a long period of experimentation with sampling and testing of seeds, with the aim of examining whether such techniques could be used as alternatives to the official certification procedures, it was concluded that simplification of the procedures could be possible without entailing a significant decrease in seed quality. in view of this conclusion, the proposal for a directive, which covers four production sectors (forage, cereals, beet and oilseed and fibre) could contribute to the desired simplification effort, as well as extending the scope of field inspections under official supervision to all crops and increasing the scope of 'equivalence' of eu seeds to all types produced in third countries. since the legislative amendments proposed by the proposal are designed to reduce bureaucracy and promote the development of the market, i voted in favour.

in writing. we are aware of the pressure to give the european union fiscal sovereignty, that is to say the power to levy taxes, and we are firmly opposed to this, because this sovereignty is an essential element of the sovereignty of a state. we are aware of the dangers of progressive tax harmonization which is aimed, step by step, at the federal path. however, we have never opposed greater fiscal coordination to tax the free movement of capital, to combat tax evasion and fraud, to end tax havens and to prevent money laundering. the savings directive, which is part of the so-called monti package, despite its dangers and shortcomings, contributes to a system of exchange of information, including the lifting of banking secrecy, between the tax administrations of the member states so that they can tax the interest of a resident of their country obtained in another member state. the council therefore authorised the commission to negotiate agreements with switzerland, the usa, andorra, liechtenstein, monaco and san marino for these states to apply equivalent measures to prevent capital flight. these agreements would deserve our support, not because of the obstacles to the internal market, as the rapporteur complains, but because coordination is necessary to tax capital and combat tax havens, particularly when the tax is not paid. in writing. the proposal follows the authorisation given by the eu council to the european commission (decision of 16 october 2001) to negotiate agreements with switzerland, the united states of america, andorra, liechtenstein, monaco and san marino to combat the cases of natural and legal persons who end up being exempt from all forms of taxation in their state of residence on interest received in another state. this proposal promotes mechanisms to combat unfair tax competition and will naturally lead to an improvement in the functioning of the single market. on the other hand, an effective instrument to combat money laundering is being put into practice, in this case in relations with andorra. the unanimous vote by the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection was a clear indication of the desire to pursue all these objectives. i voted yes.
in writing. the implementation of the argo programme in 2003 fell far short of the objectives due to under-utilisation of funds, caused by insufficient knowledge of the programme by national administrations and, on the other hand, by the difficulty in mobilising the necessary co-operation. this funding programme is mainly intended to promote cooperation between member states in the fields of asylum, immigration, crossing of external borders and visas. the aim of this proposal is to amend the argo decision so that it is possible to finance projects of one member state alone, without the direct participation of other member states, for measures in the field of the union's external borders, which, being in an area of free movement, are logically of common interest to all member states. i voted in favour of the proposed amendments because, although not the ideal solution, it is nevertheless what can be done at this time - before the new financial perspectives for the period after 2006 - to contribute to burden sharing in the context of integrated management (short voting statement pursuant to rule 163 (1))

in writing. the practical implementation of the argo programme - an action programme for administrative cooperation on external borders, visas, asylum and immigration, established by council decision in june 2002 - has been beset by difficulties, mainly because the measures envisaged have proved too bureaucratic. the member states are facing increasing difficulties in organising and mobilising, with partners in other member states, the resources needed to implement projects. the commission therefore proposes that, in order to promote the general objectives of the argo programme, the number of actions to be proposed in the field of external borders should be increased and diversified. the granting of financial aid to national projects in the field of external borders, with a view to compensating for certain structural deficiencies at strategic border crossing points, reflects a desire, often expressed by both the council and parliament, for ever greater coordination between the various member states as an essential response to contemporary challenges. it should be recalled that the length of the external land border of the european union has almost doubled since the recent enlargement. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. the main purpose of this proposal for a directive is to take account of the recent enlargement of the european union and the specific situation of the new member states, particularly as regards the achievement of the recycling and recovery targets, by giving them more time to adapt their national systems to the community targets, which we do not object to in principle. however, despite the european commission's commitment to present a report on the implementation of the directive by 30 june 2005, it is important to re-emphasise the importance of reuse and prevention in relation to packaging and packaging waste, giving them priority over recycling. it is important to remember that prevention should be the first line to reduce the impact of packaging on the environment; reuse the second line and everything that cannot be reused should be recycled. in this sense, the current directive may have adverse effects on existing reuse systems. therefore, more incentives should be created to introduce new packaging reuse systems where existing ones do not represent an environmental benefit.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mrs dorette corbey (a6-0027/2004) - packaging and packaging waste on a proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directive 94/62/ec on packaging and packaging waste. on 31 december 1994, directive 94/62/ec on packaging and packaging waste entered into force. at the time this proposal was submitted to the european parliament and the council, accession negotiations were under way with ten new member states. the new member states acceded to the european union on 1 may 2004 without the transitional periods relating to the original directive having expired for all the acceding states. in addition, there was insufficient information on the conditions for increasing recovery and recycling targets in these states. the directive does not therefore contain any specific proposals for the accession countries in the operational part. this proposal sets 31 december 2012 as the deadline for the 10 new member states to meet the recovery and recycling targets for packaging waste. i consider it essential that all efforts be made to encourage packaging reuse systems in order to ensure that the
in writing. as i have said on many occasions, the recovery and recycling of packaging waste must be increased throughout the european union in order to reduce its environmental impact. the good results achieved by the member states in a union of 15 can and should be achieved by newcomers too. the commission is proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road. i found the proposal put forward by the rapporteur very relevant, in the sense that all member states should continue to be encouraged to impose packaging reuse systems in order to ensure a high level of environmental protection, while giving the new member states a period for better adaptation.
in writing. the present proposal to amend the regulation on the european agency for reconstruction has political consequences for the republic of cyprus which we consider very serious. as has been pointed out, this is a matter of using an eu agency set up with the aim of using community funds for the balkan region after the destruction of yugoslavia to manage future community funds for the turkish cypriot community. in other words, it is now intended to use this agency, which manages funds for third countries - which obviously does not apply to cyprus - to provide 'assistance' to the turkish cypriot community, which is living under the occupation of turkish troops. this will in fact result in the implicit recognition of the occupying authorities and the illegal turkish republic of northern cyprus (an entity recognised only by turkey). what they are proposing is a procedure for financial aid to the turkish cypriot community which makes a blank slate of the fact that the republic of cyprus, a member state of the european union, has part of its territory militarily occupied by turkey, which is unacceptable. the paradox is that we are voting on the use of the agency for the practical implementation of a regulation (short explanation of vote pursuant to rule 163 (1))
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr anders samuelsen (a6-0031/2004) - european agency for reconstruction on the proposal for a council regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 2667/2000 on the european agency for reconstruction. i believe that the agency's task is fundamental, especially in view of the fact that south-east europe is a key region for the european union. however, the european parliament cannot fail to exercise its responsibilities as budgetary authority, nor allow a future that is less than structured and stable in the competences and tasks of the european agency for reconstruction. overall, the agency appears to be performing its task of managing the main community aid programmes in the region effectively. parliament called on the commission to present a report clearly indicating the division of tasks and responsibilities between the agency's operational centres and the commission's delegations, accompanied by an analysis of the operation of the regulation.
in writing. the european agency for reconstruction has demonstrated, as indicated in recent evaluation reports, a good capacity to implement the development assistance policy for the balkan region as laid down in that cards regulation and to achieve the objectives of its mandate. the lisbon european council (march 2000) confirmed that the main objective remains the fullest possible integration of the countries of the balkan region into the general political and economic mainstream of europe and that the stabilisation and association process is the cornerstone of its policy in the balkans. and the european council in vila da feira (june 2000) recognised these countries as potential candidates for membership of the european union. the implementation of the assistance policy which has been implemented and whose relevance and effectiveness have been confirmed should therefore be followed up by the extension of the mandate of the agency, and a stable community financial framework should be in place until 2006. i voted yes.
in writing. one of the fundamental issues raised by this proposal concerns respect for the full integrity of the republic of cyprus. it cynically calls on the european parliament to ensure that the european council takes an 'impartial' decision. fair to whom? we have to ask. is it ever possible to demand impartiality between occupier and occupied? between perpetrator and victim? it calls on the european parliament to take a "fair" decision. we affirm that there is no truly just resolution that does not condemn the turkish occupation of northern cyprus, demand the withdrawal of its troops and the implementation of un resolutions. any solution that is formulated with a view to the 'economic development of the turkish cypriot community' must therefore, without fail, respect the republic of cyprus, its territorial integrity and its sovereignty. it will not be acceptable for the european union to develop direct trade relations with the occupied part of cyprus to the detriment of and in addition to the cypriot government. as the cypriot authorities have rightly and legitimately stated, the european union's trade with the occupied part of cyprus must necessarily include the cypriot government. hence our vote.
in writing. regardless of the outcome of the referendum in cyprus, the european union must maintain its decision to provide financial support to the turkish cypriot community, provided that this does not call into question respect for the european union's position on this matter. i therefore voted in favour of the report by mrs mechtild rothe (a6-0032/2004) - financial support instrument (cyprus).
in writing. the proposal for a council regulation aims to promote the economic development of the turkish cypriot community by giving practical substance to the commitment, promised in the council declaration of 26 april 2004, to: 'end the isolation of the turkish cypriot community and facilitate the reunification of cyprus by promoting the economic development of the turkish cypriot community'. the turkish cypriot community clearly expressed its desire to secure its future within the european union in a referendum on 24 april 2004. and that has also been the expressed wish of the european union on several occasions. however, the known overall framework eventually made it impossible to use the amount provided for in the financial perspective for 2004-06. i therefore agree that the european union should provide assistance to the turkish cypriot community, in particular in the areas of economic development, economic integration of the island and improved contacts between the two communities and with the eu, in order to facilitate the reunification of cyprus, as also proposed in the regulation. i welcome the important proposal and i voted in favour.

in writing. although i object to some points, there are important reasons why i voted in favour of the raül romeva i rueda report (a6-0022/2004) - arms exports. above all, i agree with the idea that effective control of arms exports on a global scale can only be ensured by an international arms control regime. therefore, strict international rules on arms exports should be promoted in the framework of the 2006 un conference on the review of small arms with a view to the adoption of a legally binding international arms trade treaty, including measures for the conversion and restructuring of companies producing military goods. on the other hand, the maintenance of the arms embargo on china is a positive sign that the european union is giving its criteria in this matter.
in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the military operation 'althea' in bosnia and herzegovina (b6-0162/2004). i believe that operation althea should reinforce the european union's overall approach to bosnia-herzegovina and support the progress of that country. this action aims to strengthen local police capacity and the fight against organised crime by gradually transferring responsibility for security to local authorities. the stabilisation and association process in bosnia and herzegovina is an essential framework for the country's path towards stability and development. i would like to remind you once again that this country must rely primarily on its own efforts on its way to peace and stability. the decision by the european union to use nato assets and capabilities for the 'althea' mission is fundamental, thus confirming the collaboration between the two organisations and implementing the december 2002 agreement on the european union's access to nato planning and command assets ('berlin plus').
in writing. he refers to the european parliament's resolution that this is the 'first large-scale military mission of the european union' with some 7 000 military personnel. others add that it is "mostly" a transfer of command from nato to the eu, "without major changes to the composition of the troops on the ground". it is written that such a 'mission' will strengthen the 'preparation of bosnia-herzegovina's eventual accession to the eu'. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. we say that it is a matter of continuing the military occupation of this balkan country by nato, now through its european/eu pillar, in a process of accelerated 'transatlantic' militarisation. to paraphrase greek mythology, as cynically did the present warlords - responsible for the horror of its effects - it would seem that 'mars', the god of war, preoccupied with more pressing concerns - the war on the iraqi people - gave his wife 'althea' the task of looking after bosnia-herzegovina, but always under his armed 'protector' arm. it is the peoples and the peace that they lose.
in writing. the fact that operation althea is the largest military mission ever conducted by the european union should be a good moment to boost the political and popular debate about the limits and independence (and possible interdependence) of the member states' defence policy. it would be useful to monitor the operation closely and to promote the debate on defence in a european framework, possibly in the context of the discussion of the constitutional treaty. i think it is important that nato maintains a headquarters in sarajevo and that it remains closely linked to the operation. the experience it has, the success it has achieved in bosnia and the fact that it is the main military structure in which most member states are integrated are factors that contribute to ensuring that its relevance and its central importance in a geostrategic context that is desired as a euro-atlantic priority is not overlooked. the difficulties which bosnia-herzegovina still faces at the present time are evident. in addition to terrorism, the difficulties in enforcing good governance mechanisms and rampant corruption, reports from military personnel involved in previous operations show that there are still several cases of latent animosity.
in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on climate change b6-0129/2004. i believe that the kyoto protocol is a first attempt by the international community to combat climate change and that this does not mean that other measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions that could be adopted at national level should be relegated to the background, but rather that they should be considered as complementary. the european union should play a leading role in the negotiations to be held at the cop-10 conference in buenos aires. cop-10 is a good opportunity not only to build on the decisions taken at previous conferences of the parties, in particular in bonn, marrakesh, new delhi and milan, on the implementation of the kyoto protocol, but also to launch a broad debate on the main issues for the second commitment period, with a view to achieving the community objective of keeping the average global temperature increase below + 2 °c above pre-industrial levels; reiterates its position that the principle of equal rights for all citizens of the world should be applied in the long term.
in writing. the problem of climate change and its effects on the planet is one that is increasingly being tackled in the context of globalisation and implies a different view of the world and of the development models in practice. the known studies on climate change point to accelerated worsening of the effects of this phenomenon. if the phenomena of climate change continue, they will have serious social, environmental, economic and public health consequences. in addition to the understanding that the prevention of climate change undoubtedly requires the adoption of policies and measures by each state to reduce the emission of greenhouse gases, i would also like to stress the importance of the kyoto protocol, the first international instrument in the fight against climate change. i believe that the eu delegation to the buenos aires conference should take a leading role in the negotiations, seeking to alert its international partners to the need to protect the climate and should also engage in a frank, open and sensible dialogue with the united states so that they reconsider their decision not to ratify. i voted yes.

the rapporteur. mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to begin by thanking my colleagues on the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, in particular the shadow rapporteurs and, most especially, mr michael cashman, for their cooperation. we are all needed to work together in responding to the times of insecurity we live in. it's not worth sticking your head in the sand. the need to strengthen the security of our citizens is undeniable and we must always do so without compromising on the essential freedoms, including the right to privacy of personal data. the proposal we are discussing today was presented to parliament in february 2004 and is the result of a coherent approach to biometric identifiers, involving harmonised solutions for national documents of third countries, passports for citizens of the european union and the vis system and the second generation of the schengen information system. increased security of travel documents and the integration of biometric identifiers should contribute to the fight against terrorism and illegal immigration and also to the enhancement of security in the exercise of freedom of movement. the best way to prevent the use of false identities is to check whether the person who presented the document is the rightful holder. the use of new technologies has many advantages in terms of identifying individuals and preventing the forgery of documents. we must fight against so-called visa-shopping and identity theft. the attention paid by the european parliament to data protection is fully justified. a balance must always be struck between the need for security and respect for individual rights and freedoms as recognised by national and community law. this is an essential and a priori condition for the adoption of the use of biometric identifiers. for all these reasons i have clearly supported the amendments tabled in the letter of the article 29 working party and i stress the need for measures on access: who can have access and for what purposes. member states should establish a list of competent authorities, of safeguards in relation to persons who are unable to provide some of the selected biometric data, such as fingerprints - as is the case for victims of burns or of organ amputations - of safeguards that at border controls, in particular in the case of a false rejection, there is a place for the concerned citizens to be informed of the reasons for such rejection and of the means at their disposal to resolve the situation quickly. finally, new tasks are assigned to the supervisory authorities in this area, accompanied by an increase in the resources needed to perform the new tasks. i would like to end by listing the four issues which are crucial to the adoption of this report. first, a single purpose for the use of the data. it should be clarified beyond any doubt that data may only be used for the purpose of identity verification and in no case for the purpose of identification or even covert surveillance. secondly, the question of the database. the report i am presenting to you clearly rejects the creation of a central database. biometric data should be stored exclusively in the passport. the creation of a database is not necessary to ensure a more reliable link between the passport and its holder and the risk of misuse of the function, i.e. the use of the data for purposes other than those originally intended, is too high. in order to avoid confusion or misrepresentation, i would point out, however, that nowhere in the commission's legislative proposal or in the current council text is there any specific proposal for the creation of such a database. there was a reference in the explanatory statement to possible future consideration of this possibility and only for this reason do we propose that the position of the european parliament be made clear from now on. thirdly, the technical solution chosen. the technical specifications must be robust enough to lend credence to the use of biometrics. we cannot risk rushing into solutions which later on will be considered ill-prepared or technologically outdated or even expensive. such an action would undermine the confidence of the citizens. and a fundamental question, commissioner frattini, the most delicate part in terms of data protection does not result from the choice of principle but from the way it will be implemented. that is why we have proposed that the experts responsible for examining technical specifications in the light of data protection should be given the opportunity to evaluate the technical specifications and, if necessary, to suggest corrections to existing problems. fourth and last point: amendments to the original proposal. at its meeting on 26 october the council decided to make the following amendment: the introduction of fingerprints, which was previously optional, has now become mandatory. from a political point of view, the civil liberties committee had already approved by a large majority the introduction of these two biometric identifiers, with the only difference that it had left it to the discretion of the member states to adopt or not the second. all the reservations were withdrawn in the council and it was the member states themselves who decided to put aside this discretion and to opt for the two options. i therefore believe that there is no objection to parliament voting in favour of this report, making its position on this matter clear and stressing the guarantees we want to be safeguarded at all times.

in writing. we are aware of the pressure to give the european union fiscal sovereignty, that is to say the power to levy taxes, and we are firmly opposed to this, because this sovereignty is an essential element of the sovereignty of a state. we are aware of the dangers of progressive tax harmonization which is aimed, step by step, at the federal path. however, we have never opposed greater fiscal coordination to tax the free movement of capital, to combat tax evasion and fraud, to end tax havens and to prevent money laundering. the savings directive, which is part of the so-called monti package, despite its dangers and shortcomings, contributes to a system of exchange of information, including the lifting of banking secrecy, between the tax administrations of the member states so that they can tax the interest of a resident of their country obtained in another member state. the council therefore authorised the commission to negotiate agreements with switzerland, the usa, andorra, liechtenstein, monaco and san marino for these states to apply equivalent measures to prevent capital flight. these agreements would deserve our support, not because of the obstacles to the internal market, as the rapporteur complains, but because coordination is necessary to tax capital and combat tax havens, particularly when the bulk of the tax burden falls on the employees. however, we believe that the terms of the agreement do not guarantee such a purpose.

in writing. the rapid development of new technologies - in particular the new opportunities offered by the internet and new online technologies - is countered by the problem of the growth of new dangers and new abuses in their use. measures are therefore needed to protect the end-user from unwanted content and to encourage safer use. i therefore support this initiative which seeks to adopt a multiannual community programme to promote safer use of the internet and new online technologies. its action will focus on areas such as content potentially harmful to children, content not desired by the end user and illegal content such as child pornography. it succeeds the action plan for a safer internet (1998-2004), which was a very successful outcome and has stimulated a wide range of initiatives promoting the best ways to benefit from the potential of new media in a secure way. it is also positive that new hotlines are to be set up in all member states, which should be incorporated quickly and effectively into the existing european hotline network, which allows for the coverage and exchange of reports on the most worrying types of illegal content.
in writing. we voted in favour of this report because it gives special attention to an area where there is general agreement. we agree that the fight against misuse and the promotion of safer use of the internet, particularly by children, and the fight against illegal and unwanted content is an objective that we believe needs to be given greater attention. we welcome the proposal to set up a programme to finance and coordinate the fight against illegal content, enabling users to be informed of content rather than policed; the creation and coordination of service centres in eu countries and their coordination with future members and third countries, limiting the funding of private software companies for filtering; the strengthening of the participation of ngos and the creation of self-regulation mechanisms by servers rather than the establishment of judicial control procedures. the evolution of the internet, which has allowed it to go beyond the previous domains and to reach the so-called "navigation" of the available pages, is dominated by commercial interests, turning it into a medium of diffusion of advertising par excellence, extended to the pornography industry and illegal content, in particular child pornography and xenophobic and racist material. it is therefore necessary to take measures, but without jeopardizing fundamental rights and freedoms.
in writing. i voted in favour of the edith mastenbroek report (a6-0033/2004) - safer use of the internet and new online technologies. internet penetration and the use of new technologies such as mobile communications are still growing significantly in the community. at the same time, there are still dangers, especially for children, and abusive practices in the use of technologies, and new dangers and abusive practices are also emerging. measures are therefore needed to promote safer use of the internet and to protect the end-user from unwanted content. the new programme, safer internet plus, contains a number of good proposals for the continuation of existing programmes and the creation of new ones. its focus on the end user is the most realistic approach, and its insistence on awareness is its main virtue. the rapporteur, like us, believes that the programme should stress the importance of transparency and the representation of all stakeholders at all levels and act on the four fronts proposed - combating illegal content, tackling unwanted and harmful content, organising the 'safer internet forum' and raising awareness among citizens in general.
in writing. as a consequence and an integral part of the current security drift by the eu institutions, the current proposal from the european commission and the council deserves our rejection - a position which was adopted by the european parliament in the previous legislature. as is widely denounced, this is a disproportionate measure - and of questionable legal basis - which is part of a supranational dynamic and the creation of the foundations of the instruments of surveillance and control at eu level - such as the creation of a personal data base at eu level - especially since there is no legal framework for the protection of citizens or any parliamentary supervision, in particular of national parliaments. it is a measure which is subserviently designed to meet the requirements of the united states for the entry of eu citizens, without reciprocity. the council, at the initiative of the security 'g5' (great britain, germany, france, italy and spain), goes even further than the 'requirements' for the use of biometric data - whose effectiveness is more than questionable in the face of the arguments put forward for its introduction, the so-called 'fight against terrorism' - by introducing two (photography and digital printing) instead of one. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr carlos coelho (a6-0028/2004) - passports for citizens of the union. the proposal aims to make passports more secure by introducing harmonised and legally binding standards for the security features of eu citizens' passports and by introducing biometric identifiers. the introduction of a biometric identifier will make it extremely difficult to forge passports, as biometrics will ensure that the person presenting a passport is in fact the holder for whom it was originally issued. the use of biometrics is a very sensitive issue from the point of view of data protection. the necessary safeguards will have to be put in place to ensure full compliance with the provisions of the data protection directive. in fact, personal data should be adequate, relevant and not excessive in relation to the purposes for which they are collected and subsequently processed. however, we believe that the report strikes a good balance between the security that needs to be guaranteed and the freedom that we should all enjoy.

the rapporteur. i have no objection to the report on the dutch initiative on vehicle theft being placed on the agenda, mr president, because i think it would be a kind gesture towards the dutch presidency if parliament, before it finishes, gave its opinion on its initiative, which is, moreover, a peaceful initiative and does not generate controversy among the benches. what i do not think is reasonable is that this should be done to the detriment of the initiative on registers. why would you do that? because what is at stake in the matter of the registers is the introduction of biometric data. the european parliament has already decided on this matter in the last session in brussels, with regard to passports. now we have to close the file on the visas. this is not a matter of codecision. it is a matter on which parliament gives its opinion to the council and either parliament gives its opinion in time to influence the council's decision or we lose out by 'failure to appear' because the council will decide in the absence of parliament's position. our position was well founded - it had the support of the socialists in the committee on civil liberties - and i do not see why we should dispense with this vote at today's sitting. so, mr president, i think we can add the report on the dutch initiative - a nice gesture for the presidency in office - but without withdrawing the report on visas, which was, moreover, adopted by a very large majority in the committee on civil liberties and with the vote of the socialists.
