(summary statement pursuant to rule 142 (1) of the rules of procedure)
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the president of the commission has already given this parliament proof of his determination and enthusiasm to take over the leadership of the executive of the european union on the basis of a reforming culture, practices, policies and procedures. i hope that the commission as a whole will be able to find what is always the most difficult thing in the life of the institutions, with the impetus and the will to reform: the discovery of the right distance between realism and utopia. it is the search for this constant balance - which some call 'sensibility' - that has enabled europe over the last fifty years to develop the social model which is the driving force behind european identity. the essential components of this model have been peace, prosperity and the convergence of cultures. this model proved to be the winning model. but today we are faced with a reality in which many aspects have recently emerged that were previously unknown to us: a worrying demographic situation coupled with unprecedented technological developments, the most decisive factors in the consolidation of the phenomenon that has made the world smaller: globalization. in these circumstances, if europe is to remain a space that coexists with the winning model, it must face unhesitatingly the inevitability of reforms that lead, in the first place, to the strengthening of its competitiveness. this means opening up markets, increasing productivity, more and better research, more innovation and a greater bet on people and ideas. however, the reforms needed for europe cannot be seen as the sole task of the commission. i think that the most critical point of the reform era that is now beginning has more to do with the commitment and risk-taking on the part of the member states in implementing these reforms. it is only with a strong commitment from the member states that the participation of the most dynamic sectors of society and the intermediate powers can be encouraged, and without this there is no reform possible. this is also where i believe parliament should act.
mr president, mr president of the commission, when it comes to defining strategic guidelines, we should be clearer so that we can better express our ambition. the european union must be the europe of freedom, and freedom exists only in a healthy economic environment and with real and effective security. we need a competitive economy to meet the challenges of growth and full employment in a globalised world, and we must be able to reap the benefits of this. the challenge we face is to achieve an economy which makes balanced use of natural resources, which is efficient because it is modern and not because it accepts breaking the commitments on which the essence of its social model is based. wealth cannot be produced without work, and more wealth cannot be produced by working less. there is no such miracle, and those who persist in this mirage will be responsible for less development and less cohesion, both economically and socially. on the other hand, we need security. not security from speeches that exploit fear or those that ignore threats, but from strong policies that ensure effective borders and effective internal security. it is also necessary for europe to share with our traditional allies an international policy which promotes democracy and peace in our neighbouring territories and which contributes to a more secure and developed world. mr president, the coming years will require the commission under the presidency of mr barroso to show competence and a firm line of action in a period marked by the uncertainties arising from the ratification of the constitutional treaty and the financial austerity imposed on the member states by the stability and growth pact. we cannot have a union with more powers, more policies, more obligations and more states on the one hand and less budget and less resources on the other. it is an impossible equation, which makes impossible in the long term what we all want, a free and developed economy in a safe territory. this is the key to our model and the policy guidelines which will underpin it in the years ahead.
in writing. i voted in favour of the request for consultation of the european economic and social committee - european agricultural fund for rural development on the proposal for a council regulation on support for rural development by the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd). i believe that the european economic and social committee should be consulted given the strategic importance of the cap reform in 2003 and 2004. having concluded that the main focus of policy reform in the new financial period should be on rural development, it should also be underlined that more than half of the eu-25 population lives in rural areas, which cover 90% of the territory. rural development is therefore an important policy area, as reiterated in the conclusions of the lisbon (march 2000) and gothenburg (june 2001) european councils. it seems to me therefore essential to find together with the various institutional actors the measures that will help to accompany and further complement the reform of the cap and ensure coherence with the instruments and policies of the first pillar; as well as to contribute to other political priorities of the european union, such as the sustainable management of natural resources, innovation and competitiveness in rural areas, as well as economic and social cohesion.
in writing. i voted in favour of the request for consultation of the committee of the regions - erdf, esf and cohesion fund - on the proposal for a council regulation laying down general provisions on the european regional development fund, the european social fund and the cohesion fund. i believe that cohesion policy is one of the fundamental instruments of solidarity within the european union. a policy which must be ambitious and capable of meeting the challenges of the latest enlargement and the new prospects for economic growth in europe. the consultation of the committee of the regions is essential given the strategic importance of these funds. the union's cohesion policy is an important contribution to achieving the objectives of growth and cohesion, as by reducing economic and social disparities, the union helps to ensure that all regions and social groups can contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the union.
in writing. i voted in favour of the request for consultation by the committee of the regions - erdf on the proposal for a council regulation on the european regional development fund. this consultation seems to me to be essential, given the importance of the erdf for correcting regional imbalances. with the recent enlargement, regional disparities within the eu have widened, with a large increase in regions lagging behind. i believe that the harmonious development of the various regions of europe is a permanent challenge to which we must respond with clarity of objectives and firmness in political decisions. the development of the community's territory, which has increased with enlargement, requires greater territorial cooperation, based on joint projects for local development within the framework of crossborder cooperation and on measures leading to integrated territorial development, for which we need the participation of all regional actors.
in writing. i voted in favour of the request for consultation of the committee of the regions - cohesion fund on the proposal for a council regulation establishing the cohesion fund. the contribution of the committee of the regions to this process of revision of the cohesion fund is indispensable since this is the fund which will contribute financially to the implementation of projects in the fields of the environment and the trans-european networks in the field of transport infrastructure. i believe that this revision should maintain the fundamental principles which define this policy and be based on an overall balance between strengthening the strategic dimension on the one hand and simplifying the system of implementation on the other, without thereby drawing a framework for reducing the solidarity between the states which is the principle and characteristic of this union of states.
in writing. i voted in favour of the request for consultation of the committee of the regions - european grouping of crossborder cooperation (egcc) on the proposal for a council regulation on the creation of a european grouping of crossborder cooperation (egcc). the committee of the regions should be consulted given the importance of the powers exercised by local and regional authorities as public authorities. in view of the serious difficulties faced by member states, regions and local authorities in implementing and managing crossborder, transnational and interregional cooperation actions, within the framework of different national legislation and procedures, it is essential that appropriate measures be taken at community level to overcome these difficulties. this new instrument of cooperation at community level allows the setting-up of cooperative groups with legal personality within the community, known as european crossborder cooperation groups (eccgs). the harmonious development of the community as a whole and the strengthening of economic, social and territorial cohesion require the strengthening of crossborder cooperation and the adoption of measures to ensure that obstacles to crossborder cooperation are removed.
in writing. the requirements of full and harmonious integration of the 10 new member states require that all protocols previously restricted to the 15 member states be adapted as soon as possible.

in writing. i voted in favour of the council's proposal for a directive because i considered that it had already been sufficiently and unequivocally considered and assessed by the agri committee and deserved unanimous approval. however, i question the goodness and necessity of these matters of mere rectification or legislative updating following the same (albeit simplified) procedure as other reports dealing with matters of significantly greater importance. in my view, in the present case, the amendment of directive 87/32/eec can only be understood in the light of an excessively positivist interpretation of community law, since the storage of frozen bovine semen intended for 'semen collection centres' (with own production) could, by means of rules of common legal interpretation, include 'semen storage centres' (without own production), without any formal rectification being necessary for that purpose. it may seem like a joke. but sometimes even ridicule can be taken seriously; or the serious can seem ridiculous.
in writing. the proposal to amend the council regulation on eaggf support for rural development 'in order to avoid a difference in treatment between the member states' which were part of the european union before enlargement and the current 25 countries' is a positive one, but it should be noted that this measure arises in the context of a budgetary discussion in which a real reduction of funds will be made compared to the pre-enlargement period. this means that a policy is being pursued where support for rural development is used as part of a strategy to contain cap expenditure, the liberalisation of agricultural markets and the wto negotiations. these measures do not address the need to redress the deep injustices in the european union's agricultural policy, nor do they serve the urgently needed path towards economic and social cohesion between its various member states. the effective promotion of rural development requires farmers, agricultural production and a model of sustainable human development based on the exploitation of specific economic, social and cultural characteristics and diversity.
in writing. as this is an amendment to the regulation to avoid a difference in treatment between the former member states and those which joined this year, and as there is no budgetary change as a result of this amendment, i am in favour.
in writing. i believe that the states which joined the community after 1 may 2004 deserve treatment from their institutions which should be at least identical to that accorded to the oldest member states. i therefore voted in favour of the proposed amendment, since it is intended to prevent a situation of inequality in the limit of the financial contributions to be made on the basis of regulation no 1257/1999, and the third indent of the second subparagraph of article 47 (2) should be applied to the new member states.

in writing. milk produced in the austrian regions of kleinwalsertal and jungholz is only available to german buyers, since the only access to those areas is by road from germany. regulation (ec) no 1782/2003, which introduced direct payments for the milk and milk products sector, left the management of the individual reference quantities of the producers concerned to the german authorities. at the same time, it stipulated that the payments relating to the milk premium were to be made by the austrian authorities within the limits of their national reference quantity and the corresponding budgetary limit. the result was, as one might expect, a highly irrational situation. it is essential that the dairy premium be administered in a fair and balanced way. the reference quantities for the producers concerned for germany should therefore be converted into reference quantities for austria from the 2004/05 milk year. i voted yes.
in writing. i voted in favour because i believe that, following the council decision of june 2004, it is essential that the legal instruments be adapted accordingly so that this process can proceed in accordance with all its objectives, which will only become possible - and truly effective - with the amendments suggested by the council here.
in writing. perhaps as a citizen of a member state which has benefited and still benefits from financial instruments promoting development and cohesion at european level, and as a witness to the real improvements which have resulted from them for my country, i believe i am in a position to understand the crucial importance of access to those instruments by the new member states and also by the candidate countries, such as croatia. i therefore think it is useful to amend the regulations which provide for these instruments so that this country can have satisfactory access to them as part of the pre-accession process which is now under way. the instruments in question (phare, ispa, sapard) could, during the period of validity of this financial perspective, contribute to structural improvement in the administrative, judicial, environmental, agricultural and transport sectors, preparing croatia for the adoption of the unified pre-accession instrument (ipa) which will be made available to it from 2007.
in writing. the essential reliability of statistical data suggests a widespread practice of agreements between different countries to ensure the validity of data used as indicators on various subjects, in particular by the fact that they are recognized and mutually validated. in the particular case of the swiss federal republic this question is of greater importance for reasons of neighbourliness.
in writing. this report is in line with the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of an agreement in the field of statistics between the european community and the swiss confederation. as you know, the european union and switzerland have enjoyed close relations over the years, economically, socially and politically. the aim here is that these relations should also cover statistical cooperation. i am in full agreement with this aim, which, moreover, should have been achieved long ago on our part. in fact, switzerland was a signatory to the agreement on the european economic area (eea) and this agreement included statistical cooperation; but it was switzerland that could not ratify it because of a negative national referendum in 1992. the 1992 deadlock must be finally overcome, the negotiations decided on in 2000 must be concluded once and for all, and a full framework for cooperation with switzerland must be established, also in the statistical field.

in writing. this is the third readmission agreement concluded between the european community and a third country, as part of the so-called 'fight against illegal immigration'. the rapporteur stresses, and i quote, that 'the negotiations on readmission agreements have been going through difficulties, particularly because of the european union's problems in offering something in return for the agreements'. as we have been denouncing, it is basically a matter of expelling all the workers who, yearning for a better life, emigrate to another country, but who are confronted with a 'management' of human resources that sifts them, dismissing those it considers unnecessary. this is a procedure which is part of a logic of exploiting the workforce in a 'global' way, of which these agreements are only one of the visible faces. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. moreover, agreements of this kind, which have already been concluded with a number of countries, are of the utmost importance in the fight against illegal immigration, which, while being demanding that the law be strictly observed, also take care to ensure respect for human rights. reasons why i'm in favor of your approval.
in writing. on the basis of the amsterdam treaty, in the context of managing migratory flows, the tampere summit called for the union to develop 'assistance to countries of origin and transit with a view to promoting voluntary return and to assisting the authorities of these countries to strengthen their capacities to combat effectively trafficking in human beings and to assume their readmission obligations towards the community and the member states' (iv.26.). the agreement to which the proposal for a decision refers is aimed specifically at regulating the conditions under which the union and the sinhalese authorities will readmit persons who are not legally resident in the territory of the other party, a practice which the community would like to see included in all future agreements with third countries. well, that's my guess. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption, and the council will be consulted on it. i voted yes.
in writing. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a regulation on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. the commission was unable to obtain unanimous agreement in the council on its proposal for a directive on the simplification and rationalisation of reduced vat rates. the deadline for directive 1999/85/ec, which allows member states to apply a reduced rate of vat on labour-intensive services on an experimental basis, has therefore been extended successively, and now expires on 31 december 2005. the aim of this adaptation of the directive is to enable it to be applied to the new member states as a result of enlargement, which we think is the right thing to do. although the commission's evaluation report states that the effects of this measure are virtually nil and the cost-benefit ratio is poor, the commission's main objection is related to the difficulties in vat harmonisation, although it states that this measure does not distort the rules of the internal market. despite some reservations about the measure and knowing that it will not solve the problems of high unemployment in the european union, we think that this permission should be maintained for those member states that want to apply it permanently, with a view to making an additional contribution to job creation and to combating the parallel economy. let us hope that the new member states will contribute to this objective.
in writing. the council adopted on 22 october 1999 directive 1999/85/ec amending directive 77/88/eec with a view to the possibility of applying a reduced rate of vat to labour-intensive services on an experimental basis, allowing member states wishing to do so to test the effects of a vat reduction on these specific sectors in terms of job creation and the decline of the parallel economy. the experiment was eventually the subject of an evaluation report which revealed that it was not possible to identify a direct relationship between the reduction in vat rates and the reduction in unemployment and the shadow economy. the solution of lowering vat rates as a way of stimulating the labour market and reducing the shadow economy does not seem to me to be the best and most appropriate. however, the fact that the new member states were not allowed to apply reduced rates (the experiment was to be definitively concluded by 31 december 2003) led to an unfair situation. i voted in favour of this because i believe that the new member states should be given the same opportunity.
in writing. international fund for ireland on a proposal for a council regulation on the ec financial contributions to the international fund for ireland (2005-06). the fund is still very important in the reconstruction of areas devastated by the instability of decades of terrorism. their objectives remain pressing and at this historic moment in the negotiations for a lasting peace, the european union must show its solidarity with the irish people.
in writing. the international fund for ireland, set up in 1986 to contribute to the implementation of the anglo-irish agreement by promoting economic and social progress and encouraging contacts, dialogue and reconciliation between nationalists and unionists throughout ireland, has been extremely useful and positive in promoting economic and social development for peace and reconciliation in the region. the process of consolidating peace in northern ireland and the border region of ireland is again surrounded by threats and uncertainties, and the northern ireland assembly has been suspended. in this context, the promotion of peace through the economic and social development of the regions on both sides of ireland, a process which has been exemplaryly carried out at grassroots level by the international fund for ireland, is of increased importance. i therefore believe that the commission should adopt the proposal for a council regulation on community contributions to the international fund for ireland, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. respect for the principles underlying the rules of parliamentary immunity is fundamental to the functioning of a representative democratic institution. for this reason, the decision to waive the parliamentary immunity of a member should be accompanied by the necessary precautions. in the present case, the case is a judicial proceeding concerning conduct unrelated to political activity. i therefore vote in favour of the report.
in writing. the report also calls for the creation of a european network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the environment. as we have already said, the fundamental question is what this instrument will do: - whether it will enhance the value of a country's human resources; - whether it will enable the economically more developed countries to exploit more effectively the human resources of other countries by increasing the 'mobility' of workers. we are rightly concerned that this will lead to an increase in the immigration of technical and scientific staff to the more economically developed countries, and that this will lead to the creation of a european labour market, or even a european 'exchange' of skilled staff. it should be emphasized once again that the documents now proposed already exist as a result of cooperation with the council of europe and/or unesco. that is why we vote in favour of, but are critical of, attempts to undermine apparently positive objectives.
in writing. i congratulate mrs novak on her excellent work on the establishment of the single community framework for the transparency of qualifications and competences - 'europass'. the aim of this project is to create a uniform 'portfolio' of documents which will enable citizens to indicate their personal qualifications in a comparable way throughout the european union when applying for a job or a course. europass will facilitate mobility in europe for professional and learning purposes, which contributes to achieving the objectives of the lisbon strategy. i support the creation of europass, as mobility is an important factor in creating better jobs and reducing the skills gap in the european labour market. i am sure that it will provide the necessary impetus to reduce the obstacles faced by european citizens in this field. i also stress the need not to prolong the legislative process and that is why i voted in favour of europass, which will allow it to enter into force as early as january 2005.
in writing. in the spirit of greater coordination, rationalisation and transparency of qualifications and competences, it is advisable to promote integration into a single framework of measures in the field of certification of qualifications, which does not concern the recognition of diplomas but only the simplification of the procedures for presenting qualifications and competences. that is why i voted in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. the aim of this legislative proposal, which is to create a uniform dossier of documents enabling citizens to indicate their personal aptitudes, skills and qualifications, is to promote the recognition on the labour market of periods of training and traineeship spent abroad, thus stimulating mobility in europe, both in terms of employment and for the purpose of apprenticeship. this project, in addition to encouraging the comparison of qualifications and skills, helps to achieve the lisbon 2000 objectives of making europe the 'most dynamic and competitive economic area in the world' by 2010. the europass, including documents relating to periods of apprenticeship in different countries, higher education qualifications, language skills and vocational training, contributes to a large extent not only to the above objectives but also to the qualitative improvement of general and vocational training in europe. it is a very positive measure of great importance for young people and should enter into force as soon as possible. i voted yes.
mr president, commissioner, seven years is a long time in the world we live in today. since the last financial perspective, the european union has undergone its largest enlargement ever and continued to develop its deepening with the entry into force of the treaty of nice and the signing of the constitutional treaty. in the last seven years, the world has become more globalized and societies more complex and more diverse. attitudes, habits, behaviors and even values have changed. it is therefore essential to adapt the financial perspective to the current political context and to the new realities of the world in which we live. with the decision on the financial perspective we have a unique opportunity to show a more ambitious vision for europe, a winning vision which i think the commission shares. we must therefore avoid at all costs reducing the objective of the financial perspective or the mere exercise of budgetary consolidation, as some seem to be intending. in this connection, i would like the commissioner to comment on three assumptions which i believe are fundamental to the financial perspective. first, the credibility. the political priorities linked to strengthening the competitiveness of the economy and european cohesion must be required to go hand in hand. secondly, the unequivocal statement of a break with previous practices. i am referring to the need to reform the european union's own resources. thirdly, the creation of imaginative solutions, such as making the money in the european union budgets also serve as leverage to mobilise other means from the financial sector, whether public or private.
we consider the commission's proposal for the next financial perspective to be clearly insufficient to respond to the current social, economic and environmental challenges, the needs for economic and social cohesion increased by enlargement, the high levels of unemployment and poverty found in the eu. quantitatively, they propose an average real expenditure of 1.09% of community gni, lower than agenda 2000 (1.10%) and earlier benchmarks; the commission's proposals are based on the principle of subsidiarity, which is the basis for the european union's policy on the environment. in this debate, the question could be asked whether barroso confirms and aggravates prodi, since statements by the commissioners open the door to (re) negotiating downwards the already insufficient package, in line with the signatories of the 'letter of six' who want to impose a 1% ceiling on the community's gni to the budget, which has always deserved our opposition. we therefore want to make clear our rejection of financial perspectives whose annual average expenditure falls between the commission proposal and the ceiling of the 'letter of six', which is continually being brought closer together. finally, we support the maintenance of the financial framework for seven years, since even in this case it seems that the intention is to make the 'negotiation' ... downwards and for less.
mr president, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, the report which mr catania is presenting to us today calls into question the policy of repression and prohibition pursued by the member states. the rapporteur is calling for a change in the current strategy and it will not surprise anyone that we vote against this report. mr catania referred to the report of the european monitoring centre for drugs and drug addiction. mr estievenart was with us last month and he pointed out that, and i quote, 'there are positive signs of progress in reducing some of the most serious consequences of drug use'. he stressed that the number of drug-related deaths was beginning to fall. it noted that heroin use had stabilised in several countries, that the hiv epidemic among users had slowed down and, quote 'at the same time, it stressed that measures to reduce the harms associated with drug use had been stepped up and that users' access to treatment and complementary care had been increased. " this clearly shows that not everything was negative. there is still a lot to be done and despite all the policies we have been developing, there are still huge problems with the production and trafficking of drugs and with the consumption which continues to reach very high levels in all the member states. in the context of enlargement to the ten new member states, it is essential to intensify cooperation with the new border states. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, there is room for a european policy to combat drugs, a policy which prevents associated crime and which, as it is in the programme, meets the four major objectives: the prevention of drug use and dependence, the reduction of the supply of and demand for illicit drugs, the limitation of social and health damage and the reduction of crime. this is the path to which we are called. it's the path of combat, not the path of ease.

as well as a further strengthening of policy areas that are of crucial importance for effective action by the european union on the challenges facing the world of today and tomorrow. the fifth round secure communications link with europol has been established. member states will exchange information from criminal records, europol and eurojust will be better informed by member states concerning november, which in the coming years will contribute substantially to the fight against terrorism. this does not mean, however, that we can sit back – on the contrary! the eu remains vulnerable and there is still much work to be done in implementing the eu action plan. in the next six months the eu will therefore continue its efforts. the multiannual strategic programme 2004-2006 issued a clear mandate to the netherlands presidency to take a decision on principles and guidelines in order to enable the eu to achieve political agreement on the financial perspectives by june 2005. six months of intense discussions under the netherlands presidency have resulted in clear principles and guidelines. they provide for a framework for the council to reach a general political agreement. the principles and guidelines will be accompanied by an elaborate progress report, which constitutes an overview of the positions of member states based on the legislative proposals, communications and further technical clarifications by the commission. an important part of this report is the 'building blocks', which have provided a useful structure for the discussions and have contributed to the process of moving towards a consensus according to the established time frame. the result of this approach is an analysis and a clear picture of the positions of member states in relation to policy content and financial implications. considering the work done and results achieved under the netherlands presidency, progress as scheduled should be within reach. we now pass the baton on to luxembourg, which will continue the discussion in a spirit of mutual understanding directed at finding a consensus acceptable to every member state. in this respect, let me also reiterate here that the important role of the european parliament in reaching an agreement with the council on the next multiannual financial framework is understood by all, and appropriate language will be included in the council's conclusions. at the european council meeting the eu drugs strategy 2005-2012 will be adopted. the strategy will be a key instrument to confront drug use and trafficking effectively with a view to ensuring a high level of health protection, wellbeing and social cohesion, as well as a high level of security for the general public. the strategy is based on a balanced approach towards supply and demand reduction. the commission will be requested to present an action plan based on this strategy for 2005-2008 to the council and the european parliament as soon as possible. i look forward to close cooperation with parliament in this area. the european council will welcome the progress made under the netherlands presidency in the field of immigration and integration. common basic principles for immigrant integration policy within the european union have been established. moreover, the need for common basic principles on integration, clear goals and means of evaluation mechanisms, and greater coordination of national integration policies and eu initiatives in this field is also underlined in the hague programme. in the field of external relations the european council will discuss four issues. first, we will address the situation in ukraine. i am glad that the parties concerned have reached an agreement on reform of the election laws and on a modification of the constitution. we have seen that these changes have brought the ukrainians a little closer to each other. we should now focus all our attention on the election process; because our goal remains free and fair elections, without external interference, where the ukrainian people can be certain that the election results reflect their will. that is also the best way to guarantee the absence of violence and to maintain the territorial integrity of ukraine. the second subject to be discussed is the middle east peace process. of course, in the short term attention will have to go primarily to the preparations for the palestinian presidential elections. but we should also keep in mind the longer-term perspective. therefore, we must ensure that the short-term actions fit into the framework of the road map, because both the israelis and the palestinians should return to the road map in order to be able to realise the long-term, final goal of a two-state solution. thirdly, the european security strategy was adopted a year ago and the european council will mark that. in the area of key threats and increasing the security in our common neighbourhood, the eu has achieved quite a lot. examples include our efforts in the field of non-proliferation vis-à-vis iran, and also the support package for iraq that we were able to offer prime minister allawi at the november european council. meanwhile, a number of challenges remain, for example the situation in darfur. for the implementation of the security strategy, relations with the us remain of vital importance and therefore ministers will discuss how we can further strengthen our transatlantic relationship. fourthly, the european council will also have a discussion with kofi annan, who will elaborate on a number of elements of the high-level panel's report. government leaders will then have an exchange of views with him, especially about the threats and challenges of our time and the millennium development goals, also in view of the major un event in 2005. the european council will endorse a number of conclusions adopted by the ministers for development cooperation in november. in general the european council will emphasise that the official development assistance of the european community needs to contribute in a coherent way to poverty eradication in all developing countries. the european council will also underline that the focus on the poorest should be increased, in particular in africa. the european council will also discuss the un high-level event in september 2005, when the world community will take stock of progress made towards the achievement of the millennium development goals. apart from the main themes on the agenda of the european council, other issues to be addressed are commonly shared values, consular cooperation, the eu human rights agency and the european external action service. on commonly shared values, the european council will note with approval the series of public debates hosted by the netherlands presidency, engaging participants with wide-ranging backgrounds and experience on the european identity and the concept of commonly shared values as the foundation of european integration and cooperation. on consular cooperation, the european council will confirm the commitments of the european union to intensify consular cooperation among member states. closer consular cooperation gives substance to the concept of european citizenship and helps member states to deal more effectively with an ever-growing demand for consular services and to face new challenges, such as the consequences of an increasing number of terrorist activities, including bomb attacks and hostage-takings. with a view to enhancing the coherence and consistency of eu human rights policy, the european council is expected to call for effective follow-up to the december 2003 decision to establish an eu human rights agency. on the european external action service, the european council will invite the secretary-general/high representative, together with the commission, to prepare a progress report on this preparatory work and to take appropriate steps to keep the european parliament informed. the netherlands presidency has made it its duty to ensure smooth and efficient cooperation between the commission, the council and parliament to make it possible to deliver on the issues to be discussed at the european council meeting. on 21 december prime minister balkenende will brief you on the outcome of the meeting. commission. mr president, the forthcoming european council in brussels will be the first for the new commission. it will be an important meeting, marking the next steps in the process of building a larger, more prosperous and safer european union. it will be a sign of our ambition for a union which is dynamic and on the move; a union ready to share its destiny with the european family; a union which is concerned about the security of its citizens. i would hope that the spirit coming out of the european council later this week is one of cooperation. how else can we generate the trust in europe’s institutions and politicians that is needed for a smooth ratification of the constitution? we have heard from the presidency about its expectations and the issues that the summit will address. let me comment briefly on three issues: enlargement, the fight against terrorism and the financial perspectives. firstly, our policy of enlargement of the union has been the key in freeing us from our cold war past. the gravitational pull of the prospect of eu membership has transformed and modernised several post-communist societies. it has thus reshaped the european order. this was and remains an achievement of historic proportions that we should not underestimate. your house has been instrumental in supporting this process, but our enlargement is still incomplete. this european council will take the next steps for four countries, offering them the potential – through enlargement – to join the european mainstream. last october the commission made it clear that it should be possible to conclude the accession negotiations with bulgaria and romania in 2004. indeed, this negotiating process was closed yesterday, thanks to the increased efforts by the european union and by these two countries. i congratulate the netherlands presidency for its excellent work and close cooperation with the commission on that particular subject. the accession treaty for both countries now needs to be finalised and we hope that it can be signed after receiving the assent of this house during the spring of next year. in the remaining period up to accession, the commission will be watching closely to see that both countries deliver on the commitments made during the negotiations, and in some cases this will mean a further acceleration in their efforts. at the request of the european council, on 6 october the commission adopted its report on turkey and a clear recommendation. the main message in the commission’s assessment is that turkey has sufficiently fulfilled the copenhagen political criteria and that accession negotiations should now be opened. we consider this recommendation, which was very carefully prepared, to be well balanced and a good basis for a decision by the council. i am looking forward to taking comfort from the position your house will take on this question later today. turkey has made further progress in the last weeks. it has adopted five of the six pieces of legislation signalled by the commission in its report; the sixth law, on the execution of sentences, is pending before the turkish parliament. it is now time for the european council to honour its commitment to turkey and announce the opening of accession negotiations. a clear date should be indicated. we consider that, apart from the matters i have just mentioned, no other conditions ought to be added. the european council will no doubt wish to recall that political reforms will have to continue in the course of the negotiations and ask the commission to monitor further progress closely. we should also ask our turkish friends in all honesty: if you want to become a member of a club, is it not normal that you recognise the other members of the club? i am convinced that this will come at the right moment in the course of this difficult process, and preferably sooner than later. the objective of starting negotiations cannot be other than accession but we accept that the accession process is open-ended and its outcome cannot be guaranteed beforehand. as in the past, transitional arrangements and certain specific safeguards may need to be considered. but let me state what our ultimate challenge will be: in the end, we need not only to overcome diplomatic obstacles, but also to conquer the hearts and minds of european citizens on this issue. croatia represents the first of the western balkan nations preparing to start the process for accession to the union. the commission is ready to support the launch of such negotiations, but believes that any progress should be conditional on increased cooperation between the croatian government and the international criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia. if such cooperation is confirmed, then negotiations can be started in 2005.

mr president, of the various subjects to be discussed at the next european council, apart from turkey, which we have already mentioned on other occasions, the fight against terrorism continues to assume enormous importance. the evaluation of the dutch presidency's action programme of june 2004 is proof of this. in the face of a threat to all, the most appropriate strategy is one that leads us to act together, going beyond the national level and even into the areas of justice and internal security. in fact, the way we deal with terrorism today is nothing like the way it was dealt with in the '70s and '80s. the events of 11 september 2001 brought about a radical change in security, confronting european countries with new responsibilities and new challenges, the urgency and seriousness of which was confirmed by 11 march. in a globalised world, politics, diplomacy, information, internal security and defence must complement each other to respond to these new types of threats. security has become a global and indivisible concept which today combines internal and external security, including support for third countries in the fight against terrorism. the european union and its member states have an obligation to rationalise their defence capabilities and to strengthen the means of diplomatic cooperation, intelligence services and judicial and police coordination, in a genuine synergy of national and transnational policies. as a portuguese member of parliament, i would like to stress that my government - then headed by mr barroso, now president of the commission - has transposed all the community legislation on the fight against terrorism and has taken the necessary operational measures to implement it. in this context, too, it is worth noting the option, which has just been taken up by the european parliament, of introducing biometric data in passports. as long as it is accompanied by the necessary precautions, this measure represents a strengthening of the mechanisms for preventing crime and thus of the strengthening of the security of citizens, which is our first objective. the various speeches on this subject in the run-up to the european council show that parliament wants to send a clear signal that this is the path which we must continue to pursue together without breaking.

in writing. i voted in favour of opening the eu accession process for turkey, which does not imply deciding on the final outcome of that process, which will take years to negotiate. and i voted against a partnership statute, because that would mean that the eu would not honour its promises. i voted in favour, mainly because of the testimony of numerous turkish human rights defenders who confirmed that there were positive developments in the situation in turkey. clearly, these developments are not enough: there are still political prisoners, torture in prisons and much more to be done. but a breakdown in the process of opening negotiations at this stage would have disastrous consequences for the human rights situation in turkey. i voted in favour, although there has been no serious reflection on where and how far europe should go. because i reject the political and cultural boundaries of the 'christian club of europe' and the prophecies of a 'clash of civilizations'. i voted in favour, on the assumption that turkey cannot delay the recognition of the republic of cyprus, which is a member of the eu, nor the withdrawal of the part it occupies militarily. i voted in favour of turkey's recognition of the genocide of the armenian people, because i consider it essential for reconciliation with its neighbours and with its history.

in writing. the proposal is to reform community legislation on pesticides by replacing the four existing directives with a single regulation. at the same time, it is intended to secure some fundamental objectives, such as establishing a uniform level of consumer protection throughout the community, in particular by defining the role of the european food safety authority (efsa), and increasing food trade within the european union. i believe that important steps have been taken from the first to the second reading, in particular by the adoption by the council of amendments proposed by the european parliament and also by the introduction of amendments on its own initiative which have frankly improved the commission's initial proposal. i believe, however, that there are still aspects which can be clarified, in particular the distinction between residues (in the context of maximum residue limits) and pesticides. on the other hand, i also agree with the rapporteur that situations where mrls are exceeded should entail consequences for those responsible and that subgroups likely to consume a higher amount of a given type of product should be protected.

in writing. the tangential approval of this report by the committee indicates that the rapporteur has departed from the european strategy to combat drugs by proposing an approach to the problem which, in my view, not only does not solve it but aggravates it. in fact, it is no longer new in this house to try to present the liberalisation of consumption, the absolutization of the idea of harm reduction and the adoption of a speech of surrender in the face of trafficking as solutions. this practice has a long history and is still commonly associated with the effort to impose it on the member states, in direct conflict with the principle of subsidiarity, which must continue to apply to this matter, despite the need for coordination in the fight against trafficking. the proposed laxity and decriminalisation are known forms of disempowerment of public authorities and are a false ally of those whose will and decision-making capacity are diminished by the effect of drugs, and are a profoundly wrong signal to the younger generations. it is ironic that the rapporteur invokes fundamental rights and claims to oppose an 'ideological approach' to this issue in order to justify an eminently ideological position, which is, in fact, contrary to basic fundamental rights.

question no 2 by antonio lópez-istúriz white (h-0420/04) subject: relations between the eu and the european region of the pyrenees and the mediterranean on 29 october, the european region pyrenees-mediterranean (catalonia, aragon, the balearic islands, the southern pyrenees and languedoc-roussillon) was established as an area for cooperation between regions, particularly in the fields of railway, aeronautical, logistics, innovation and research infrastructures, with the ambition of opening its doors to new regions. the european region will have no political content, since this is foreign to the very concept of the new legal entity created, whose efforts are aimed at the cooperation already mentioned. in this connection, can the council indicate what role the european union will recognize in this european region and, more specifically, what participation it will be granted in the context of community policies? in addition, can the council indicate what management and control capacity will be allocated to the european pyrenees-mediterranean region in respect of community funds earmarked for and to be used for regional promotion and development?

question no 10 by ewa hedkvist petersen (h-0438/04) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: driving under the influence of alcohol there was a tragic accident in sweden recently where a heavily intoxicated lorry driver who had just left the ferry in trelleborg drove off the rails, killing five people in two cars travelling in the opposite direction. different approaches to the alcohol problem and different rates of alcoholism in different european countries make it more difficult to solve the problem of drunken drivers and to prosecute them. this is particularly true in the context of international traffic. in 2001, on a proposal from the eu commission, the council of ministers decided to recommend that member states introduce a maximum alcohol content of 0.2 g/l for professional drivers. the recommendation was adopted in place of a directive on a common maximum limit for the alcohol content of road traffic. to date, which countries have applied this ceiling? will the council assess its recommendation and what results at community level have been achieved from the observance of the limits set out in the recommendation?
question no 11 by mr nikolaos vakalis (h-0441/04) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: exclusion of public expenditure on research from the calculation of the maximum authorized government deficit the eu's ambition to become the most competitive economy in the world (the lisbon agenda) requires a significant increase in the allocations for european research policy. research expenditure is strategic for the eu in that it is an investment in its survival in a highly competitive international environment. however, statements about this ambitious european research policy are hardly compatible with the restrictions imposed by the stability and development pact, which prohibits member states from increasing public expenditure beyond 3% of gdp. in order to encourage member states to make available 1% of gdp for public funding of research policy, i believe that this amount should not be taken into account in calculating the 3% of gdp limit imposed by the stability pact. does the council agree that public expenditure on research is a strategic expenditure of high priority for the eu and that as such it is justified to exclude it from the criteria of the pact? the argument that such a decision will set a precedent for a number of other exceptions (e.g. military expenditure) is not tenable given that the strengthening of research is a planned european strategic objective without any analogy with other national or european objectives.

commission. mr president, i thank mr ribeiro for his report on the proposal to protect deep-water coral reefs from the effects of trawling in certain areas of the atlantic ocean. this is the first time i have addressed the plenary of this parliament and it is satisfying that the first proposal that i am dealing with is focused upon the protection of deep-water coral reefs – an issue of great importance to us all. doubtless, we will have many an occasion in future, both within this plenary and within the committee on fisheries, to discuss issues not only relating to conservation and the preservation of fish stocks but also relating to issues such as deep-water coral reefs. having studied the scientific evidence and considering the irreversible damage that certain fishing gear can cause to these unique habitats, we propose in this regulation to ban the use of bottom trawls and similar trawl gear in the areas concerned. with this proposal, we fulfil the commitment given at the fisheries council of 23 october 2003, when the new 'western waters' regulation was approved to ensure protection for these habitats. i am happy to note that the rapporteur recommends that parliament approve these measures, as does the committee on the environment, public health and food safety in its opinion. the commission welcomes the adoption of measures to minimise the impact of fishing on marine ecosystems. they show our determination to work for the integration of environmental concerns in the common fisheries policy, as envisaged in the reform of 2002, and as repeatedly called for by public opinion. i turn briefly to the amendments proposed in the report before us. i can accept amendments 1, 2 and 3. however, i have difficulty in accepting amendment 4, since it is not in line with the legislation on the mandate that is given to regional advisory councils. these councils are to be consulted on the development of proposals for legislation, but consultation of them is not envisaged on the implementation of such legislation. as for amendment 5, the commission has difficulty accepting the substance of this amendment as it is currently worded. the commission is bound to review all proposals in the light of new scientific evidence. hence, obliging the commission to do so in a specific timeframe could also work against the spirit and purpose of the proposal. furthermore, we need to be conscious of the fact that the production of scientific evidence is very much dependent on the member states and, therefore, the commission is not in a position to guarantee its availability as prescribed in the amendment, that is, within a specified timeframe. on amendment 6, the commission notes that while it could find such an amendment acceptable, it is not really necessary since the geographical application of the regulation is well known and already established. as for amendment 7, in accordance with scientific advice, the main threat to the very fragile deep-water habitats is bottom trawling. damage caused by other gear, in particular specific gear such as gillnets and longlines, may be real, but is very minor compared to the erosion effects of trawls. furthermore, extending the prohibition on trawling throughout the european economic zone would appear to be excessive, i.e. would appear not to be proportionate since the majority of this area does not have submarine features threatened by fishing. in these circumstances, the commission is not in a position to accept amendment 7. finally, the commission has difficulty accepting amendment 8, because it would create a duplication of effort. comprehensive revisions of the status of deep-water features are currently being carried out by the international council for the exploitation of the sea, ices. this is considered to be sufficient.
the rapporteur. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: the preparation, discussion and vote in committee of this report was an almost surprising process of learning, illustrating that one is always in time to learn, to learn always. an activity that i only knew superficially, i confronted and above all enriched everything that, in theory, the papers and the study could provide us. by contacting and informing myself of those who are connected with the activity, those who make their living from it, those who study it in depth and seriously, those who have responsibilities in it, i have learned a lot, and i know that much remains to be learned. i have been asked three questions, starting from the need to protect the environment which was under attack and was in danger of being attacked more. what predatory activities should be moderated or prohibited? to what extent? under what jurisdiction? after much listening and much reflection, i became convinced that a ban on bottom trawling would be insufficient to protect coral reefs and other formations where i survey the hot springs. i've been proven that the art of bottom-dwelling is just as predatory or even more so. that's why i explicitly included it. why the resistance to this inclusion? why do powerful interests use it? because, the commission argues, there will be insufficient scientific evidence to prove the harmfulness of this art. however, if that were the case, the precautionary principle should be used. the delimitation of the areas to be protected is defined in the commission proposal by the criterion of degrees of longitude and latitude. i regard this option as political rather than technical, at least not only technical and with a strong political significance. the non-use of the criterion of miles from the coast serves to disregard or to minimize the link to national exclusive economic zones as something to be forgotten. after the negotiation of the regulatory replacement after the period which ended in november 2003, from 200 to 12 then to 50 to reach 100 miles, the failure in the commission proposal to take account of the situation created in the 100 to 200 mile zone is, in my view, serious and must be corrected. which brings us to the key issue of jurisdiction. firstly, the mere omission of the national jurisdictions of spain and portugal, which was not omitted in the previous proposal when it came to the jurisdiction of the united kingdom over the formation of the darwin mounds reefs off the coast of scotland. does this mean that the united kingdom is being given a jurisdiction which is being denied or forgotten or hidden for spain and portugal? this leads to the truly delicate and fundamental questions that life imposes when confronted with the concrete. before the ratification of the constitutional treaty, this proposal completes the principle of the european union's exclusive competence for the conservation of marine biological resources. this decision is highly controversial and we find it unacceptable, since it replaces national and regional competence over part of the national territory, even though it is covered by community competence and has exclusive status. the balance between exploitation and conservation is obviously at stake. this balance was achieved when fishing was not industrial and predatory and the conservation of marine biological resources was under national and regional jurisdiction, and its replacement is therefore not justified by the need to correct incorrect or lax practices. (iii) there are two types of fishing, coastal fishing and, more or less, or even semi-artisanal and industrial fishing, the former being penalized, with serious social consequences and regional economies, by the predatory nature of the latter, which, due to its economic and political power, will continue its activity more readily; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. my report and the amendments which i tabled in the plenary to reaffirm it have the intention which i have tried to make clear in this speech, awaiting the vote of this house. i am grateful for that vote and i am very grateful for all the help and cooperation i have had in putting this report forward.
