in writing. i voted in favour of this report because of the importance of fisheries for portugal, particularly in the case of international fisheries agreements in which portuguese fishermen have a direct interest. i would also like to support my vote by saying that the question is one of extending the existing protocol and that the proposed amendments do not in any way prejudice national interests.
in writing. the period covered is the period between the expiry of the protocol to the fisheries agreement between the european community and the islamic federal republic of the comoros and the date on which the commission considers that it has carried out the assessments necessary for the renegotiation of the agreement. the proposed solution, given the significant activity of the community fleet in this sea area (40 tuna seiners and 25 surface longliners), is to extend the previous agreement until a new fisheries protocol is concluded. the extension does not imply any change in the terms and restrictions of the previous protocol, and the financial compensation and fishing opportunities available to ms are maintained. given that the portuguese fleet maintains fishing opportunities for 5 surface longliners in that area, it is important for portugal to support this extension and to ensure a favourable renegotiation of the agreement. i voted yes.
in writing. i welcome the decision to allow full application of article 67 of the treaty, so that qualified majority voting and codecision can be used for title iv matters such as immigration, asylum, crossing borders, etc. we have gained efficiency, we have strengthened the role of this parliament, guaranteeing the principle of democratic legitimacy, which is fundamental for the adoption of rules on such sensitive matters as asylum and immigration policy and others involving the fundamental rights of citizens. i support mr bourlanges' report and the two specific proposals he makes to us, because: - codecision and qualified majority voting in legal immigration matters are essential for the management of the union's migration policy. the signing of the constitution on 29 october 2004 ensured that the measures provided for in the field of legal immigration should not affect the right of member states to determine the volumes of admission of third-country nationals to their territory to seek work there. - the limitations on the jurisdiction of the court in title iv, introduced in amsterdam because of fears of overloading and excessive delays, also make no sense, since article 225a was introduced in nice... (short explanation of vote pursuant to rule 163 (1))
in writing. the rapporteur wanted to propose that the court of justice should have its jurisdiction extended by the repeal of article 68 tec - an addition to the proposal for a council decision to the effect that various areas of title iv, part iii of the tec (visas, asylum, immigration and other policies relating to the free movement of persons) should be governed by article 251 tec. as i have said on other occasions, i think it is better for the union to gradually consolidate skills and practices rather than seek to feed a continuous glut of skills. the whole proposal is a sensitive subject and the report is full of the sick maximalism of a centrifugal europe, without any popular support for this approach. i am not sure that the proposed repeal will in any way strengthen the legal protection of european citizens and of third countries, as mr bourlanges claims. i'm rather of the exact opposite belief. and i think that the european parliament would do better to simply support the proposal for a decision as it has been put forward - which in itself represents an important and ambitious step forward in the area of freedom, security and justice - and to resist embarking on this sickly fear of the 'beyond'.
in writing. the subject of the commission proposal, which the rapporteur supports, to maintain until the end of 2006 a legal basis and a financial framework for operations to defend and promote human rights and democratic principles in developing countries and other third countries, deserved my vote in favour because i consider that such maintenance, when matters of major importance in terms of the community's external policy are at stake, is of utmost utility and is fully justified.
in writing. community funding under this regulation takes the form of grants or contracts, which the european commission proposes should also be extended, in duly justified cases, to legal persons, which i also agree with. the participation of civil society should be supported, regardless of the institutionalised nature underlying it in each case. it is imperative that the union pursue, improve and intensify the path set out in the commission communication of 8 may 2001 entitled 'the role of the european union in promoting human rights and democratisation in third countries'. the european union is seen by many as the last window of hope. as the afet committee (with only one abstention) has shown, the european initiative for democracy and human rights (eidhr) must therefore use all possible instruments in its aspirations, focusing primarily on support for democratisation, good governance and the rule of law. i would like to refer to the speech i made yesterday in the plenary debate. i naturally voted in favour.
in writing. natural disasters such as floods, heat waves, forest fires, earthquakes, ecological disasters caused by toxic waste, toxic industrial accidents, serious industrial accidents and terrorist attacks are highly unpredictable and, for this reason, cause numerous victims and considerable economic damage. it is important to know and exchange experiences, to rationalise resources, to investigate and seek technical solutions to minimise the impacts caused, but above all, it is important to focus on a policy of investment in prevention and education, involving community, national, regional and local political institutions and all civil society organisations in a solidarity, responsible and differentiated partnership. the people, in their immense wisdom, say that 'prevention is better than cure', which is perfectly applicable to the case of the forest fires that ravaged portugal in the summers of 2003 and 2004 and the case of the oil spill by the prestige and erika oil tankers. we welcome the extension of the community action programme in the field of civil protection and its budgetary increase, but we also believe that this is a matter in which there should be no time limit because of its permanent nature. civil protection also involves the definition of a transversal policy: based on new models of agriculture and spatial planning that humanize urban and industrial growth... (the minutes were approved)
in writing. i congratulate mr papadimoulis on the excellent report he has produced on the proposal for a council decision amending decision 1999/847/ec as regards the extension for two years of the community action programme in the field of civil protection. the aim is to ensure continuity in this area until the date of entry into force of a new legal instrument. this programme aims to strengthen the protection of citizens, the environment and property in the event of natural or technological disasters throughout the community by providing additional assistance from the other participating countries when national response capacity is insufficient. since the adoption of this programme, its effectiveness and the need for action at european level have been demonstrated, notably during the prestige disaster and the fires in the summer of 2003. the report also highlights seven areas where the programme could be improved, notably in terms of cooperation, exchange of information and increased resources. i also support the need to increase the annual budget of this programme to eur 2.4 million per year (in 2005 and 2006).
in writing. given that the community's civil protection programme currently in force expires on 31 december this year, and that it is useful that there should be a gap between this date and the start of the next legal instrument, i consider it advantageous to extend the current programme for two years, although i regret that the programme will be extended without the necessary evaluations of the 2000/2004 period having been carried out. the financial reinforcement which the commission is asking for is realistic and is particularly important in the case of portugal. for the reasons i have given, i am voting in favour.
in writing. several events, such as the prestige accident, the forest fires - particularly in my country - and the floods in southern france have highlighted the need for action at european level. the scale of certain disasters often exceeds national response capacity, and the provision of mechanisms such as the one created by the current programme at european level is increasingly justified. the proposal goes in that direction, providing for an increase from eur 1.5 million (in 2004) to eur 2.4 million per year (in 2005 and 2006). i support this development, which is part of the reinforcement of cooperation in the field of civil protection, to which the european union began responding in the first community action programme in the field of civil protection adopted in 1997, and which had as another highlight, for major disasters, the creation of the solidarity fund in november 2002. the european information and surveillance centre is very important, as it allows member states or third countries to send requests for assistance. a permanent network of contacts within the commission is thus established to ensure uninterrupted links between the civil protection centres of the participating states and to promote the sharing of information.
in writing. the commission proposal provides for a ban on the use of bottom trawls in certain areas including the most sensitive seamounts from the point of view of their habitat within the 200 miles of the aar, the ram and the canary islands. similar restrictions already exist in an area in the northwest of scotland. 1.1 i believe that further progress should be made towards a ban on the use of bottom-set gillnets. indeed, such networks also cause serious problems for ecosystems, which are aggravated in the azores eez by the volcanic and rocky nature of its seabed. there are several studies that confirm the sensitivity of deep-sea habitats, such as deep-sea coral reefs, hydrothermal vents and fisheries of seabeds and seamounts.
in writing. i fully support the european commission's proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 850/98 of 30 march 1998 on the protection of deep-sea coral reefs against the effects of drift in certain areas of the atlantic ocean (com (2004) 58 final). i welcome the european commission for presenting this proposal, because it fulfils its promise to propose an amendment to the technical measures in force in the community to prohibit trawl fishing up to at least 200 miles around the outermost regions of the azores, madeira and the canary islands, with the aim of protecting the ecosystems of some of the most sensitive areas located in the 'seamounts' outside the 100 miles. the deep-sea habitats targeted in the commission proposal were until recently protected from trawling (the use of bottom trawls or similar towed nets operating in contact with the seabed) thanks to the special access regime resulting from the accession negotiations. however, this scheme ceased to apply in august 2004 and it was essential to ensure the continuity of protection of these areas under community legislation.
in writing. the protection of deep-sea coral reefs in the atlantic ocean is obviously of particular interest to portugal. the proposal is to prohibit the use of trawls in the waters of the azores and madeira (and also the canary islands) in order to protect deep-sea coral reefs, which are of great importance for the conservation of biodiversity. it is estimated that 65 percent of fish species in these areas depend on these reefs at some point in their lives. given this need for effective protection, the extension of the ban on bottom trawling is to be defended, since it also causes serious problems for these ecosystems due to the loss of nets (ghost fishing). in this context, and although i am not satisfied with the final result of the vote on the amendments, i consider the result achieved by this report to be very positive and have therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation provides for a ban on the use of bottom trawls in the most sensitive environmental zones within the first 200 nautical miles of the azores, madeira and the canary islands. i support the measures proposed in general and i also consider it essential that the specific features of each area be properly taken into account. i therefore also supported the amendment proposals to include fixed bottom trawls in the proposed prohibitions, and i deeply regret that this measure was not included in the final version of the committee, contrary to the rapporteur's recommendation. i have therefore been working with a number of colleagues to get it back up and approved by the house. in fact, it is known that these types of networks are highly damaging to ecosystems, mainly because of the high probability of network loss situations. and in the specific case of the azores, this risk is further enhanced by the volcanic nature of the seabed. so it made no sense to leave the protection halfway.
in writing. another resolution in which the parliamentary groups of the ps, psd and cds-pp, using language full of mystifications and sometimes omissions, reaffirm - together! - their options and the fundamental axes of the european union - neoliberalism, federalism and militarism. and it is not surprising that they reaffirm - all of them together! - the 'promotion of increased competitiveness' as their 'top priority' - or, more precisely, of capitalist competition - their support for the 'lisbon strategy' - following the example of the big employers in europe - 'the improvement of labour markets' - the cynical name for the attack on workers' rights - 'the reform of pension schemes' - that is, their progressive privatisation - 'the completion of the single market' - or rather, the liberalisation of energy, transport and telecommunications - among many other examples... a 'good' package wrapped in language with social concerns and good intentions, which seeks to hide the contradictions and the true essence of right-wing politics actually carried out at eu level, as well as its very serious consequences. the socialist party, the socialist party and the cds-pp may try to conceal or hide their broad understanding, but the reality is that they are being exposed. let us not forget him in portugal on 20 february.
in writing. i voted in favour of the compromise resolution on the commission's political guidelines, with particular reference to the pact on economic, social and territorial cohesion policies. as i have said many times, i consider cohesion policy to be a guiding principle and a fundamental cornerstone of the european union as a whole, without which it would lose its meaning. without cohesion policies, the union would be nothing more than a 'hyper-market' and an instrument of subordination to the big and dominant players in all areas. the principle of cohesion, as the founding principle of the union, is, moreover, a fundamentally christian-democratic concept. the left's adherence to this understanding is welcome. but we cannot abandon the left in the affirmation and defence of the principles that are ours. in other words, the development of competitiveness is necessary, but not to destroy cohesion, but to make it stronger.
, in writing. as we have been saying, the economic/political objectives of the present enlargement are clear, as expressed once again in the resolution we have just voted. the resolution whitewashes the implementation of neoliberal policy as a criterion and background for eu membership, although it refers to the idolized "functioning market economy", i.e. capitalism and the domination and exploitation by large financial and economic groups of an increasingly significant part of the country's economy. as the 'foreign direct investment' report says, which some say is reaching 'record levels', this means that the large foreign financial groups are increasingly dominating the bulgarian economy. the 'applause' for bulgaria's efforts is contrary to the objectives of the eu. economic and social cohesion is not built on the basis of competition and the movement of capital in pursuit of the most unrestrained exploitation. these, while leaving behind the trail of unemployment and poverty - as exemplified by the relocations of companies from portugal - do not create real wealth in the country to which they relocate. the resolution itself states that many people do not feel any improvement in their economic situation and that emigration continues.
in writing. as the commission and the report in question have pointed out, bulgaria has made the necessary progress towards accession to the european union, particularly in the economic and judicial fields, although it must be recognised that, among other equally important issues, there is a need to combat crime, corruption and trafficking in human beings more effectively. in this context, and considering that the reforms still under way can be developed in time, i am in favour of the idea that bulgaria should accede on its own merits, and for this reason i believe that the accession treaty should be concluded in 2005 so that accession can take place in january 2007. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. the report, which follows on from the previous ones, assesses the progress made in a perspective which defines the neoliberal capitalist nature of the enlargement processes. the criteria to be met and the progress made are presented in more or less detail, criticisms are made and praise is given so that, in the end, these countries define and are ever closer to adopting and implementing a legal/institutional framework - the so-called 'community acquis' - which underpins the neoliberal model of the eu. the spirit of the advocates of this policy is so great that they do not hesitate to put forward proposals in a clear attempt to settle accounts with the history of the peoples' struggle, and thus for the thousandth time there is the fraudulent adulation of the 'market economy', of 'structural reforms' in the framework of 'competition' and 'market forces', of 'bringing the privatisation process to a successful conclusion' and of 'dismantling unviable enterprises' and of 'creating an environment favourable to foreign enterprises and investment'. the demands are constantly being reaffirmed, even if accompanied by the hypocritical lamentation of their grave consequences for the workers and peoples.
in writing. in february 2004, the european parliament adopted a report lamenting that, despite some progress, romania still did not fully meet the copenhagen criteria. however, as this year draws to a close, the general view is that some progress has been made towards accession, although it is also recognised that there are still many areas where this objective is not fully achieved. it therefore makes perfect sense to try to negotiate the terms of the treaty in 2005 and to leave a safeguard clause in case romania's actual accession has to be delayed until january 2008. which, by the way, seems likely. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i hope that romania will be able to conclude the negotiations with a view to signing the treaty of accession to the european union as soon as possible. i consider the rapporteur's recommendations and warnings to be very important, and i understand the importance of the romanian authorities and people being aware of the most serious contingencies of the accession process. i would remind you in particular that specific safeguard clauses may be applied in the event of serious non-compliance and that there is a risk that accession could be postponed for one year if the application of the acquis and compliance with the copenhagen political criteria are in question. i believe, however, that these warnings are only meaningful if they serve to encourage merit and performance and never to set standards that are impossible, too high. i particularly agree with the rapporteur's idea that the commission should set up a permanent mechanism of close monitoring and assistance which could help romania along this path and i think it is essential that the commission should continue to keep the european parliament fully informed of the progress of the process leading to romania's accession. the adoption of the report is particularly timely, after the way the presidential elections in romania were concluded last sunday.
on behalf of the group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, zimbabwe is unfortunately one of the regulars, one of the most frequent visitors to our debates on thursdays on the urgency of human rights. this says two things: it says the persisting seriousness of the situation and it also says the ineffectiveness of the measures we have taken. what we must condemn, of course, is the ruin of a country and a people deliberately promoted by an evil and authoritarian regime. as has been mentioned here, the poverty statistics are increasingly impressive and zimbabwe was a country that could not only feed all its people but even help solve problems of hunger and deprivation in the african continent or other parts of the world if it was properly managed. but the mugabe regime, despite international and european union warnings, continues to aggravate political oppression and we look with great concern to the elections announced for march. either you can quickly bring about some transformations and minimally serious conditions of debate in the country or these elections will not be free and fair and it is doubtful that they are worth even observing. it is the case of roy bennette, the case of the persecution of tsvangirai after he visited us here, it is also - and i would like to draw your attention to this - the very negative influence that this regime can have in the region where the future of democratic regimes or of regresses to authoritarianism is also at stake. for example, i was recently in mozambique, which held elections (the results are still being finalised) but we learned that the election campaign, that mozambican voters were voting abroad and that opposition parties were being suppressed in zimbabwe, the parties opposing frelimo. so there are conditions. the fate of zimbabwe can decisively influence the consolidation of democracy in the region, as we hope, following the example of south africa, and thus consolidating democratic aspirations in mozambique and angola, or it can, on the contrary, represent a return to forms of authoritarianism. i would like to call for increased pressure on neighbouring countries and for more dialogue with the african union, signifying the importance of the african union and also of exerting its forms of pressure on the evil mugabe regime.
on behalf of the group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the situation in the great lakes and in particular in the democratic republic of congo is a wound, a volcano in the heart of africa, which is unfortunately always ready to explode. after a conflict that has caused three million deaths over six years but which, according to the international rescue committee, still causes 31,000 deaths every month, there are signs that the situation remains unstable and unfortunately extremely erratic. the joint parliamentary assembly of the acp states recently met in the hague and, interestingly, our meeting opened with good news - the news of the dar es salaam conference and the commitment made by all the heads of state there that the conflicts had ended - but on thursday, when we closed the meeting, our co-chair, glenys kinnock, gave us the sad news: the rwandan army had crossed the borders and entered the democratic republic of congo. so we need to be more effective in this area to stabilize the region. i appreciate the image of mr posselt comparing the situation with the thirty years' war and i hope he is right because it means that this conflict will end and that these regions of the african continent will be prosperous, stable and modern as germany is today. that's what drives us. and to stabilize the african continent in open and democratic societies. what do we have to do here? we must recognize that we have not done enough against the militias of the former rwandan government, which are a pole of instability and a pretext for permanent instability in the eastern democratic republic of the congo, and we must act more energetically to disarm them. we must make it clear that any invasion is unacceptable and that respect for the borders of the countries is a principle which must be respected by all the states in the region. we must complete the democratic transition in the democratic republic of congo and consolidate the stabilisation of the country, including the need to reunify the congolese army. we must strengthen the means of the united nations mission to ensure peace and stability in the east of the drc and to create conditions on the ground that will not make us turn back, that is, that will lead everyone to honour the 2003 peace agreements, that will lead everyone to honour the commitments made in tanzania on 20 november and that will lead everyone to implement the un security council resolutions on time.
